chapters.title: Chapter 2301: The reports are... worse than we estimated.
paragraphs: "Our Universe’s first Incubus, he isn’t just a Progenitor of a single World, he is the Progenitor of ALL the Incubi that will ever exist in our Universe.
Don’t compare his bloodline to the normal power scale, you know.
He is beyond that scale."
Nux’s smile then turned even more loving and—
"After all, he is the Universe’s Child."
The women’s expressions changed.
"Progenitor of all Incubi..."
Aisha muttered in her head. She looked at the child, then she looked at Nux and—
"So how strong would he be?"

She asked out of curiosity. It was a question that interested every single woman present here, after all, the more they knew about Allura’s child, the more information they would have about their own.
Of course, the women weren’t particularly interested in their children’s strength, if it were up to them, they couldn’t care less about how strong their children would be, but...
They had seen how the Universe worked, it was a cruel, merciless place. One needed strength, not just to achieve greatness, but just to survive without being bullied by others.
So yes, their children’s potential mattered.
Nux knew that as well, but Aisha’s question was more complicated than that.
"As I said, the normal power scale, or the power scale that came from the Main Universe, cannot be used for him, he is born in an entirely different Universe.
There is no accurate ’level’ I can tell you, there are several factors.
How much he trains, what Law he comprehends, all these factors would play a big role, and the biggest factor out of all would be..."
Nux paused for a moment, finally moving his eyes away from his child and looking at Aisha, then his other wives.
"It’s my strength, or the strength of our Universe."
"The strength of our Universe?"
Vyriana narrowed her eyes.
"He is the Universe’s first Incubus, his strength would grow together with the Universe."
"Does that mean... even his potential is constantly growing...?"
Lyriana questioned and Nux nodded.
"That is correct."
"He is your child alright."
Astaria shook her head and the rest of the women nodded with smiles. This level of confusion when they were only discussing the child’s potential...

But honestly, this time, this made some sense, even in the women’s minds. They couldn’t understand it well because even though they were now connected to Nux’s Universe, they still came from the Main Universe.
Their minds were used to it and its power scale.

But to compare a being of one Universe with another Universe’s power scale... it was foolish on their part. A more accurate way to think about the child’s potential would be to create another power system, a system for Nux’s Universe.
And in this system, if Nux’s potential stood at the very top, his children’s potential would be a step lower, and other beings born in the Universe later would then fit into lower levels.
Yes, it was crude, most of it didn’t even exist, but that was just how things were.
Nux’s Universe had just formed, the first true being of the Universe had just taken birth, it was impossible to create proper power scales when there were no beings to fit into those power scales.
"You people are thinking too much."
Suddenly, Allura spoke up with a light smile on her face. Then she held her child more firmly and—
"He is our child."
She spoke, looking into Nux’s eyes.
"He will be just fine, I assure you.
And even if he doesn’t, we will always be there to protect him, won’t we?"
She asked, Nux nodded, so did the rest of the women. Allura smiled at that reaction, then, with a relieved look on her face, she closed her eyes and...
She drifted into dreamland.
And as if sensing his mother’s calm, the child too closed his eyes just like his mother did and... he went to sleep as well.
The people around her saw that sight of the mother and son sleeping together and for a moment, no one said anything.

The women just looked at each other with light smiles on their faces, while Nux stared at Allura and his son with the same gentle, protective smile on his face for a long, long time. The sight of his wife, who was now a mother, and his newborn child together had put him in a trance-like state, a state he wouldn’t be recovering from for a good while.
Skyla, looking at the mother, father, and the son, frowned and then tilted her head in confusion—
"So... are we not going to name him...?"
"I don’t think we can."
Rune shook her head.
"Allura must already have a name in her mind."
Riona answered, then she looked at Amaya and smiled with a gentle look on her face.
"I know I did."
Amaya didn’t know how to react, she just held her mother’s hand tightly, Riona did the same and the mother and daughter just stared at each other without saying anything.
"Mhm, I am sure she must have a name."
Eisheth nodded as well, looking at her own daughter. Aisha smiled brightly and directly hugged her mother, she was much more forward than Amaya.

Seeing such a sight, Evane and Astaria too looked at each other. Unlike Amaya and Riona or Aisha and Eisheth, they... weren’t exactly close, at least not before Nux. They were technically grandmother and granddaughter but... the number of times they had interacted with each other was limited.

So ever since they got close because of Nux, there was some level of... awkwardness between them, but of course, as awkward as they were, the fact that they had some form of connection with each other couldn’t be hidden and that connection had only become stronger.
So Evane too slowly walked towards Astaria and just stood next to her. An action that put a light smile on Astaria’s face.
Just like that, time passed, the people stayed in the room, watching Allura and her son sleep together, at the same time imagining what it would be like when they would have their own children.
Yes, every single one of them was excited about their ’turn’. After all, for most of them, this child would be their first and even for those who wouldn’t be giving birth for the first time—
Just the idea of giving birth to a child with a man who loved them with his all, it was... very fulfilling.
"Alright, then I’ll just name my own child."

Skyla pouted as she looked down and rubbed her own belly. Lane, who was standing with her, laughed at that reaction. She stared at Skyla’s belly, then her own. Then she looked around and stared at the other women and their bellies.
It was... a strange sight.
To think they would all be giving birth to new members of the family soon...
Just imagining numerous children running all over the place with big smiles on their faces... it felt... impossible.
Especially considering everything they had been through.
Lane smiled inwardly as she looked at her belly again.
And while Nux’s Universe was... celebrating the new member and was eagerly waiting for the new future members of the family, the Main Universe—
It was in chaos, it was in... shambles.
And the one who had it the worst was... the Supreme World of Darkness.

At the very heart of the Supreme World of Darkness, a vast hollow was carved into a mountain of... black glass, so deep that even sound felt afraid to fall into it. Rivers of slow, glowing crimson ran through the cracks in the floor like veins. Above, the ceiling was a moving sky of ash and shadow, swirling in a constant storm that never released rain.

At the center of that hollow was... a Throne Pit—a circular stage of obsidian bones, surrounded by pillars that looked like the ribs of a dead titan. Chains as thick as towers hung from those pillars, chains that were connected to the throne. Almost as if they were trying to hold something... that shouldn’t be released.
On this throne sat a being.
A being that the Universe called Son of Darkness or Son Darkness.

Son Darkness was the voice of Ul’Thakar, Darkness itself, one who carried Darkness’s authority when the Infinity himself did not move. A being that played a similar role as Lord Light did back in the Supreme World of Light.

His skin was pitch-black, like polished nightstone, catching faint reflections from the red rivers below. His eyes were a deep crimson with no warmth inside. A crown of shadow-metal hovered above his head.
And in front of him—
He didn’t fidget.
He didn’t sigh.
He simply watched the figure kneeling before him.
A being that... wasn’t made of flesh like the way mortals were, his body seemed like it was built from... smoke.
Thick, layered, and heavy smoke.
Every edge of him frayed into drifting strands, as if the world couldn’t decide where he ended. When he bowed, those strands poured forward like a cloak and pooled on the floor in silent waves.

Two long, jagged, and uneven horns curved from his skull. Between those horns was his... head. A mess of black, thorn-like, half-solid and half-mist spikes. Just like Son Darkness, his eyes were crimson.
One look at him would make most beings in the Universe tremble in fear, but right now, this being was kneeling.
He was... afraid.
Afraid to say what he was about to say—
"My Lord..."
But nonetheless, he began, because that was what he had to do.
"The reports are... worse than we estimated."

chapters.title: Chapter 2302: Phase Two of this war.
paragraphs: "My Lord..."
The Darkness Born spoke in a low, grim tone.
"The reports are... worse than we estimated."
And... Son Darkness did not respond. He only stared at the being giving the report, the Darkness Born trembled.

Just like Lord Light, Son Darkness too had power over all Darkness Borns, no matter how strong they were. If he wanted, he could erase them from existence and he wouldn’t even have to answer to Ul’Thakar.
Why would he?
HewasUl’Thakar in some sense, he was created out of his will, he had some part of his consciousness inside him. In Ul’Thakar’s absence, Son DarknesswasDarkness.
And the Darkness Born knew that—
That was the reason he was shivering in fear in the first place. Then finally, Son Darkness tapped on the throne’s armrest with his finger.
It was a silent command to continue.
The Darkness Born gulped, then he slowly raised his head and continued—
"In the last cycle... about one hundred thousand Darkness Worlds have perished."
"One hundred thousand...?"
Son Darkness tilted his head, the crimson in his eyes became brighter. Those words surprised even him.

The Darkness Born trembled even more strongly, the Eternal-level Darkness Borns had all left for war, only the ’weak’ Darkness Borns were left to report to Son Darkness. Because they were weak, their worth was already low in Son Darkness’s eyes, which put them at a higher risk of being erased.

Since the war started, Son Darkness has erased six Darkness Borns simply because he did not like what he heard and while normally, the Darkness Born would have enjoyed a sight like this, when it was happening to him—
It wasn’t that amusing.
But again—
Tap
Son Darkness tapped on the armrest again, the Darkness Born understood the signal and continued with the report.
"Light has broken the Supreme Rules,"
He spoke in a bitter tone.
"And from how swift their movements were, they didn’t do it out of desperation, they had planned it all. They broke the Supreme Rules willingly."
The Darkness Born then lifted his hand and a shard of shadow-crystal formed above his palm. A crystal that then started showing images in the air.

"Primordials attacked the Lowest-Level Worlds, Transcendents attacked Low-Level Worlds, and Eternals attacked Middle-Level Worlds. There were no armies, no mass attacks, just a few beings targeting a single world they knew they could destroy.
Everything happened so quickly that our worlds couldn’t even call for reinforcements. All of their armies perished before the battle even began.
They didn’t even leave the Worlds’ Will alone, all of the Worlds were devoured, making sure the damage is permanent."
The images shown in the air then dimmed down, the Darkness Born raised his head as if wanting to say something important and—

"They did the same with our High-Level Worlds as well. Since they couldn’t target all our worlds, they only targeted our most important ones. A world that was being defended by five Eternals met fifteen enemy Eternals, Eternals that were armed with stronger relics and artifacts.
Because of that, most of our pillar worlds are... gone."
For the first time, Son Darkness’s crimson eyes narrowed slightly. The Darkness Born took that as permission to speak more bluntly.
"The worlds that held our supply lines, our archives, the channels that carried orders and resources across the faction, with all those worlds now destroyed, we are... blind in most regions.
Communication routes have collapsed. Dark Relays that took thousands of years to build are shattered. Some worlds still cannot be contacted at all because the paths to them are broken.
For a moment, the Darkness Born hesitated, but then forced the next words out.
"We cannot distribute weapons properly, we cannot move reinforcements efficiently, we cannot even confirm some of the worlds’ status, whether they still exist or have perished.
We are... in quite a bad position."
The moment those words were said, the entire Throne Pit turned... even colder. The crimson rivers on the floor pulsed, the place seemed to become even darker.
This wasn’t good.
Son Darkness’s expression alone was more than enough to understand that.
It had only been a week since the war had begun, and if this was the extent of damage in just a week then...
The first part of the war—
It was won by Light.
And no being of Darkness liked hearing that.
"And us?"
Suddenly, Son Darkness questioned.
"What about us?"
He asked, wanting to hear some level of good news. Light had gone all out, their plan was a clean, complete strike, a plan like this often leaves... weaknesses. Weaknesses that can be used later.
Son Darkness himself had given orders to attack Light’s defenseless worlds, and now he wanted to know how that played out.

"Our surviving worlds that weren’t attacked by Light did well, the Lowest-, Low-, or Middle-Level Worlds couldn’t do anything impressive because by the time they attacked, they had an army waiting for them, an army that had the home advantage.
But our High-Level Worlds were different.
Most of Light’s High-Level Worlds had no Eternals defending them, they were abandoned, their entire army had left, only the weak remained, weak that the Light most likely left to die.
And just like you ordered, our men went on and continued to devour Light Worlds, and we made sure to target only the High-Level Worlds.
Till now, we have devoured about four thousand High-Level Worlds, but now the pace has slowed down."
The Darkness Born explained and Son Darkness tilted his head,
"And why is that?"
He asked.
"Light has completely abandoned defense, maybe because they have lost so many worlds to Anomaly already, losing more worlds does not make a difference to them.
They are focusing on offense and their Eternals, abandoning their own worlds, have begun targeting our Eternals.
Even our Darkness Borns fighting in the war are facing trouble because almost all of Light Faction’s Eternals are now participating in the battle.
If we do not reinforce them soon, then we will lose even on the front where we have an advantage because of Anomaly’s actions."
"So instead of attacking Light Worlds, our Eternals have gone to reinforce our frontline?"
Son Darkness asked and the Darkness Born nodded.
"That is correct, my Lord."
"So you are telling me...
The enemy attacked us, within a week they destroyed a hundred thousand of our worlds, and in return...
We have only destroyed four thousand and our attacking line has now gone to the frontline to fight a battle that will take centuries or even thousands of years to conclude...?"
Son Darkness asked and once again, silence fell over the place. The Darkness Born did not dare to answer, not when the question was asked in such a tone.
His silence, however, was enough of an answer.
And Son Darkness... as tough as his reaction was, in his mind, he too understood what was necessary.
Yes, war brought death and destruction that strengthened Darkness, yes, in theory, a war should strengthen Darkness.
That alone should give Darkness quite a strong advantage.
But...
This time, Light had a better plan, or more accurately, they had a stronger veil. While their attack wasn’t exactly a surprise, the quickness and decisiveness of it was indeed surprising.
This gave them quite a strong advantage, an advantage that they used well.
This war, from the start to the point they were at right now, had all gone according to Light’s plan.

In critical time, they took down their weaker worlds, they took down their important worlds, they destroyed the communication lines, they destroyed the worlds that were supposed to supply, they... fractured the Darkness Faction itself.

And even now, even when their attacking units that should have had free rein to go and destroy as many of Light’s High-Level Worlds as they wanted were forced to join the frontline as reinforcements, it went according to Light’s plan as well—
Because if they had not—

All their Eternals, including the Darkness Borns, would have perished and that would have weakened Ul’Thakar to an extent where Seraphielle wouldn’t just have an advantage, she would have an advantage strong enough to actually kill Ul’Thakar.
Yes, death, destruction and such were supposed to strengthen Ul’Thakar, but not when all the death and destruction came from just the Darkness Faction, that would weaken even Ul’Thakar.
It was all forced, the Darkness Faction had completely fallen for Light’s trap, it was something that hadn’t happened since the beginning of time and that is what made it so frustrating.
But...
This time, Son Darkness did not lose himself.
As much as he would like to erase the Darkness Born kneeling in front of him, he understood that there was no point to it.
He needed to calm himself.
He needed to... prepare himself.
For Phase Two of this war.
The phase where everything will now stabilize and Darkness—
It would finally take over and devour Light.

Most of Light’s High-Level Worlds had no Eternals defending them, they were abandoned, their entire army had left, only the weak remained, weak that the Light most likely left to die.
And just like you ordered, our men went on and continued to devour Light Worlds, and we made sure to target only the High-Level Worlds.
Till now, we have devoured about four thousand High-Level Worlds, but now the pace has slowed down."
The Darkness Born explained and Son Darkness tilted his head,
"And why is that?"
He asked.
"Light has completely abandoned defense, maybe because they have lost so many worlds to Anomaly already, losing more worlds does not make a difference to them.
They are focusing on offense and their Eternals, abandoning their own worlds, have begun targeting our Eternals.
Even our Darkness Borns fighting in the war are facing trouble because almost all of Light Faction’s Eternals are now participating in the battle.
If we do not reinforce them soon, then we will lose even on the front where we have an advantage because of Anomaly’s actions."
"So instead of attacking Light Worlds, our Eternals have gone to reinforce our frontline?"
Son Darkness asked and the Darkness Born nodded.
"That is correct, my Lord."
"So you are telling me...
The enemy attacked us, within a week they destroyed a hundred thousand of our worlds, and in return...
We have only destroyed four thousand and our attacking line has now gone to the frontline to fight a battle that will take centuries or even thousands of years to conclude...?"
Son Darkness asked and once again, silence fell over the place.
The Darkness Born did not dare to answer, not when the question was asked in such a tone.
His silence, however, was enough of an answer.
And Son Darkness... as tough as his reaction was, in his mind, he too understood what was necessary.
Yes, war brought death and destruction that strengthened Darkness, yes, in theory, a war should strengthen Darkness.
That alone should give Darkness quite a strong advantage.
But...
This time, Light had a better plan, or more accurately, they had a stronger veil.
While their attack wasn’t exactly a surprise, the quickness and decisiveness of it was indeed surprising.
This gave them quite a strong advantage, an advantage that they used well.
This war, from the start to the point they were at right now, had all gone according to Light’s plan.

In critical time, they took down their weaker worlds, they took down their important worlds, they destroyed the communication lines, they destroyed the worlds that were supposed to supply, they... fractured the Darkness Faction itself.

And even now, even when their attacking units that should have had free rein to go and destroy as many of Light’s High-Level Worlds as they wanted were forced to join the frontline as reinforcements, it went according to Light’s plan as well—
Because if they had not—

All their Eternals, including the Darkness Borns, would have perished and that would have weakened Ul’Thakar to an extent where Seraphielle wouldn’t just have an advantage, she would have an advantage strong enough to actually kill Ul’Thakar.
Yes, death, destruction and such were supposed to strengthen Ul’Thakar, but not when all the death and destruction came from just the Darkness Faction, that would weaken even Ul’Thakar.
It was all forced, the Darkness Faction had completely fallen for Light’s trap, it was something that hadn’t happened since the beginning of time and that is what made it so frustrating.
But...
This time, Son Darkness did not lose himself.
As much as he would like to erase the Darkness Born kneeling in front of him, he understood that there was no point to it.
He needed to calm himself.
He needed to... prepare himself.
For Phase Two of this war.
The phase where everything will now stabilize and Darkness—
It would finally take over and devour Light.

chapters.title: Chapter 2303: Nux’s Universe.
paragraphs: The war between the Supreme World of Light and the Supreme World of Darkness continued and with time, it only got worse.

The initial phase of the war was over, Light’s surprise attack had taken many of the Darkness Faction’s Worlds, but now that the war had stabilized, when the two sides were finally at a similar level and there were no more surprise attacks—
The war had only become more... destructive.
Because now—
The damage wasn’t concentrated at a single point, it was spreading out. Territory after territory was being destroyed, not just of Darkness or Light’s, anything close to their battle was destroyed.
The Universe was crying, the death, destruction, and suffering were at their highest, the weak were being preyed upon, rules were being bent like they never existed.
The entire Universe had become a place of outlaws, the innocents had no place here.
It was...
Hell.
A place where Chaos had been unleashed.
And in this chaos—
Ten long years passed.
Ten years in Nux’s Universe, how many years it was in the Main Universe, it didn’t matter, not to Nux, because his focus was on his own Universe.
And in these ten years—
His Universe had changed, a lot.
So much that as Nux sat inside his room, with Shadow lying with her head resting on his lap, he... couldn’t help but reminisce.

It all started with a small little black ball that he one day sensed inside him, a black ball that devoured everything it was offered, a ball with devouring power so strong that he called it a Black Hole.
A hollow space inside his own body, born from God knows what.
Then, he began using it.
He began to... devour, actively.
Laws, living beings... or even... active Worlds, and everything he devoured became part of this space inside him before it turned into something... new.
Over time, the more he devoured, the more ’complete’ this space became, until finally, it became an independent Universe that could exist on its own.
The devoured worlds were no longer stars with no signs of life, they became habitable worlds that could support life, Nux’s Universe began to feel like... an actual Universe.
A Universe with many, many worlds inside it.
The number had already reached four digits. Yes, that was how many worlds Nux had devoured till now, and now, almost all of these worlds had life, different kinds of life.
Some were calm.
Some were violent.
Some were filled with endless wars.
And unlike the Main Universe, where most beings were fighting because two of the strongest beings in existence were battling against each other—
In here—
The rules were different.
Nux’s Universe valued absolute freedom.
People here were allowed to do whatever they wanted. Good, bad, right, wrong, none of it existed here.
If you were ambitious and wished to reach the top of the Universe, to rule those around you, you were allowed to.
As for the methods you used, it didn’t matter.
In this Universe, people didn’t fight for others, they fought because they wished to, for their own personal ambition.
As for those who did not wish to fight and climb to power through different, more... diplomatic means instead—
That was possible too.
In different worlds, worlds where politics existed but fighting itself was prohibited.
Yes, it was that simple.
While the Main Universe outside burned and the people there suffered regardless of what they wanted—
People in Nux’s Universe did whatever they wanted.
They fought.
They loved.
They built.
They destroyed.
Freedom.
This was... true freedom.
And yet...
Even in a place like this, even in a place where people were allowed to do whatever they wanted—
One rule existed.
A single rule.
No being was allowed to reproduce.
Nux’s Universe was complete, yes, but it was still... a relatively young Universe, in a Universe’s average cycle, it wouldn’t be wrong to call Nux’s Universe a newborn Universe.

So while it could support life, life here could not grow. To reach that level, a level where the Universe could produce its own worlds, and sustain and grow life naturally, it would take many, many years. According to Nux’s estimate, that number was about a few hundred million.
In a situation like this, where the Universe itself could not sustain growth, giving birth to a child would mean... giving birth to a being who, no matter how much time passed, would never grow.
Yes, even a ten-year-old child would remain a newborn and would perish once his lifespan was over.
At least, that is what happened naturally.
But there were exceptions to this as well, beings who could grow, even when the Universe could not support their growth.
The beings for whom the Universe itself was going out of its way to support only their growth.
Beings who were otherwise called...
The Children of the Universe.
Every bit of the Universe’s energy, every fragment of its power, every trace of ’growth’, it was all being directed to two places—
One, a safe reservoir for emergency situations.
And the other—
To these children, children who, even inside this new Universe that could not properly support life, were growing tremendously.
Of course, this fact itself raised countless questions, countless voices of dissatisfaction.
Why can’t we reproduce and extend our bloodline?
Why can’t our children grow when they are growing just fine?
But these questions weren’t answered, no one had to answer them.
After all, the Universe itself represented freedom, in here, one could do whatever they wanted.
You wanted to give birth?
Go ahead.
But choices came with consequences.
And giving birth came with the consequence of living with a newborn child who would never grow, no matter how much the parents tried.
A child that wouldn’t be able to cultivate, a child that would perish the moment his mortal lifespan was over.
If parents were fine with that sort of life for their children, no one stopped them.
Just that—
After seeing others live through this pain, no being tried.
As for those who already had children before they were devoured into this Universe?
Well they...
They were unlucky.

Because just like other children, those children too wouldn’t grow. In these ten years, these children who should have grown, children who should have changed, who should have gotten stronger, children who should have matured—
They didn’t.
They remained the same.
Unchanged.
Frozen.
Not by time... but by lack of resources.
Because the resources were being directed to the new generation, to the only generation the Universe cared about.

And while people did complain in their hearts, they also understood the important truth. The Anomaly wasn’t a graceful god who was here to serve them, he wasn’t here to bless them with a happy, fulfilling life.
He was a selfish, greedy, hypocritical being and this entire Universe existed just for him.
And for those who would inherit it.
But even then—
Life inside the Universe wasn’t cruel.
And the more Worlds the Anomaly devoured, the more people that came here proved it. Life here was nowhere close to what it was outside.

People weren’t being hunted here, they weren’t being forced into battles they didn’t want to participate in, they weren’t being abandoned, left to die by their world leaders, they weren’t being enslaved.
Not being able to reproduce?
Not being able to grow?
Those who came from literal war zones where they could die any second now had no complaints about that rule.
All they wanted to do was to eat, rest, and... to smile.
And in Nux’s Universe—
That was very much possible.
It was strange.
A place where one of the most basic rights—reproduction—was taken away, people were still happier than they had ever been.
Because here...
They were free.
Free to reign, free to spill blood, free to climb to the top—
And amongst all this chaos, amongst all these worlds that were filled with endless ambition—
There was another place.
A single world that was different from all the rest.
A world where none of it existed.
Umbrasol.
A world that was once called the World of Death, a place where Darkness ruled, a world that was... special to Nux since its existence changed his journey forever—
Now...
That world had become something else entirely.
It had become bright, peaceful, and alive.
Different from all the worlds in Nux’s Universe—
There were no ranks there.
No nobles.
No hierarchy.
No ambition.
There was only one King, his Queens, and his Princes and Princesses, other than these, every single person in this world, be it a street vendor or a rich merchant, had the same rank.
The new Umbrasol was... peaceful.
Crimes here were strictly not allowed, not even the smallest of theft.
Nothing.
People who lived here did not desire power.
They did not chase strength in any form. Be it physical power, cultivation power, or even political power—
That desire simply did not exist.

These were the people who were... exhausted after living a life like it was a race, now they wished to live silently and peacefully until it was their time to leave. These weren’t the people who dreamt of ruling others.
They only wanted one thing.
A simple life.
Those with ambition, those with a desire for power, those who wished to rise above others, they simply weren’t allowed in.
And so...
Umbrasol became a haven.
For the weak.
For the tired.
For those who simply wanted to live.
Farms stretched across the land.
Children laughed in the streets.
People worked, not to survive—but to live.
And at the center of it all...
They existed.
The King.
The Queens.
And... the children.
The only beings in this Universe who were... allowed to grow.

chapters.title: Chapter 2304: Poop!
paragraphs: Morning in Umbrasol was different from before, the sky here was no longer grey and dull like it once was when Nux first visited Umbrasol.

Umbrasol was now different. The sky here was oddly fresh. Golden light spread slowly across the land, touching the rooftops, the trees, the small houses lined neatly along stone roads. A cool breeze moved through the streets, carrying the smell of fresh bread and flowers.

People here woke up without worry, no one rushed to work, no one feared another. Every being that became part of Umbrasol was thoroughly screened, their deepest, darkest desires were examined, and only once they passed, only once it was ensured that these people had no intention of stirring trouble—
Were these people let in.
Other people knew that, this was also the reason why none of them feared anything. In this Umbrasol, even the concept of locks did not exist simply because no being here would steal.
The children here played and laughed in the open without their parents being worried about someone harming them.
This was Umbrasol, a calm, peaceful world like no other.
And in this calm, peaceful world—
A small bell rang.
A shop opened.
It was a simple sweets shop.

Glass jars here were filled with colorful candies, fresh pastries sat neatly arranged on wooden trays. The owner, an old man, a being with a single black horn above his head, green skin, and kind eyes, hummed as he wiped the counter without a worry in the world.
Then—
The door of his candy shop opened and a little girl, no more than ten years old, walked in.

The girl had soft pink-silver hair that fell just above her shoulders, her hairstyle slightly messy as if she had just woken up and didn’t bother fixing it. A few loose strands framed her face, moving gently with the breeze, giving her an effortlessly cute and carefree look.

Her big pink eyes sparkled with innocent mischief, shining brightly as if she was always thinking of something playful. Her cheeks were naturally rosy, and when she smiled, it made her look even more adorable.

She wore a soft and fluffy light pastel pink dress, with small frills lining the sleeves and the hem. The dress had delicate ribbons tied neatly at the front and around her waist, forming a tiny bow that bounced slightly every time she moved. The fabric looked light and comfortable, perfect for running around without a care, her skirt spread out slightly, giving her a doll-like appearance.
*Picture*
She walked straight to the counter, stood on her toes, and looked at the sweets, an action that automatically put a smile on the old man’s face.
The girl’s gaze then locked onto one small, glowing sugar candy and—
"I want that one,"
She spoke in a sweet, excessively adorable voice as she placed her hand on the counter, as if she was putting something on top of it, but didn’t actually put anything.

The shopkeeper blinked for a moment, as if he couldn’t believe how soft and sweet her voice was. He placed his hand at the same place the girl had, picked up whatever she had put on the table like he was playing along with her game and—
"Of course.
Take it."
He spoke with a smile.
The little girl smiled back, reached out, grabbed the candy, and turned around, happily unwrapping it.
As she walked out, the shopkeeper waved at her.
"Come again!"
And the girl—
"Yes~"
She answered cutely as she skipped out adorably.
Outside—
She took a bite and the instant she did—
"Mhmmmm~~"
Her eyes lit up.
"So sweet~"
She praised while at the same time praising herself in her mind, but just as she was enjoying herself—
"Selene."
She heard a voice and the little girl froze.
Then, with the candy still in her mouth, she turned around slowly and her eyes fell on a boy standing a few steps away.
He looked around her age.

He had neat, smooth dark crimson hair that was carefully kept in place, not a single strand out of order, as if even the wind knew better than to disturb it. The deep red shade of his hair contrasted beautifully with his pale, flawless skin, giving him a quiet yet striking presence.
His calm red eyes were clear, steady, and completely unreadable, showing next to no emotion, as if nothing in the world could truly shake him.
He wore a simple, well-fitted dark outfit. The fabric rested smoothly against him, giving off a quiet sense of refinement.
*Picture*
The boy looked at the candy in her hand, then he looked at her.
"You stole it."
He spoke and the instant he said those words, the girl placed her hands on her mouth and widened her eyes in disbelief like she couldn’t believe she was being accused like that.
"I did not!"
She countered instantly but—
"You already spent your pocket money, I have been counting."
The boy answered with a calm look on his face and Selene, she scrunched her nose.
"That is creepy. Do something else with all this time you have."
"You stole it."
The boy, unbothered by those words, repeated his own.
"Oh come on!"
Selene raised her voice.
"I did not *steal* it from him, I was just practicing! Practicing! Even if you go in there and tell him I stole from him, he would let me go, I can assure yo—"
"That’s because you used your ability to charm him."
The boy interrupted.
"You first used illusions to fool him into thinking you gave him money, then you charmed him so that even if you get caught, he doesn’t make a scene. That is stealing and using your powers unjustly."
The boy spoke.
"He is a Divine! There is no way my powers would work on him! I am not that strong yet!"
Selene countered and the boy... he only stared at her without saying anything else and Selene...
Her shoulders dropped and she caved in—
"Alright, alright, my powers work on Divines now! Happy!?"
"I will be if you go and pay him."
The boy answered.
"You already know I cannot! I already spent my money on candies! I don’t even eat that much, only five a day. See? Even my teeth are all white!"
Selene cried, her big pink eyes instantly turning moist.
She was a drama queen, that’s for sure.
The boy looked at her and sighed, then—
*Flick*
He flicked a coin at her and—
"Go pay him."
The instant he said those words, Selene’s moist pink eyes cleared up and shined with joy.
"Noctis! You are the best of the best! You are even better than Veyron!"
She jumped in joy but before she could go into the shop to pay, a red strand made of blood grabbed her arm and—
"Pay me back later."
Noctis spoke as he looked at her, his red eyes glowing slightly.
Selene looked at him, their eyes met and Selene grinned—
"Pay back what? I don’t know what you are talking about. Hehe~"
Noctis narrowed his eyes.
"You wish to do this?"
"What? You wanna fight?"
Selene didn’t back down, her pink eyes now glowed even more strongly as she stared at the strand of blood around her wrist.
"You cannot defeat me."
Noctis spoke with a confident calm.
"I cannot, but you think Father will let you beat me after I surrender?"
Selene’s grin widened. Her plan was simple, enter the battle, surrender instantly, and hide behind her Father, that way, she wouldn’t have to pay her brother back.
"Father will take my side, you might even have to pay double once you are caught."
Noctis was still calm.
"How will I get caught? No one saw what happened here!"
Selene grinned, she was very confident but...
"Are you sure about that...?"
Noctis asked a simple question and Selene...
She paused.
Then, she closed her eyes and expanded her senses, and there she saw her—
About a few kilometres away, on a rooftop—

A small figure sat quietly, her knees pulled close to her chest as she balanced effortlessly on the edge. Her soft black hair fell gently around her face, slightly uneven, with a few loose strands brushing against her cheeks. Two fluffy ears rested atop her head, twitching lightly with every shift in the wind, reacting to even the smallest sounds around her.

A thin, sleek tail moved slowly behind her, swaying in a calm, controlled rhythm. Her golden eyes were sharp and focused, glowing faintly under the sunlight, yet holding a depth far beyond her small, delicate appearance.
Her face was soft and innocent, almost doll-like, but her gaze was anything but childish.
She was Kira Leander.
*Picture*
Their elder sister.
And the moment Selene sensed her—
"Poop!"
She cursed.
Then, she glanced at Noctis, whose expressionless face was now replaced with a small, victorious grin and—
"You knew she was watching!"
Selene pointed her little finger at him in anger.
An action against which Noctis just smiled and—
"What? Wanna fight?"
He repeated the same words she said before and Selene only got even angrier.
"Poop!"
She cursed again.

Golden light spread slowly across the land, touching the rooftops, the trees, the small houses lined neatly along stone roads.
A cool breeze moved through the streets, carrying the smell of fresh bread and flowers.
People here woke up without worry, no one rushed to work, no one feared another.

Every being that became part of Umbrasol was thoroughly screened, their deepest, darkest desires were examined, and only once they passed, only once it was ensured that these people had no intention of stirring trouble—
Were these people let in.
Other people knew that, this was also the reason why none of them feared anything.
In this Umbrasol, even the concept of locks did not exist simply because no being here would steal.
The children here played and laughed in the open without their parents being worried about someone harming them.
This was Umbrasol, a calm, peaceful world like no other.
And in this calm, peaceful world—
A small bell rang.
A shop opened.
It was a simple sweets shop.
Glass jars here were filled with colorful candies, fresh pastries sat neatly arranged on wooden trays.
The owner, an old man, a being with a single black horn above his head, green skin, and kind eyes, hummed as he wiped the counter without a worry in the world.
Then—
The door of his candy shop opened and a little girl, no more than ten years old, walked in.
The girl had soft pink-silver hair that fell just above her shoulders, her hairstyle slightly messy as if she had just woken up and didn’t bother fixing it.
A few loose strands framed her face, moving gently with the breeze, giving her an effortlessly cute and carefree look.
Her big pink eyes sparkled with innocent mischief, shining brightly as if she was always thinking of something playful.
Her cheeks were naturally rosy, and when she smiled, it made her look even more adorable.
She wore a soft and fluffy light pastel pink dress, with small frills lining the sleeves and the hem.
The dress had delicate ribbons tied neatly at the front and around her waist, forming a tiny bow that bounced slightly every time she moved.
The fabric looked light and comfortable, perfect for running around without a care, her skirt spread out slightly, giving her a doll-like appearance.
*Picture*
She walked straight to the counter, stood on her toes, and looked at the sweets, an action that automatically put a smile on the old man’s face.
The girl’s gaze then locked onto one small, glowing sugar candy and—
"I want that one,"
She spoke in a sweet, excessively adorable voice as she placed her hand on the counter, as if she was putting something on top of it, but didn’t actually put anything.
The shopkeeper blinked for a moment, as if he couldn’t believe how soft and sweet her voice was.
He placed his hand at the same place the girl had, picked up whatever she had put on the table like he was playing along with her game and—
"Of course.
Take it."
He spoke with a smile.
The little girl smiled back, reached out, grabbed the candy, and turned around, happily unwrapping it.
As she walked out, the shopkeeper waved at her.
"Come again!"
And the girl—
"Yes~"
She answered cutely as she skipped out adorably.
Outside—
She took a bite and the instant she did—
"Mhmmmm~~"
Her eyes lit up.
"So sweet~"
She praised while at the same time praising herself in her mind, but just as she was enjoying herself—
"Selene."
She heard a voice and the little girl froze.
Then, with the candy still in her mouth, she turned around slowly and her eyes fell on a boy standing a few steps away.
He looked around her age.
He had neat, smooth dark crimson hair that was carefully kept in place, not a single strand out of order, as if even the wind knew better than to disturb it.
The deep red shade of his hair contrasted beautifully with his pale, flawless skin, giving him a quiet yet striking presence.
His calm red eyes were clear, steady, and completely unreadable, showing next to no emotion, as if nothing in the world could truly shake him.
He wore a simple, well-fitted dark outfit.
The fabric rested smoothly against him, giving off a quiet sense of refinement.
*Picture*
The boy looked at the candy in her hand, then he looked at her.
"You stole it."
He spoke and the instant he said those words, the girl placed her hands on her mouth and widened her eyes in disbelief like she couldn’t believe she was being accused like that.
"I did not!"
She countered instantly but—
"You already spent your pocket money, I have been counting."
The boy answered with a calm look on his face and Selene, she scrunched her nose.
"That is creepy.
Do something else with all this time you have."
"You stole it."
The boy, unbothered by those words, repeated his own.
"Oh come on!"
Selene raised her voice.
"I did not *steal* it from him, I was just practicing!
Practicing!
Even if you go in there and tell him I stole from him, he would let me go, I can assure yo—"
"That’s because you used your ability to charm him."
The boy interrupted.
"You first used illusions to fool him into thinking you gave him money, then you charmed him so that even if you get caught, he doesn’t make a scene.
That is stealing and using your powers unjustly."
The boy spoke.
"He is a Divine!
There is no way my powers would work on him!
I am not that strong yet!"
Selene countered and the boy... he only stared at her without saying anything else and Selene...
Her shoulders dropped and she caved in—
"Alright, alright, my powers work on Divines now!
Happy!?"
"I will be if you go and pay him."
The boy answered.
"You already know I cannot!
I already spent my money on candies!
I don’t even eat that much, only five a day.
See?
Even my teeth are all white!"
Selene cried, her big pink eyes instantly turning moist.
She was a drama queen, that’s for sure.
The boy looked at her and sighed, then—
*Flick*
He flicked a coin at her and—
"Go pay him."
The instant he said those words, Selene’s moist pink eyes cleared up and shined with joy.
"Noctis!
You are the best of the best!
You are even better than Veyron!"
She jumped in joy but before she could go into the shop to pay, a red strand made of blood grabbed her arm and—
"Pay me back later."
Noctis spoke as he looked at her, his red eyes glowing slightly.
Selene looked at him, their eyes met and Selene grinned—
"Pay back what?
I don’t know what you are talking about.
Hehe~"
Noctis narrowed his eyes.
"You wish to do this?"
"What?
You wanna fight?"
Selene didn’t back down, her pink eyes now glowed even more strongly as she stared at the strand of blood around her wrist.
"You cannot defeat me."
Noctis spoke with a confident calm.
"I cannot, but you think Father will let you beat me after I surrender?"
Selene’s grin widened.
Her plan was simple, enter the battle, surrender instantly, and hide behind her Father, that way, she wouldn’t have to pay her brother back.
"Father will take my side, you might even have to pay double once you are caught."
Noctis was still calm.
"How will I get caught?
No one saw what happened here!"
Selene grinned, she was very confident but...
"Are you sure about that...?"
Noctis asked a simple question and Selene...
She paused.
Then, she closed her eyes and expanded her senses, and there she saw her—
About a few kilometres away, on a rooftop—
A small figure sat quietly, her knees pulled close to her chest as she balanced effortlessly on the edge.
Her soft black hair fell gently around her face, slightly uneven, with a few loose strands brushing against her cheeks.
Two fluffy ears rested atop her head, twitching lightly with every shift in the wind, reacting to even the smallest sounds around her.
A thin, sleek tail moved slowly behind her, swaying in a calm, controlled rhythm.
Her golden eyes were sharp and focused, glowing faintly under the sunlight, yet holding a depth far beyond her small, delicate appearance.
Her face was soft and innocent, almost doll-like, but her gaze was anything but childish.
She was Kira Leander.
*Picture*
Their elder sister.
And the moment Selene sensed her—
"Poop!"
She cursed.
Then, she glanced at Noctis, whose expressionless face was now replaced with a small, victorious grin and—
"You knew she was watching!"
Selene pointed her little finger at him in anger.
An action against which Noctis just smiled and—
"What?
Wanna fight?"
He repeated the same words she said before and Selene only got even angrier.
"Poop!"
She cursed again.

chapters.title: Chapter 2305: Good to see you too, Mira.
paragraphs: "Poop!"
Selene cursed as she stomped her leg on the ground. Noctis laughed, then he walked towards his sister, gently held her hand and—
"Alright, let’s go in and give the shopkeeper his money."
He spoke responsibly, then he stared at his sister and—
"And stop saying that word, if I hear it again, I will tell Mother Edda."
"And I will tell Mother Melia that you are stalking me!"
Selene didn’t give in.
"I wasn’t stalking, I was counting. It’s different. And it was your brother who told me to do so. He said you didn’t have the money to eat so many candies every day, yet you somehow did."
Noctis revealed the truth and Selene widened her eyes—
"Veyron!?"
She asked, her pink eyes now reflecting anger. Veyron was her real brother, Edda was pregnant with twins, Selene and Veyron, and the two had quite different personalities.

Selene was playful and loved to tease people around her, Veyron, on the other hand, was smarter. He normally acted dumb, childish even, but his mind was scarily quick, he noticed small things that children of his age would often miss.
"Yes."
Noctis nodded.
Noctis was Melia’s only son, he, like his mother, did not talk much, and he had power over blood. He was one of the stronger kids, not many siblings could actually defeat him in a battle.
"That traitor! And to think I gave him one of the candies I stol—"
Little Selene swallowed her words before she said too much, Noctis narrowed his eyes at that, however, before he could ask anything, Selene grabbed his arm and pulled him into the shop.
The sibling pair went in, paid the shopkeeper, despite him saying no many times, then, as they came out—
"How did you even know Sister Kira was here?"
Selene asked curiously.
Kira was Thyra’s only daughter and she and Noctis, because they both were people of few words, were quite close to each other.
Noctis was one of the few people Kira actually talked to.
"Did she follow you here?"
Selene asked curiously.
She wanted to meet Kira too, she wanted to get close to her. Kira had a nigh-perfect stealth, most beings in the world could not detect her presence if she didn’t want them to.
Selene could see countless uses of this ability, so she wanted to get close to her, but Kira, who had already sensed her intentions, usually avoided her.
"She did. The two of us will spar after I return."
Noctis nodded.
"So you only came here to stop me?"
Selene couldn’t believe it.
Just what was wrong with this brother of hers? Why come in the middle of her candy heist? What had she done? Was there a personal vendetta involved?
"Yes."
Noctis nodded.
He then looked at Selene with a solemn look on his face and—
"You should not break rules and you shouldn’t steal, you may not think it through, but your actions can hurt people."
"I don’t steal that much."
Selene muttered in a low voice.
Noctis, however, shook his head.
"It starts small. It is better you stop before it becomes a habit."
"Okay, mom!
Blehhh!"
Selene stuck her tongue out, showing her displeasure. Then, after a while, she thought of another thing—
"Wait."
She spoke out loud. Then, she turned towards Noctis with an excited look on her face and—
"Aren’t you and Sister Kira close?"
"We spar with each other regularly."
Noctis nodded.
"Then her statement doesn’t count!"
Selene grinned.
"Else I could say you stole from me and Velora will say it’s true! Hah!"
Selene’s grin widened, she was so proud of what she thought that she placed both her hands on her waist and puffed her chest.
Noctis looked at her, somewhat shocked, then—
"You still don’t get it, do you?"
"What?"
Selene asked, confused.
And in return, Noctis just asked another question—
"You do know Nyx is back from Aurendor, correct?"
And the instant she heard those words, Selene’s expression changed.
"What...?"
She quickly looked down at her own shadow and noticed it was trembling very softly and that was all it took for her to realize what was happening.
That was Nyx.
She was Mother Lane’s daughter.
A Primordial Shadow Demon, a being who has the ability to... exist inside all shadows simultaneously.
She had been learning to use this ability to grow as a strategist, as a being who would know the location of an entire army before the battle even begins.
She had gone to Aurendor together with Mother Lane to practice her ability, if she was back, then it would mean she had succeeded and if she had succeeded...
Then it meant Nyx watched everything that happened...
Selene couldn’t lie her way out of this.
Selene pointed her finger at Noctis, in an instant, all her excitement about her victory puffed away and she...
"You came prepared, didn’t you!?"
She raised her voice, blaming Noctis.
Noctis just shrugged and—
"Give me my money back, or I will talk to Mother Edda."
Saying those words, Noctis walked away.
"You! Just you wait!"
Selene raised her voice, then, with a cute ’hmph’, she turned towards a different direction and walked away from Noctis, all while angrily eating her candy.
"Hmph! My mood is spoiled!"

Selene complained in her mind, then, as if she thought of something, she changed the direction she was walking in and dashed in a different direction as if she already knew where she wanted to go next.
A few minutes later, she was in a completely different place.
A park.
A place for children and their parents to visit and spend some time together, the moment Selene arrived here, the first thing she heard was children laughing loudly.
She looked around, as if trying to find someone and her eyes finally fell on a group of children running and chasing each other.
Selene smiled when she saw that sight, her eyes then fell on the center of these children, a place where another girl her age stood.

She had soft auburn hair tied into a loose ponytail, with a few gentle strands slipping free and framing her face, giving her a naturally carefree look. The warm tones of her hair glowed softly under the sunlight, adding to the gentle, comforting presence she carried.

Her bright blue eyes sparkled with pure joy, as if she saw the world as something beautiful every single moment. Her cheeks were lightly flushed, and her wide, genuine smile made her look unbelievably adorable.

She wore a light, airy dress in soft pastel shades, simple yet charming, with delicate folds that moved easily as she ran around. The fabric looked comfortable, made for someone who never stayed still for long. A small ribbon was tied at her waist, slightly uneven, like she had done it herself.
The girl clapped excitedly.
"Again! Again!"
The other children cheered as they ran towards her, and she, being much faster than them all, avoided them without any trouble whatsoever.
"Slow! You people are too slow~"
She laughed lightly but the rest of the children didn’t fall back, they laughed as well and continued to try and catch her.
Selene saw that and walked closer, the instant she did, she felt the air around her change, it felt... lighter, warmer even.
And just as she expected—
The instant she got close—
Her mood became better.
"Hehe~"
Selene then disappeared and appeared right beside the girl, out of all the children here, she was the only one who had the ability to do that.
She placed her hand on the girl’s shoulder, shocking the girl for a moment, she couldn’t believe someone actually caught her, but the moment she turned around to see who it was—
"Sister Selene!"
Her eyes widened with pure excitement and happiness and—
"Sister!!"

She jumped on Selene and hugged her as tightly as she could. Selene, after spending some time with Noctis, clearly appreciated the change. An adorable grin appeared on her face as she hugged her sister back.
"Good to see you too, Mira."
She smiled.
Mira then moved away, the smile plastered on her face never faded away even for a moment, then, she excitedly turned towards the benches at which the parents of the children were resting and—
"Mother!!"
She waved excitedly.
"Look! Sister Selene is here!"

She spoke and Skyla, who was sitting on the bench, resting after playing with the children for a few hours, waved back at her daughter and then at Selene with a light, gentle, motherly smile on her face.
It was... quite strange to see such a mature look on Skyla’s face. It just went on showing how much the existence of a child changes a person.
That difference was now clear on Skyla’s face, her motherly gentleness made her... even more charming.
A sight Nux would always appreciate, a sight... he had usually been having a hard time controlling himself in front of...
"Let her play with all of you as well, okay?"
Skyla spoke politely, as she looked at Selene, who had started waving at her as well.
She was good with children to begin with, so almost all children were very close to her, something she enjoyed a lot.
"Yes!"
Mira nodded excitedly before she grabbed Selene’s hands and started telling her the rules, rules Selene quickly grasped and the game continued.

chapters.title: Chapter 2306: The Training Field.
paragraphs: While Selene, Mira, and other children in the Universe were playing in the park, some of Nux’s children were... somewhere else.
A place most children would actively avoid.
The training grounds.
The place was quiet, most people here did not speak, they just observed and tried to learn, and they did it quietly, not bothering anyone.

The training ground was a wide open field at the edge of Umbrasol, surrounded by tall trees and stone structures built for practice. The ground was smooth, but there were cracks here and there—old marks left behind by people who trained a little too seriously.
There were no guards here, they didn’t need to, not when a few of the Universe’s strongest beings were overseeing the training from a distance.
At the center of the ground, a boy stood. He didn’t look any older than Selene, Mira, Noctis, or the other children, but the air around him felt... heavier.
He was Drakar Leander, a Primordial Dragon, son of Ember of Leander.
He had short, deep black-crimson hair, slightly messy but sharp, with a few strands falling over his forehead. His golden eyes burned faintly, with a steady intensity that didn’t fade.

He wore a simple dark outfit, sleeveless, made for movement. It clung lightly to his small frame, but even then, there was something about the way he stood that made him feel far bigger than he actually was.
Drakar took a step forward—
Crack

And the instant he did, the ground beneath him cracked. Yes, it was clear that this little guy was the reason behind the cracks on the ground. It was as if the earth itself had stopped resisting under his feet.

The boy, however, did not react to that, he was already expecting it, he just took another step, this one was even stronger, leaving an even wider crack, as he dashed forward towards another boy his age.

The boy had long, dark red, messy and unkempt hair that reached his shoulders. His sharp golden eyes shone brighter than Drakar’s, filled with excitement, almost like he was constantly looking for a fight.
He was wearing a red sleeveless shirt, with a terrifying Dragon printed on the front, matching the boy’s fiery and aggressive aura.
He was Zyrax.
Another Primordial Dragon, he was Vyriana’s son and just like his mother, he was obsessed with strength.

The moment Drakar dashed at him, Zyrax straightened slowly. His long dark red hair danced in the wind, and the grin on his face only grew wider. Like Drakar, he too extended his fists, prepared to meet head-on—
Their fists finally collided and—
BOOOOOM
Pure, brute physical force exploded.
The ground cracked even further, a tree on the left leaned at a dangerous angle, almost as if it was about to tear apart but stopped at the last second and returned to its original position.
A sight Zyrax did not like.
"You did it again,"
He spoke in a slightly disappointed voice.
"You pulled back at the end."
Drakar stared at him, his golden eyes were steady.
Drakar was a little shorter than Zyrax, but his shoulders were broader. Unlike Zyrax’s restless presence, Drakar felt more... compact, controlled.
"You were pushed back."
He spoke, looking at Zyrax’s feet, that were now a few inches behind where he originally was.
"Yes, yes, I was. You came out stronger in that exchange."
Zyrax laughed, but then he spread his arms dramatically and—
"But I am still standing and I am asking for more—
That is not victory.
You fight till your opponent doesn’t dare ask for more."
He spoke with a wide grin, Drakar, however, just frowned and—
"Is that even possible when my opponent is a crazy fool li—"
Before he could even complete his words, Drakar felt the air around him change. A low, suffocating pressure spread through the field, a pressure that got heavier with each passing second.
The pressure itself wasn’t visible, but its impact was. The leaves on the trees began to rustle without the wind, the pebbles on the ground began to shake slightly and—
BOOOM
The very air collapsed inwardly as the pressure became even more suffocating.
A Dragon’s Aura.
Zyrax let it all pour out of him with a shameless, joyful grin on his face.
"Stop holding back."
He spoke as his golden eyes shone even more intensely and his aura burned even more fiercely, rolling from his body like flames.

An elbow to the shoulder.
A knee to the stomach.

Fight!

The training grounds.

chapters.title: Chapter 2307: Let it collapse. I’ll take responsibility.
paragraphs: BAM
Thud
Drakar’s body went flying, it tore through a tree and finally—
Drakar finally collapsed on the ground and for the next second, dust swallowed him completely.
Zyrax stood in the center of the ruined ground, breathing hard, yes, after the battle, even he was tired too.
But the best part was that he knew it wasn’t over.
Drakar could still go on.
"Stand up, I know you can still fight!"
He spoke excitedly, his breathing flaring even more strongly.
"Don’t you dare act in front of me!
If you break, then break after you win!"
Zyrax spoke even louder and finally—
The dust cloud that had formed shifted slightly and Drakar walked out slowly.
The calm on his face had changed. He no longer seemed... patient. He seemed... irritated. Battle was one thing, but hearing Zyrax’s voice, even when he was exhausted to this point—
It made him angry, he wanted to shut this little thing up for good.

Drakar glared at Zyrax intensely, scales now covered both his arms, his shoulders, and a part of his neck. Thin lines of red light moved beneath them like flowing magma. That was pure heat his body was now radiating, and it had started burning the ground under him.
A ground of a High-Level World that could even bear the battle between Transcendent-Level Beings.
"There you are."
Zyrax’s smile turned savage as he glanced at Drakar.
This.
This was exactly what he wanted to see.
Drakar, on the other hand, didn’t say anything.
He just vanished, so quickly that even Zyrax couldn’t react to his movements. He could barely raise his guard in time.
BOOOOOOM
Drakar’s fist slammed into his crossed arms with enough force to send a deep ring-shaped crater through the ground around them.
BOOOM
Before Zyrax could recover, Drakar drove a second strike into his stomach, lifting him off the ground.
"Khwwaakkh!!"
Zyrax spat into the air, his eyes widening just a little, and Drakar followed with a third hit to the chest that launched him straight through the air.
Thud
Zyrax hit the ground.
His body bounced once, then twice, then...
Then the monster rolled, absorbing the impact naturally and... he forced himself up.
Yes, he was standing.
And...
He was still smiling.
Even now.
Even when his scales were lying on the ground beneath him, broken.
But it didn’t matter.
Zyrax’s grin widened, the remaining scales on his body spread further, Zyrax’s scales were jagged and darker than Drakar’s, they crawled up the sides of his face and down both hands.
His aura rose wildly in answer, meeting Drakar’s heavier force with... violent excitement.
"That!
Do that again!"
He laughed as he exploded forward.
Drakar didn’t hold back either, this was no longer the time to exchange small strikes, now, they were going all out and it was like seeing two storms collide, trying to crush each other.
BOOOOM BOOOOM BOOOOM
Auras burst in waves, the field split deeper, every impact sent pieces of stone and broken trees spinning away like thrown knives. A nearby hundred-meter-large boulder cracked from top to bottom.
The air itself shook under the weight of their Dragon Auras, it had become strong enough to crush any being under the Primordial Level.

Zyrax swung wide, forcing Drakar to block high, then drove a shoulder into him and pushed. Drakar planted his feet, stopping the charge, and the two locked there for a moment, foreheads nearly touching, scales scraping against scales.
Zyrax’s eyes gleamed.
"Harder! Put more strength!"
He grinned.
Drakar’s brows twitched.
"Shut up!"
He cursed and then he did exactly what Zyrax had demanded.
He pushed more power into the fight.
The pressure around his body thickened even further. His aura no longer merely clashed with Zyrax’s. It began... crushing it back.
The broken ground beneath his feet sank, heat blasted outward from him in a sharp pulse and Zyrax—
The moment he felt this change.
The moment he realized Drakar had gotten stronger than before, that he did indeed push past his limits and had actually become stronger than him—
"HAHAHA!!
You did it!"
He laughed and he shoved harder too, refusing to give ground.
This was it, this was what he wanted.
To push his big brother beyond what he was capable of, so he could use that to get stronger.

And as their clash continued, the place around them began to fall apart in earnest. A large section of the field to their right collapsed inward with a loud crack. About ten nearby trees snapped directly, dust and fragments rained down over the field.
Still the two Dragons fought.
Zyrax swung, Drakar blocked.
Drakar answered, Zyrax caught the blow on his scales and took the damage just to stay close.
They slammed into each other again and again, each exchange more dangerous than the last and Zyrax sensed it...
His plan had worked.
He was growing.
He was getting stronger.
A little more—
He wanted to fight a little more—
But then—
"That is enough.
Stop it."
A cold voice cut through the chaos.
The two Dragons paused and they both turned towards the voice with frowns on their faces.
"If this continues, the entire place will collapse in five more exchanges. We cannot have that."
The third entrant spoke again.
It was Oraya Leander, only son of Amaya Leander.
Oraya stood in the middle of all this chaos with a calm, easy look on his face, almost as if the chaos around him did not affect him one bit.
He looked entirely out of place there.

He had pitch-black hair that was kept neatly despite the violent wind around him, not a single strand was out of place. His black eyes were calm, sharp, and observant, quietly scanning the destroyed surroundings around him with precise focus.
He was wearing a long vest, layered with a high-collared shirt, showing that he was more of a strategist than a fighter.
His posture was straight and relaxed with one hand inside his pocket, honestly, the way he stood with that solemn gaze, combined with his childish features, made him look even more adorable.
Drakar breathed heavily, his shoulders rising and falling. Zyrax wiped dust from his cheek with the back of his hand and—
"Five?"
He asked in an amused tone.
Oraya nodded.
"That is correct.
The battle made Drakar stronger, you became stronger too, that was why I didn’t interrupt before.
But now that you two have already gotten stronger, there is no point in continuing. You will only destroy the place."
"What makes you think we can’t grow even stronger?"
Zyrax asked, his golden eyes shining with clear resistance, as if he wanted to prove Oraya wrong, something he had been trying for as long as he could remember, but had never once succeeded.
Oraya too, looked at him for a moment, his black eyes seemed as if they could see through everything and—
"You won’t.
Your body is exhausted, so is his mind.
Even if you force yourself to fight, the best possible improvement will be your instincts, nothing else."
"That’s enough too!"
Zyrax smiled as he rubbed his fists, Oraya, however, shook his head again.
"It is not. Not when you are already in this state, resting and fighting later once your body has recovered will have more benefits."
Zyrax stared at him for a good moment, then, he just clicked his tongue.
"You bore me."
He spoke as he placed his hands behind his head.
Drakar didn’t say anything, but his annoyance deepened. He had finally stopped listening to Zyrax’s voice inside the fight, and now Oraya had stepped in with his ’analysis’.
And just when he thought this was over—
Another figure dropped from above.
"You people aren’t stopping just because black hair here said you won’t grow, are you?
Just prove him wrong!"
The boy grinned and the moment Oraya looked at him, he just shook his head.
"Like you have ever done that."
He spoke lightly.
The boy’s mouth twitched in annoyance, but since he knew the black-haired boy was correct, he didn’t argue and turned towards the Dragons instead.
"Ignore him, you just fight!"
He spoke as he grabbed his sword and Oraya... he just facepalmed.
Two Dragons were still manageable, but how was he supposed to stop them when even this one got involved?

Ragnar Leander was a sword freak, just like his mother. So much so that he didn’t even put his sword inside his storage ring, the sword stayed with him the way another child might keep a favorite toy, except there was nothing childish about the way his fingers curled around it.

Ragnar himself had brown hair, slightly disheveled from the jump, his brown eyes stared at the Dragons and the destruction around them with bright interest, clearly, he too, wanted to join in the fun.
Zyrax too, looked at his elder brother with great interest.
Ragnar and Zyrax were close, solely because they had a similar mindset.
A battle?
They were always ready for it.
"Let’s do it.
Let’s make it a three-way! Last one standing wins!"
Zyrax announced despite being the weakest of the three.
"That sounds goo—"
Ragnar was about to agree but—
"The place is about to collapse."
Oraya spoke directly.
Ragnar, however, just shrugged and rested his sword over his shoulder.
"Let it collapse.
I’ll take responsibility."
He spoke confidently.

Drakar didn’t say anything, but his annoyance deepened.
He had finally stopped listening to Zyrax’s voice inside the fight, and now Oraya had stepped in with his ’analysis’.
And just when he thought this was over—
Another figure dropped from above.
"You people aren’t stopping just because black hair here said you won’t grow, are you?
Just prove him wrong!"
The boy grinned and the moment Oraya looked at him, he just shook his head.
"Like you have ever done that."
He spoke lightly.
The boy’s mouth twitched in annoyance, but since he knew the black-haired boy was correct, he didn’t argue and turned towards the Dragons instead.
"Ignore him, you just fight!"
He spoke as he grabbed his sword and Oraya... he just facepalmed.
Two Dragons were still manageable, but how was he supposed to stop them when even this one got involved?
Ragnar Leander was a sword freak, just like his mother.

So much so that he didn’t even put his sword inside his storage ring, the sword stayed with him the way another child might keep a favorite toy, except there was nothing childish about the way his fingers curled around it.

Ragnar himself had brown hair, slightly disheveled from the jump, his brown eyes stared at the Dragons and the destruction around them with bright interest, clearly, he too, wanted to join in the fun.
Zyrax too, looked at his elder brother with great interest.
Ragnar and Zyrax were close, solely because they had a similar mindset.
A battle?
They were always ready for it.
"Let’s do it.
Let’s make it a three-way!
Last one standing wins!"
Zyrax announced despite being the weakest of the three.
"That sounds goo—"
Ragnar was about to agree but—
"The place is about to collapse."
Oraya spoke directly.
Ragnar, however, just shrugged and rested his sword over his shoulder.
"Let it collapse.
I’ll take responsibility."
He spoke confidently.
