sentences.text: "...Are you two... doing this?"
The man asked as he slowly walked towards the two children.
Lysera looked up at him with a soft, gentle smile on her face and—
"Doing what?"
She asked curiously.
The man hesitated for a moment, he had no clue how he was supposed to explain it, but he tried anyways.
"This... everything.
Trees, water, wind... nothing is moving the way it should."
"It is working as it should."
Aurelios answered calmly, he had a gentle smile on his face, just like his sister, a smile one couldn’t be angry in front of.
"That’s... not how it usually works,"
The man muttered, he still looked somewhat confused.
"That is because it is usually unstable."
Aurelios answered as if it was a matter of fact.
"...Unstable?"
The man frowned in confusion.
Lysera stood slowly, brushing her dress with her hands.
"Things decay.
They weaken and they fail."
She spoke as she looked around, at the vast field around her.
"That is not necessary."
She commented.
The man paused for a moment, his eyes fell on the structure behind him, the perfect wall without any crack, then, with a somewhat lost look on his face—
"...but that’s how the world is."
He muttered.
"That’s how the world is because no one does anything to change it.
We will."
Aurelios answered with a determined look on his face.
The man looked at him, feeling slightly overwhelmed, but he didn’t say anything.
Lysera then walked a few steps forward, her eyes fell on a small plant growing near the base of the structure, its leaves slightly curled.
Aurelios frowned at that behavior, but he didn’t stop her, not yet.
Lysera crouched beside it, her fingers touched it gently, the plant responded just like the grass did, its color deepened, leaves straightened, stem thickened, then—
It grew.
Its roots expanded beneath the soil, its structure shifted, its form changed, it became... stronger.
Then even stronger again.
Then it changed further.
The leaves sharpened.
The edges hardened.
The plant twisted slightly, forming a shape that no longer matched anything natural in Umbrasol.
The air shifted and finally—
"...that is enough."
Aurelios spoke with a solemn look on his face.
Lysera paused.
For a brief moment—
The warmth around her disappeared, the atmosphere grew heavy, her soft eyes darkened slightly.
"It can grow more."
She spoke in a low, slightly threatening voice.
"It does not need to."
Aurelios responded accordingly.
"It can."
"That is not the same."
Aurelios spoke.
"If it grows any further, the world around it won’t be able to adapt, it won’t be able to reproduce and evolution needs reproduction, you should understand that more than me.
Altering one sole existence is an experiment, not evolution.
Understand the difference."
Lysera did not say anything, she just stared at Aurelios and the plant behind her stopped changing.
It remained in its altered form, different from what it was before, stronger than what it was before, but it was no longer evolving.
Lysera exhaled softly, then her expression returned to gentle.
"...alright, as you say, big brother."
Aurelios nodded slightly, the tension in the air eased down, or at least that’s what it looked like, but the man who had approached them... slowly took a step back and—
"I... think I should go."
Neither child stopped him, he turned and walked away, faster than before, almost as if he was running away.
And once he left, the two siblings looked at each other and Lysera grinned—
"See?
You scared him."
"I wasn’t the one turning a simple plant into a monster."
"I wasn’t making it a monster."
"You were making it so it wouldn’t be able to reproduce, that is a monster."
"I did not..."
The siblings continued to argue, as the things around them continued to change in an odd way.
In the busy streets of Umbrasol, people walked freely, speaking to one another without hesitation, stalls lined the sides of the road, displaying fruits, tools, simple clothes, and handmade items.
The air carried the soft sounds of conversation, light laughter, and the occasional clink of metal or wood being adjusted.
Everything moved naturally.
Until something small happened.
A clay cup slipped from a woman’s hand.
It fell.
It should have shattered the moment it hit the ground.
Instead—
It landed upright.
Perfectly.
Not even a crack.
The woman blinked.
She stared at the cup for a moment, then picked it up slowly.
"...That was lucky."
She smiled and moved on.

Because small things like that could happen.
Sometimes.

It did not fall.

chapters.title: Chapter 2315: I want to defeat Ragnar.
paragraphs: "You could’ve broken your leg!"
The old man screamed in anger as he rushed towards Kaelion.
"But I didn’t."
Kaelion laughed and before anyone could say anything else, he ran towards a narrow gap between two stalls, narrow enough that it was impossible for him to move through it—
But that did not slow him down.
He just dashed forward and then he jumped again—
He should have hit the edge, his shoulder should have hit the wall, he should have fallen down—
But—
He passed through perfectly, without a single scratch.
Once he reached the other side, he looked at the old man through the same narrow gap and—
"See?"
He spoke before he dashed away.
Someone muttered under their breath.
"...Ridiculous."
Kaelion didn’t hear them, even if he did, he simply didn’t care. His curious eyes spotted something else, a tall stack of barrels near the side of the street.
Without thinking—
He ran toward them.
"Hey! Don’t—"
Someone shouted but...
Too late.
Kaelion climbed up the side of the barrels quickly, using small gaps between them to pull himself higher.
One of the barrels shifted.
Then another.
The entire stack tilted.
"It’s going to fall!"
People stepped back immediately.
Kaelion reached the top, he stood there, grinning as if he didn’t even sense the barrels beneath him were going to fall, taking him down with them.
The barrels tilted further, as if they were about to fall completely—
But just then—

One barrel slipped further back, into a position that somehow supported the rest, and it didn’t end there, it pushed a few more barrels, all moving into different positions that somehow supported the structure and—
The entire structure held, God knows how.
Kaelion blinked, seemingly surprised.
That worked too."
"What in the hell is that child...?"
A man muttered, staring at him with a confused look on his face.
"...that’s not normal."
Another woman spoke in a low voice.
Meanwhile, leaning against a wooden post nearby—
Another boy watched it all play out.
He was Veyron Leander, Edda’s son.
Like his sister, he was ten as well, both of them were twins.
At first glance... there was nothing special about Veyron. His hair was an odd mix of brown and faint pink, slightly out of place, like he hadn’t bothered to fix it.
His golden eyes... didn’t shine like Kaelion’s.

They were half-lidded, dull, as if he would fall asleep this very moment. When he looked at something, it didn’t feel like he was paying attention at all. In fact, it felt like he was barely even there.
His face carried no strong emotion.
No excitement.
No curiosity.
Just... boredom.
He wore simple clothes, slightly wrinkled, a bit untidy, like he had put them on without thinking.

His posture was lazy. His shoulders were relaxed, his weight leaned slightly to one side, like standing straight itself was too much effort. One hand hung loosely, the other occasionally moved just enough to scratch his head or rub his eye.
Then—
He yawned.
"...he’s going to try something else."
He muttered with that yawn.
"What?"
A man standing near him frowned.
"He’s going to jump from there."
Veyron pointed without actually putting in the effort to look at the man.
The man turned and Kaelion, he, while standing at the top of the barrels, his golden eyes shone and the man’s expression changed—
"...Don’t tell me—"
The man’s expression changed, but it was too late.
Kaelion jumped.
"—he actually did it..."
The man blinked.
The worst part?
This time, the boy had jumped even farther.
Too far actually and there was nothing below him. No box that carried blankets, no support, nothing.
For a brief moment—
It looked like he would fall straight onto the stone ground.
Then—
Another cart pulled by a Reinfer Horse passed by and...
Kaelion fell right inside it, without any injuries at all.
"...when did you get there?"
The person pulling the cart asked with a confused look on his face.
"Just now!"
Kaelion sat up, laughing.
The man standing near Veyron slowly turned his head and—
"...how did you know that?"
He asked with a surprised look on his face.
"You learn to notice when you have to live with that."
Veyron shrugged as he pointed at his brother who was now coming out of the cart with a silly smile.
Yes, the ’that’ he was referring to was his brother.
The man looked at their similar eyes and guessed they were brothers, Veyron didn’t bother with him any longer, he just looked around lazily and his eyes fell on the fruit stall nearby.
One of its wooden supports looked weak.
"Don’t touch that."
Veyron spoke again.
"...What?"
The stall owner froze.
"Just don’t."
He didn’t bother explaining.
The stall owner hesitated.
Then—
He ignored the child, he reached out and adjusted the support and the instant he did—
It snapped and the entire side of the stall dropped, fruit rolling across the ground, picked by children, who grabbed a few and ran.
The stall owner blinked.
Then looked back at Veyron.
"You knew that would happen?"
"...It was obvious."
Veyron scratched his head.
"Boy, I have been selling for years.
It was not obvious."
Veyron didn’t argue, he just shrugged and looked away.
At the center of the street, Kaelion had already jumped out of the cart and was now running again.
"Hey!"
He called out.
"Watch this!"
"No—don’t—"
He grabbed a long wooden pole from a nearby stall, and started spinning it carelessly.
"Hey! Watch out!!"
People screamed as they backed away instantly.
"He’s going to hit someone!"
And the moment those words were said—
Kaelion lost his grip.
The pole flew out of his hands, straight toward a group of people, the people’s gasps filled the air, one of them prepared to catch it, but at the very last second—
The pole hit the edge of a hanging cloth.
The cloth wrapped around it, slowed it down and harmlessly dropped it to the ground.
And the entire area turned silent.
Until...
"That almost didn’t work."
Until Kaelion laughed again.
"...Almost?"
Someone nearby muttered, his mouth twitching.
"It was always going to miss."
Veyron spoke again, still leaning against the post.
"How do you know that?"
Veyron looked at the pole on the ground, then at Kaelion, then at the person who asked this question and he just sighed—
"I just know."
He couldn’t be bothered explaining, it was too long.

That was just how Veyron was, he had keen insight, almost at the level of future prediction, so much that he, despite being weaker than most of his siblings, could fight them head-on because he was able to predict almost all their moves.
The only way for them to defeat him was through overwhelming force, which, admittedly, because of his laziness, he lacked.
"Hahaha~ That was fun~"

Kaelion, on the other hand, laughed loudly, his golden eyes began looking around again, his eyes then fell on one of the nearby houses, the tallest of all the houses there, the moment people saw the light in his eyes, they felt a bad premonition, but this time, before Kaelion could dash forward like he usually did—
Someone grabbed him from behind.
It was Veyron.
"Haahh... I can’t believe I have to be the one to do this."
He spoke in a tired voice as he facepalmed.
"Where are the responsible lot? Why is no one keeping an eye on this thing?"
He complained, calling his brother a ’thing’.
"Why are you stopping me?"
Kaelion asked. Veyron looked at him, then, with a serious look on his face—
"Stop testing your luck. You know it doesn’t work all the time. Eloria isn’t here either, do all these shenanigans when she is around."
"But my luck falls when she is around because it knows I won’t get hurt!"
Kaelion complained.
"Talk to Father, I don’t know.
I can’t let you get hurt in front of me or I’ll be blamed."
"No one will blame you, I promise."
"As if your promise means anything."
Veyron spoke directly as he pulled Kaelion with him, Kaelion resisted, actually, he was stronger than his brother, so if he wanted, he could get away, but he didn’t wish to hurt Veyron so he gave in.
Veyron, who had already predicted that, just sighed and—
"You know you can’t train your luck like this, right?"
He asked seriously and for a very slight moment, the smile on Kaelion’s face faded away.
"I am not trying to control it."
He answered seriously.
"What do you mean?"
Kaelion looked at him, somewhat surprised to see him act like this, then, he looked into his eyes and realized it.
"You are trying to understand when it works and when it doesn’t."
Kaelion nodded at those words.
Veyron asked.
Kaelion was incredibly lucky, just knowing that should be enough, no? Why bother trying to understand something random?
"So that I can control it and get stronger."
"I want to defeat Ragnar."
"That’s a tough goal."
"I’ll defeat him."
"Whatever you say."

chapters.title: Chapter 2316: PULL BACK DAMMIT!!
paragraphs: While Umbrasol was at peace with just some minor mishaps happening every other day, some of the other worlds in Nux’s Universe weren’t the same.
These were the worlds where the ambitious went, people who wanted to rule over all, no matter what it took.
Worlds where things like assassinations, duels, battles, murders, mass genocide—
All of it was an everyday occurrence.
Jiahra was one such world.
It was a Low Level World when Nux devoured it and even now, the strength of the people here was somewhat similar, Nux however, had made one change.
Now, Jiahra did not have one ruler like it previously did.
This was one of the worlds for the ambitious, but one cannot be ambitious if there is a being capable of wiping their existence with one wave of his hand.
And Nux changed that.
He... made it fair.
He placed a limit on the people who could live in Jiahra. Anyone above Saint would automatically be moved to another world and only Saints and those below would stay.
So now, there were thousands and thousands of Saints in Jiahra, beings who now stood at each other’s throats, ready to crush each other to rule above the rest.
This was no longer about one chosen being who ruled others, now, it was about skill, political manoeuvres, and war tactics. A level any being in this world could now reach.
The sky above it was grey, it always was. It wasn’t dark enough to be called night, but it wasn’t bright enough to feel like day either.

It was a dull, heavy color stretched endlessly above the land. The air was dry, carrying the scent of ash and iron, and the wind moved in uneven bursts, kicking up dust that never seemed to settle for long.

Cracked earth stretched across the ground, marked by old impacts and fresh destruction. Burnt patches spread like dark stains, and broken weapons, shattered shields and bodies were scattered all over the battlefield.
That was the new Jiahra.
And in this new Jiahra, in these past ten years, amongst all the battles, physical or political, two factions had risen up.
And right now—
These two factions were at war.
At one end, there was the Ironclad Dominion.
A faction that valued order, structure and discipline.
Rows and rows of soldiers stood in perfect formation. Their shields were locked tightly together, forming an unbroken wall of steel. Long spears extended outward, aligned with precision.
Behind them stood their greatest strength.
Iron Constructs.

Towering machines built from metal and magic, they were bulky and slow, but that made them terrifyingly durable. Their limbs were thick and reinforced repeatedly, they were capable of crushing anything that came too close.
Literal war machines made to crush the enemy.
And that said enemy was the Ashen Tide.
A faction that was the exact opposite of the Ironclad Dominion, a force that valued chaos, movement and relentless force.

Their soldiers did not stand in neat lines. They shifted, paced, adjusted constantly, some leaned forward eagerly, others rolled their shoulders, gripping weapons loosely, waiting for the moment to strike.
Their armor was lighter, their weapons varied, their strength didn’t come from structure, it came from their unpredictability and relentless pressure.
The Ashen Tide did not have literal golems standing behind them, even if a few beings there knew about magic and metal, they weren’t coordinated enough to create something like that.
But if there was one thing odd about the Ashen Tide—
It was the small figure standing at the very front of their chaotic army.
A little girl.
She didn’t look older than ten.
She had long black hair, touched with faint crimson shades. Her face was soft, so beautiful that it didn’t belong in a place like this, but her expression held none of that softness.
She wore dark, fitted clothes suited for movement that remained clean despite the chaos around her.
Her golden eyes were bright and had that sharp look in them. They moved constantly, scanning everything—the broken ground, the shifting lines, even the smallest movements in the distance.
She looked completely out of place.
Neither her size, nor her age was suited for a place like this.
Or at least—
That’s what the Ironclad Dominion thought of her.
They mistook her calmness for ignorance, that the child was too young to understand what was happening here and the trouble she was in.
But that was when the girl raised her hand, the soldiers from the Ironclad Dominion frowned, what was she doing? Calling for help? But...
Why did her face look so... calm? Shouldn’t she be crying if she wanted help?
They wondered in their heads but then—
The girl dropped her hand forward and—
"Charge."
She spoke in a low voice, but for some odd reason, her words echoed throughout the battlefield and the instant they did—
"RRRAAAAAAAAAHHHHHHHH!!!"

The Ashen Tide charged forward, every soldier rushing towards the enemy with different weapons in their hands while passing through the little girl, who stood right at the middle of that chaos with her hand still pointed at the enemy.
An action that surprised the Ironclad Dominion, they had no clue why the enemy would listen to a little girl.

But soon, the Dominion Leaders shook their heads, it was the Ashen Tide, they didn’t have a pattern, if, for some reason, they brought a little girl to signal the start of war for them, it didn’t matter.
The result was going to be the same—
"FORMATIONS!"
The Dominion General commanded, the troops aligned their shields properly and with that, the first collision began.
"TEAR THEM APART!!"
"HAHAHAHA!!"
"KILL!!!"
The Ashen Tide soldiers laughed as they pushed through, they moved so densely that the enemy shield lines were collapsing at a ridiculous pace.
Yes, the battle had only begun and the Ironclad Dominion was already being pushed back. Its soldiers were dying, their formation was being pushed back.
For the first ten minutes, everything was going well for the Ashen Tide soldiers and they carried forward that momentum and crushed every head they got the chance to.
"HAHAHAHA!!"
The Ashen Tide General, a large warrior who was now standing beside the little girl, laughed.
"See? There’s no need for strategy to wipe out those fools! You do it with sheer force!"
He spoke with a grin as he rubbed his bulging bicep.
The little girl beside him however, didn’t say anything, she just stared at the battlefield and then—
With the same calm look on her face—
"The centre is going to collapse if your people continue to push like that."
She spoke without a single change in her tone.
The General frowned at those words.
"What are you talking about? We’re winning that side."
He muttered.
If it were some other girl, he would have ignored her, what would a child know about the battlefield?
But this one was different.
The General knew better than to doubt her, he had seen her skills, this was the reason she was here in the first place.
"They’re letting you win."
The girl spoke in the same tone without even looking at him.
"What?"
The General frowned in confusion, the girl then pointed forward—
"Look carefully."
The General turned.
At first, everything looked normal.
The Ashen Tide was pushing forward in the center, the Ironclads were being pushed back, but then—
The General narrowed his eyes.
Something didn’t make sense.
This was... going too well.
The Ironclads being pushed back... looked more like they were retreating and they didn’t seem like they were doing it out of fear.
They were... luring them in.
"They’re pulling back in formation..."
He muttered with a frown.
"Yes,"
The girl nodded.
"They’re creating space."
"For what?"
He asked and the girl narrowed her eyes ever so slightly.
"The constructs."
And as if on cue—
The Ironclad front line shifted, the shield wall opened slightly, the Ashen Tide soldiers saw this as an opportunity for the first instant, but then—
They appeared.
Those massive Iron Constructs.
RUMBLE
The ground shook from their weight,
"...shit."
The General cursed.
"If you keep pushing forward, they’ll trap you between the constructs and the shield wall. You’ll lose half your force in less than a minute."
The little girl spoke again in her calm tone.
The warrior looked at her, this time, he seemed more desperate.
"...what do we do?"
He asked.
"Pull back."
The girl answered as if she was waiting for him to ask.
"What?"
The General frowned.
"Pull back just enough to make them think their plan is working."
"That’s risky."
"Yes."
The girl nodded, then she finally turned and looked at the general for the first time—
"But if you don’t, you lose anyway."
She spoke and the moment she said those words,
"PULL BACK FROM THE CENTER!"
He commanded.
"PULL BACK DAMMIT!!
OR I WILL KILL YOU PERSONALLY!!!"
He screamed and the Ashen Tide, as unorganized and rogue as they were—
With their General outright threatening them—
They pulled back despite all the fun they were having crushing heads.

chapters.title: Chapter 2317: Did you have fun?
paragraphs: "PULL BACK FROM THE CENTER!"
The Ashen Tide General commanded.
"PULL BACK DAMMIT!!
OR I WILL KILL YOU PERSONALLY!!!"
He screamed and the Ashen Tide, as unorganized and rogue as they were—
With their General outright threatening them—
They pulled back despite all the fun they were having crushing heads. Their movements weren’t smooth, but it was enough.
The forward pressure eased, and the Ironclad Dominion reacted instantly.
The Ironclad Dominion reacted instantly, their constructs surged forward and their shields closed in, exactly as the little girl predicted.
"They’re committing,"
The General commented.
The girl nodded lightly, then, she smiled.
"Good."
Her gaze moved again.
"Left flank, make them move behind the ridge. Tell them not to attack yet."
She spoke.
And the General ordered as he was commanded—
"LEFT FLANK! MOVE BEHIND THE RIDGE! DON’T ATTACK YET!"
"But we have an opening—"
Someone tried to counter but—
"DO AS I SAID!"
The General screamed and the people followed.
"They’re watching that side. If you move now, they’ll reinforce."
The girl spoke lightly, the General didn’t know how much of what she said was true, but he just decided to trust her.

His orders spread, the battlefield shifted, the Iron Constructs moved forward into empty space and the Ashen Tide soldiers split around the constructs, slipping past their slow movements, striking at the weaker sections behind them.
"Now,"
The girl spoke lightly.
"NOW!!"
The General screamed, the left flank moved as they were told and struck the exposed side of the Ironclad formation.
The shield wall broke, enough to create a small opening for the Ashen Tide to take advantage of.
Confusion spread through the Ironclad ranks.
"They’re losing formation!"
Someone shouted.
The girl’s eyes continued to watch the battlefield steadily.
"Don’t chase. Hold pressure."
She commanded.
"DON’T CHASE! HOLD PRESSURE!"
The General commanded.
The men surged and then they stabilized, not overextending their movements and avoiding all traps.
The soldiers could sense it as well, their General’s commands had just saved their lives, and this filled them with an odd sense of trust.
Trust they did not have before.

And with this new sense of trust, even the rogue Ashen Tide began to listen, they moved exactly where they were commanded to, following their General’s words to the letter without him having to threaten them.
An experience which even the General found new and... oddly refreshing.
It was... fun.
It felt... powerful.

And while he felt all these odd emotions, his eyes fell on the little girl watching everything beside him, without a change in her expression, as if everything that was happening was exactly as it was supposed to happen.
’Just... what is this girl...?’
He wondered in his head, but he knew there was no answer to this question, at least he didn’t have it.
High above the battlefield—
Two figures hovered in the air, watching everything play out in silence. No being below could sense their presence, none of them were capable of it.

They were... far, far stronger than any being present on the battlefield, so much so that with a flick of their finger, they could flatten out the entire place and it wouldn’t make a difference to them.
Not that they were planning on doing anything like that.
First, it was against the Universe’s rules, no foreign being, unless part of the war itself, could attack a world or its residents.
Second, they just didn’t want to. They hadn’t come here to attack a side, they were here to watch over that little girl, making sure she didn’t get hurt amongst all this chaos.
As for who these two beings were...?
They were the Origins.
Dagahra Origin.
Saphira Origin.
The Dragon Progenitors of Yrniel, Vyriana’s masters and... somewhat grandparents to all of Nux’s children.
And that group included the little girl below.
Ignira Leander.
She was the daughter of Ember Leander, a tactical genius with fire power that overpowered all other dragon children in the family.

And while Zyrax, Vyriana’s son, was stronger than her in a one-on-one battle, if it came to overall value as a soldier, Ignira was more than a few levels above. Her understanding of the battlefield and tactics was far stronger than most children, only children like Orion and Veyron were somewhat close but when it came to pure understanding of war, even they fell behind her.
That was Ignira Leander, who had dedicated herself to training and war ever since she was born.
Both Dagahra and Saphira adored her and her dedication, this was the reason they were quite close to her and often brought her to war-ridden worlds in order to give her real life experience.
Right now was no different, they were the ones who had brought the girl here and the girl came readily.
She may not show it, but she enjoyed these battles and taking command over the army more than she showed.
"She didn’t even hesitate."
Dagahra grinned with a proud look on his face.
"She saw the trap before it was set."
Saphira nodded, she seemed proud too.
Of course, the trap was quite obvious and easy to find, but this was war. Logic doesn’t apply here, not when the enemy is rushing forward with their weapons pointed at you.
Being able to calm herself through all that chaos and notice a trap was difficult and Ignira pulled it off fabulously.
It made the two Dragon Progenitors proud and made them look forward to the battle.
Below—
"Right side—shift inward. Cut their support lines."
Ignira continued to give her orders, the Ashen Tide’s General shouted her orders and the people moved.
The Ashen Tide adjusted again.
The Ironclad Dominion faltered.
Their structure had begun to break.
"W-What is happening!?"
"What’s wrong with these bastards!?"
"Why are they moving so... readily!?"
"Their General! It’s their General! Kill him!! Charge at him!!"
"How the fuck am I supposed to do that!? We are surrounded, the only way out is being blocked by our own constructs!"
Panic spread all over the Dominion’s troops, Ignira used that moment to give more commands, attacking right where it hurt the most.
"She’s controlling everything,"
Saphira chuckled.
"Of course she is.
She understands everything now!"
Dagahra laughed, now he looked even more proud.
"She’s still learning."
Saphira glanced at him. Dagahra, however, just snorted.
"She’s already better than most commanders I know."
It was big praise, but Saphira agreed with him at some level, Ignira was exceptional. She was actually running out of things she could teach her.
But then, Saphira’s gaze shifted slightly.
"He called earlier."
She spoke in a light tone.
"I know."
Dagahra waved his hand.
"He wants us back."
Saphira spoke nonetheless.
"Bah!"
Dagahra, however, just scoffed.
"Let him call."
"Ember also sent word."
Saphira sighed lightly.
"We’ll go when this is over."
Dagahra shrugged.
"This isn’t important."
Dagahra looked down at the battlefield and...
"It is for her."
Below—
"Ignira continued.
"Center—collapse inward."
"CENTER—COLLAPSE INWARD!!"
The General copied the girl’s orders, the Ashen Tide’s soldiers surged.
The Ironclad Dominion tried to reform, but it was already too late, their formation was broken.
And the Ashen Tide could feel it.
Victory was close.
That was when Ignira stepped forward, her golden eyes moved rapidly as they scanned the entire battlefield again.
She knew that victory was close, but she also knew these were the exact moments when things went wrong, she had learned it the hard way, so she wasn’t going to let her guard down.
Not right now.
Not when she was so close.
So the little girl continued to expand her senses and then—
She froze as she sensed something.
Then, a big grin appeared on her face.
Above her, Saphira looked at Dagahra and chuckled.
"She felt him."
"...Of course she did."
Dagahra snorted. He didn’t like this one bit. However, Ignira below had already abandoned the battlefield.
"Hey! Where are you goin—"
The General tried to call her but she just shrugged and—
"It’s a won war, what more do you need?
Take care of it yourself!"
The little girl answered, this was the most she had spoken ever since she appeared. It was almost as if her entire personality had changed.
The General had no idea why this happened, but he couldn’t think too much, not when the war still wasn’t over.
"...There she goes."
Dagahra above sighed.
What General leaves her army like that?
"She’s still a child."
Saphira smiled faintly.
Far ahead—
Space shifted.
And a being walked out.
Long black hair, gentle, calm golden eyes, a ridiculously handsome face that had a light, playful smile.
And the instant he appeared, Ignira’s eyes brightened even further and—
"Father!"
She exclaimed excitedly and jumped towards him carelessly, an action she would otherwise never do.
And Nux—
His smile widened as he shifted further and caught his daughter.
"Did you have fun?"
He asked as he gently kissed her forehead and Ignira—
"I did!!"
She nodded with a big smile on her face.

Dagahra waved his hand.
"He wants us back."
Saphira spoke nonetheless.
"Bah!"
Dagahra, however, just scoffed.
"Let him call."
"Ember also sent word."
Saphira sighed lightly.
"We’ll go when this is over."
Dagahra shrugged.
"This isn’t important."
Dagahra looked down at the battlefield and...
"It is for her."
Below—
"Ignira continued.
"Center—collapse inward."
"CENTER—COLLAPSE INWARD!!"
The General copied the girl’s orders, the Ashen Tide’s soldiers surged.
The Ironclad Dominion tried to reform, but it was already too late, their formation was broken.
And the Ashen Tide could feel it.
Victory was close.
That was when Ignira stepped forward, her golden eyes moved rapidly as they scanned the entire battlefield again.
She knew that victory was close, but she also knew these were the exact moments when things went wrong, she had learned it the hard way, so she wasn’t going to let her guard down.
Not right now.
Not when she was so close.
So the little girl continued to expand her senses and then—
She froze as she sensed something.
Then, a big grin appeared on her face.
Above her, Saphira looked at Dagahra and chuckled.
"She felt him."
"...Of course she did."
Dagahra snorted.
He didn’t like this one bit.
However, Ignira below had already abandoned the battlefield.
"Hey!
Where are you goin—"
The General tried to call her but she just shrugged and—
"It’s a won war, what more do you need?
Take care of it yourself!"
The little girl answered, this was the most she had spoken ever since she appeared.
It was almost as if her entire personality had changed.
The General had no idea why this happened, but he couldn’t think too much, not when the war still wasn’t over.
"...There she goes."
Dagahra above sighed.
What General leaves her army like that?
"She’s still a child."
Saphira smiled faintly.
Far ahead—
Space shifted.
And a being walked out.
Long black hair, gentle, calm golden eyes, a ridiculously handsome face that had a light, playful smile.
And the instant he appeared, Ignira’s eyes brightened even further and—
"Father!"
She exclaimed excitedly and jumped towards him carelessly, an action she would otherwise never do.
And Nux—
His smile widened as he shifted further and caught his daughter.
"Did you have fun?"
He asked as he gently kissed her forehead and Ignira—
"I did!!"
She nodded with a big smile on her face.

chapters.title: Chapter 2318: You don’t look tired when you are in Nux’s be—ummffhh!!
paragraphs: "Did you have fun?"
Nux asked as he gently kissed her forehead and Ignira—
"I did!!"
She nodded with a big smile on her face.
Nux chuckled at that sight, then, his eyes fell on the two Dragon Progenitors, one of whom, had an annoyed look on his face.
"Why are you here?"
Dagahra questioned.
"Hmm? Isn’t it clear? To pick up my daughter."
Nux tilted his head in confusion before answering with a smile.
"She was busy."
Dagahra spoke directly and Nux sighed.
"Her side would have won."
"She doesn’t know that."
Dagahra spoke with that same, harsh tone and at this point, Nux had already made it so Ignira wouldn’t listen to their conversation.
"It doesn’t matter if she wins or not.
This is not about winning, it is about seeing it to the end. This is how she will learn, from experience. Which she couldn’t, since you appeared.
You knew the battle was over, you knew it wouldn’t have lasted more than a few hours, yet you came here, knowing that she would drop everything and rush to see you.
I hope you understand that what you are doing is hindering her growth."
The Dragon Progenitor spoke with a solemn look on his face and finally, Nux’s easy expression changed as well.
He looked right into the Dragon Progenitor’s eyes and—
"I announced the gathering a day ago.
You were the one who ignored that, took my daughter to another world and failed to bring her back on time despite my constant calls.
Do not pin this on me, Dagahra."
Nux spoke, his eyes now shining threateningly. It was a look that made the Dragon Progenitor gulp for a moment, but he didn’t back down.
"The gathering could have waited a few hours."
"Or you could have chosen not to take my daughter away after the announcement was made."
Nux countered.
"I did what was necessary for her growth."
"She is ten.
She has ample time to grow."
"She has ample time for family gatherings as well, it won’t matter if she skipped a few."
Dagahra snorted and this time—
Nux lost it.

"I don’t want to hear that from someone who didn’t even know who half of his children were back in his day. Gatherings may not be important for you, but they are for me. They allow me to spend time with all of my family together, you may not know how valuable that is, I do."
He spoke those words and Dagahra... he turned silent.
It was one of the things that hurt him the most, one of his greatest regrets.
A family.
Or lack of one.
As a Progenitor, it was his duty to populate Yrniel, he fathered hundreds of thousands of children but...
He could never be a proper father to any of them, this was also the reason he was trying so hard with Ignira and Nux’s other children.
But...
For Nux to point this out at this very moment... it felt... heavy.
Nux, however, did not care how it felt. He continued to stare at him and—

"I respect you as a warrior and the person you are, I am also glad for everything you do for my children, but that does not mean you are allowed to keep them away from me and try to tell me how I am hindering their growth when I come to meet them.
They are MY children, she is MY daughter, I may not be the best father in the Universe, I may not understand what is best for her and her growth—
But I damn well know that me spending time with her won’t affect anything.

My daughter isn’t a machine who is supposed to train in the most optimal way, she is a child, I send her with you because she likes your training, she likes commanding armies, if she is learning something from them, that’s good.
But learning and getting stronger isn’t the priority, the priority is her enjoying what she does.
So if she abandons your so-called training and rushes towards her father like a child should—
You are no one to stop her."
He spoke and then, he stepped closer, appearing right in front of the Dragon Progenitor and—
"I hope that is clear."

Then, Nux walked past him and the instant he did, the frosty look on his face disappeared and Ignira, who was frozen all this while, suddenly returned to her senses and rubbed her face on her father’s chest, not noticing the tense environment around her at all.
"Father, did you see what I did? Hehe~ I made them win~"
"Of course I did, I even recorded my brave daughter, we will watch it with mother later, how about it?"
"Yes! Mother needs to see it as well! I will become even better than her!"
Ignira clenched her fists, her golden eyes shining brightly.
"Even better than your mother, huh? That won’t be easy."

Nux commented, even he wasn’t sure if he would be a better general than Ember, her Law was one thing, he had that power as well, just her understanding of army tactics and everything was... quite thorough.
And even though Nux’s vast knowledge probably outshined all of Ember’s, he still felt like Ember was better than him when it came to commanding armies.
"Just you wait! I’ll do it!"
Ignira, however, didn’t care. She was roaring to surpass her mother.
"Alright then, I’ll root for you."
Nux chuckled.
"You will?"
Ignira asked.
"Of course, who else will I root for?"
"Hmph! You always root for mother!"
The girl pouted.
"You two also sneak inside the room without telling me!"
She complained again and Nux...
He had no clue how to react to that.
Should he just freeze this little one when he is with her mother?
"Hmph! Hmph!"
The girl pouted even harder and Nux laughed,
"Alright alright, this time, I will root for you, okay?"
"Hmph!"
"Nira..."
Nux had no clue how to make amends with his daughter.

The strongest being in this Universe, a being who had challenged four beings, who had ruled another Universe for trillions of years, beings who were far stronger than him, without an inch of fear or uncertainty—
Was now standing in front of this little thing, constantly thinking about what to say to please her and not offend her any further.
Back in Umbrasol, the grand palace where the ’Royal Family’ stayed, a place that was usually calm and peaceful, was now a mess.
One by one, all of the children and their mothers had come for the gathering.
The first ones were Lane, Rune and Thyra, it was rare to see Lane together with the other two, at least it was ten years ago but... the children had changed that.
Their daughters, Nyx, Sable and Kira, were especially close. All three of them did not speak many words and it formed a sense of camaraderie around them. The three were together, even right now.

Then came Vyriana, Astaria, Ember and Lavinia, these four were together since the beginning, and that didn’t change with their children, since all of them, Zyrax, Ragnar, Drakar and Frostra were quite close to each other.
"Hm? Where is Ignira?"
Drakar frowned when he couldn’t find his sister.
Ember smiled at that.
"She will be here soon."
"Who is she with?"
Drakar didn’t understand.
Ignira was part of their group, she should be with them, no?
"Don’t you know? Grandpa Dagahra took her to train."
Zyrax answered with his hands behind his head.
"He hasn’t brought her back yet?"
Drakar frowned.
"It’s Grandpa Dagahra, what do you think?"
Ragnar commented and Drakar couldn’t say anything to that. Frostra, like her mother, stayed silent, just observing her siblings.
After them came another group—
Melia, Riona, Amaya, Aeliana, Eisheth and Allura...

An extremely strange group, one that almost no one would have been able to predict, but as surprising as it sounds, or actually not very surprising, their children, Noctis, Caelum, Orion, Samael, Seraphyne, and Azarion were quite close.
After all, all these children had somewhat similar personalities, all of them commanded control, just... in their own... unique way.
Then came Skyla, Edda and Aisha, Skyla’s son, Kaelion, was close to Edda’s son Veyron and Edda’s daughter Selene was very close to Aisha’s Velora.
How could they not?
The two girls were essentially the same, one used illusions to trick others, the other used her charm to make couples fight each other.
"See? I told you we came early, they haven’t even begun lunch."
Kaelion complained as he glanced at Veyron. Veyron looked at him and sighed—
"I did not have the energy to continue chasing you around, you exhaust me."
"Oh come on! It was fun!"
Kaelion raised his voice, Veyron however, just placed a finger on his ear and—
"Keep it low, will you?"
He spoke with a yawn and Edda, who watched her son from behind, just sighed—
"How did this one turn out so lazy?"
She then turned towards her sister and—
"Do you two think I am lazy?"
That was when a perverted smile appeared on Aisha’s face and—
"You don’t look tired when you are in Nux’s be—ummffhh!!"
Before she could even complete her words, someone grabbed her mouth from behind.

chapters.title: Chapter 2319: Go greet your grandma, you little thing.
paragraphs: "Do you two think I am lazy?"
That was when a perverted smile appeared on Aisha’s face and—
"You don’t look tired when you are in Nux’s be—ummffhh!!"
Before she could even complete her words, someone grabbed her mouth from behind. The children and the women turned around and their eyes fell on another woman.
Felberta.
She was holding Aisha’s mouth and—
"You still haven’t learned to control your mouth around children, have you, Aisha?"
She asked with a gentle smile that did not look gentle at all. Aisha, hearing her voice, suddenly froze, the children laughed at that.
And that was when two more children walked in behind Felberta.
Aurelios and Lysera, the creation twins.
The two siblings were quite close to each other and while they interacted with every child in the family, they usually kept to themselves so they weren’t part of any group.
Then came Evane, together with her daughter Eloria.
But Eloria wasn’t alone, she was with Mira, Skyla’s daughter, the daughter who had decided to abandon her mother today and stick with Mother Evane because she gave her a candy.

Both Eloria and Mira weren’t in any particular groups, they were... the heart of the family. Every single group accepted them readily, even those who do not talk usually open their mouths when they are around them.
"Father still isn’t here..."
Mira pouted as she looked around while holding Evane’s hand.
"He will be, don’t worry."
Evane chuckled as she looked at her.
"Where is he?"

Eloria asked, she too, was holding Evane’s hand like Mira, or more accurately, Evane was holding the two sisters because she knew the moment she let them go, they would disappear and start running around.
"He is not in Umbrasol."
Evane answered and Eloria just nodded.
"So he called his children here and moved away, huh? How irresponsible of him."
Then, another voice was heard, everyone turned towards its source and the instant they did—
"Grandma!"
Mira exclaimed excitedly, then she forcefully released her hand from Evane’s hold and rushed towards Faustina, who had a big smile on her face as she held her and picked her up.
"Mira~"
She called out.
"Hehe~"

Mira laughed as well, Faustina, like always, took out a candy and gave it to her. Then, as she looked around, she noticed Eloria was already standing beside her, waiting for her candy, one by one, other children came as well.
All of them gathered around Faustina.
Behind Faustina, the rest of the Progenitors came as well, but it was clear that the children liked Faustina the most and grouped around her.

The Progenitors just sighed, they too, wanted to hang around with the other children, and they were quite close with some of them, but they couldn’t compare to Faustina, who had never once taken a rest in this past year and had always stayed together with one of the children.
A few seconds later, another woman walked in.
It was Sharnoth, and while Sharnoth, in these years, had gotten quite close to the rest of the women, the same couldn’t be said for her son Kaelith.
Kaelith was... a complete outcast.
Mostly because of his split personality that he has no control over like Sharnoth does. Other children, though they do not show it, do feel a sense of strangeness around him.

Only Azarion, Mira and Eloria could actually talk to Kaelith without feeling anything, but even then, Kaelith himself wasn’t particularly close to any of the other children to be in a group with them.

It was something Sharnoth did not like, she wanted her child to have friends as well, her sisters were the same too, they too, wanted their children to get along with Kaelith, but children were just... children.
It was difficult to make them do something they did not want.
In the end, the only choice was to let time heal everything, wait for the children to grow an understanding and finally get close to little Kaelith.
The exact opposite to Kaelith was... Nihyron.
Shadow’s son.
Like Kaelith, he was a loner too, but he was a loner by choice.
He just did not interact with people around him, even Azarion, who could practically get even a rock talking, had a difficult time conversing with him.
And because of that—
Slap
"Go greet your grandma, you little thing."
Shadow slapped Nihyron’s head when he just stood there and watched all the children surround his grandmother.
Nihyron rubbed his head and looked at his mother with a frown,
"I will once they all move away."

Shadow just looked at her child with a frustrated look on her face. Honestly, she wanted to hit this arrogant little thing a little more to set him straight but just then, as if she sensed something, she stopped and turned in a particular direction with a smile on her face.
"He’s here."
The instant she said those words, every single person present, even Nihyron, turned in the direction she was looking at, and just as Shadow said—
The space trembled and a being stepped out with a little girl in his hands.
It was Nux.
"FATHER!!"
And the moment he arrived—
It was chaos.
Every child rushed towards him, even Kaelith and Nihyron, who usually hated following others. The women pouted at that scene—
This was... their right.

They were the ones who used to rush to him like that, but of course, they couldn’t possibly act like this in front of children, this was also the reason they let the children roam around Umbrasol as much as they wanted, so they could spend some time with Nux in private.
As for the children, they surrounded Nux the next instant.
Clearly, Nux was the favorite.
And how couldn’t he be?
He was the sucker for his children.
You wanted candies? He would create them from thin air.
You wanted to spar? He would do it with a grin.
He would teach you concepts in a way that would never be boring, he would play with you till you exhausted yourself, he would create anything you wanted.

Plus, with all his bloodlines, especially his Incubus and other similar blood, his charm was off the charts, charm that even worked on children and made his presence more... light, gentle for them. Like a loving, caring father’s.
"So this is where you were!"
Drakar complained when he saw Ignira in Nux’s hands. Ignira grinned,
"Father came to pick me up. Hehe~"
She giggled, looking at Drakar and the other children with a sense of superiority. Ragnar frowned,
"I should have gone to train as well."
He spoke as he looked at his mother, who stopped him from training because of the gathering.
Nyx, at this point, had already climbed on top of her father and was currently resting on his shoulders, her usual position.
"Father! Pick me too!"
Mira exclaimed.
"Me too!"
"Me too!"
Other children raised their voices as well. Even Nihyron had raised his hands, waiting for his father to notice him.
And Nux...
He just looked at his children with a smile, then, as his grin widened—
"Alright, I’ll pick you all."
He spoke as he activated the Giant’s blood that was now in his system and his body became larger.
He didn’t make it comically large, his Giant blood gave him the power to control his size, he only made it so all his children could be with him.
Then, he looked at the gathering table, where food was being served, and his chair that would no longer fit it.
"Hmmm. What do we do now?"
He asked.
"I’ll take care of it!"
Lysera laughed, she used the opportunity to jump down, rush towards her father’s chair and the instant she touched it—
The chair began to... evolve.
Into something that would not only fit her father, but also make sure others at the gathering table (their mothers), weren’t affected by Father’s size.
"Done!"
She raised her head with a smile.
Nux chuckled,
"That was creative."
He chuckled as he saw what Lysera had turned it into.
The chair melted softly, like it had turned into living material.
The legs didn’t just extend—they split into multiple layered supports, forming a stable base that adjusted itself against the ground automatically.
The backrest widened, then curved, shaping itself perfectly to Nux’s larger form.
But the strangest part—
The table didn’t need to change.
At first, it looked... wrong.
Nux’s body had grown larger, yet the table in front of him remained the same size as before. By all logic, it should have felt too small, too low—
But it didn’t.
When he sat down, everything aligned perfectly.
His arms rested naturally on the table.
The distance, the height, the space—
It all felt... correct.
Around him, his wives sat as they always did, completely unaffected. To them, nothing seemed like it had changed.
The table was still normal.
The space was still the same.
Lysera hadn’t made the chair bigger.
She had changed how the chair interacted with the world.
The moment Nux touched it, the chair adapted, not to his size, but to his very perspective. It created a shift that only affected how things connected to him.
To Nux, the world adjusted.
To everyone else, it stayed exactly as it was.
This was Lysera’s power of Evolution.
"Hehe~"
Lysera laughed.
Nux ruffled her hair with a proud look on his face as finally, he and everyone else began settling down at the dining table.

And that was when two more children walked in behind Felberta.
Aurelios and Lysera, the creation twins.
The two siblings were quite close to each other and while they interacted with every child in the family, they usually kept to themselves so they weren’t part of any group.
Then came Evane, together with her daughter Eloria.
But Eloria wasn’t alone, she was with Mira, Skyla’s daughter, the daughter who had decided to abandon her mother today and stick with Mother Evane because she gave her a candy.
Both Eloria and Mira weren’t in any particular groups, they were... the heart of the family.
Every single group accepted them readily, even those who do not talk usually open their mouths when they are around them.
"Father still isn’t here..."
Mira pouted as she looked around while holding Evane’s hand.
"He will be, don’t worry."
Evane chuckled as she looked at her.
"Where is he?"

Eloria asked, she too, was holding Evane’s hand like Mira, or more accurately, Evane was holding the two sisters because she knew the moment she let them go, they would disappear and start running around.
"He is not in Umbrasol."
Evane answered and Eloria just nodded.
"So he called his children here and moved away, huh?
How irresponsible of him."
Then, another voice was heard, everyone turned towards its source and the instant they did—
"Grandma!"
Mira exclaimed excitedly, then she forcefully released her hand from Evane’s hold and rushed towards Faustina, who had a big smile on her face as she held her and picked her up.
"Mira~"
She called out.
"Hehe~"
Mira laughed as well, Faustina, like always, took out a candy and gave it to her.
Then, as she looked around, she noticed Eloria was already standing beside her, waiting for her candy, one by one, other children came as well.
All of them gathered around Faustina.
Behind Faustina, the rest of the Progenitors came as well, but it was clear that the children liked Faustina the most and grouped around her.

The Progenitors just sighed, they too, wanted to hang around with the other children, and they were quite close with some of them, but they couldn’t compare to Faustina, who had never once taken a rest in this past year and had always stayed together with one of the children.
A few seconds later, another woman walked in.
It was Sharnoth, and while Sharnoth, in these years, had gotten quite close to the rest of the women, the same couldn’t be said for her son Kaelith.
Kaelith was... a complete outcast.
Mostly because of his split personality that he has no control over like Sharnoth does.
Other children, though they do not show it, do feel a sense of strangeness around him.

Only Azarion, Mira and Eloria could actually talk to Kaelith without feeling anything, but even then, Kaelith himself wasn’t particularly close to any of the other children to be in a group with them.

It was something Sharnoth did not like, she wanted her child to have friends as well, her sisters were the same too, they too, wanted their children to get along with Kaelith, but children were just... children.
It was difficult to make them do something they did not want.
In the end, the only choice was to let time heal everything, wait for the children to grow an understanding and finally get close to little Kaelith.
The exact opposite to Kaelith was...
Nihyron.
Shadow’s son.
Like Kaelith, he was a loner too, but he was a loner by choice.
He just did not interact with people around him, even Azarion, who could practically get even a rock talking, had a difficult time conversing with him.
And because of that—
Slap
"Go greet your grandma, you little thing."
Shadow slapped Nihyron’s head when he just stood there and watched all the children surround his grandmother.
Nihyron rubbed his head and looked at his mother with a frown,
"I will once they all move away."
Shadow just looked at her child with a frustrated look on her face.

Honestly, she wanted to hit this arrogant little thing a little more to set him straight but just then, as if she sensed something, she stopped and turned in a particular direction with a smile on her face.
"He’s here."
The instant she said those words, every single person present, even Nihyron, turned in the direction she was looking at, and just as Shadow said—
The space trembled and a being stepped out with a little girl in his hands.
It was Nux.
"FATHER!!"
And the moment he arrived—
It was chaos.
Every child rushed towards him, even Kaelith and Nihyron, who usually hated following others.
The women pouted at that scene—
This was... their right.

They were the ones who used to rush to him like that, but of course, they couldn’t possibly act like this in front of children, this was also the reason they let the children roam around Umbrasol as much as they wanted, so they could spend some time with Nux in private.
As for the children, they surrounded Nux the next instant.
Clearly, Nux was the favorite.
And how couldn’t he be?
He was the sucker for his children.
You wanted candies?
He would create them from thin air.
You wanted to spar?
He would do it with a grin.
He would teach you concepts in a way that would never be boring, he would play with you till you exhausted yourself, he would create anything you wanted.
Plus, with all his bloodlines, especially his Incubus and other similar blood, his charm was off the charts, charm that even worked on children and made his presence more... light, gentle for them.
Like a loving, caring father’s.
"So this is where you were!"
Drakar complained when he saw Ignira in Nux’s hands.
Ignira grinned,
"Father came to pick me up.
Hehe~"
She giggled, looking at Drakar and the other children with a sense of superiority.
Ragnar frowned,
"I should have gone to train as well."
He spoke as he looked at his mother, who stopped him from training because of the gathering.
Nyx, at this point, had already climbed on top of her father and was currently resting on his shoulders, her usual position.
"Father!
Pick me too!"
Mira exclaimed.
"Me too!"
"Me too!"
Other children raised their voices as well.
Even Nihyron had raised his hands, waiting for his father to notice him.
And Nux...
He just looked at his children with a smile, then, as his grin widened—
"Alright, I’ll pick you all."
He spoke as he activated the Giant’s blood that was now in his system and his body became larger.
He didn’t make it comically large, his Giant blood gave him the power to control his size, he only made it so all his children could be with him.
Then, he looked at the gathering table, where food was being served, and his chair that would no longer fit it.
"Hmmm.
What do we do now?"
He asked.
"I’ll take care of it!"
Lysera laughed, she used the opportunity to jump down, rush towards her father’s chair and the instant she touched it—
The chair began to... evolve.
Into something that would not only fit her father, but also make sure others at the gathering table (their mothers), weren’t affected by Father’s size.
"Done!"
She raised her head with a smile.
Nux chuckled,
"That was creative."
He chuckled as he saw what Lysera had turned it into.
The chair melted softly, like it had turned into living material.
The legs didn’t just extend—they split into multiple layered supports, forming a stable base that adjusted itself against the ground automatically.
The backrest widened, then curved, shaping itself perfectly to Nux’s larger form.
But the strangest part—
The table didn’t need to change.
At first, it looked... wrong.
Nux’s body had grown larger, yet the table in front of him remained the same size as before.
By all logic, it should have felt too small, too low—
But it didn’t.
When he sat down, everything aligned perfectly.
His arms rested naturally on the table.
The distance, the height, the space—
It all felt... correct.
Around him, his wives sat as they always did, completely unaffected.
To them, nothing seemed like it had changed.
The table was still normal.
The space was still the same.
Lysera hadn’t made the chair bigger.
She had changed how the chair interacted with the world.
The moment Nux touched it, the chair adapted, not to his size, but to his very perspective.
It created a shift that only affected how things connected to him.
To Nux, the world adjusted.
To everyone else, it stayed exactly as it was.
This was Lysera’s power of Evolution.
"Hehe~"
Lysera laughed.
Nux ruffled her hair with a proud look on his face as finally, he and everyone else began settling down at the dining table.

chapters.title: Chapter 2320: The lively atmosphere in the Meeting Hall... disappeared.
paragraphs: The mood at the dining table was cheerful and lively, the children stayed with their father, that allowed the women to return to their usual groups.
The entire hall was filled with soft noise, plates shifting, quiet laughter, and small conversations between different groups.
The long table, despite its size, didn’t feel distant.
It felt... alive.

All the children sat either on his lap or on his shoulders. Nyx sat on top of his head, the little girl was usually silent and almost always gave in to whatever, but this was one thing she never gave up on, no matter what.
This was her spot.

Selene sat on his shoulder, swung her legs lightly as she ate from his plate without asking. Mira leaned against him, happily chewing on something sweet, while whispering something into his ear with giggles, Nux reacted to every single thing she said.
Kira sat properly on his lap, chewing her food silently.
Noctis sat nearby with a straight posture. He ate slowly, calmly, his gaze occasionally shifting toward the others. Drakar and Zyrax were still arguing.
"I told you, that last strike wasn’t enough."
"It was enough."
"It wasn’t."
"It was."
Ragnar leaned forward, being with his father was the only time he didn’t have his sword in his hand, or at least around him.
"You both wasted that fight,"
He said.
"Next time, don’t stop."
Frostra sat beside him.
"You say that now, but you won’t be the one fixing what breaks."
Ragnar shrugged.
"Then don’t let it break."
"You will break it 87% of the time."
Orion, who was sitting a little further away from them, commented without looking at them.
"...you’re annoying."
"I am correct."
"Are you saying Brother Ragnar is wrong? Does that mean you are stronger than him?"
Velora asked as she looked at Orion with an amused look. The moment Ragnar heard those words, he reacted—
"Huh? What makes you think you are stronger than me?"
He was ready for a fight, but—
Seraphyne gently placed a hand on Velora’s shoulder and—
"That’s enough."
She spoke in a soft tone.
Orion too, looked at Ragnar,
"You know she is trying to make us fight.
Not here."
Ragnar turned silent too.
Caelum sat quietly, Eloria listened to others curiously, at the same time, she picked food and fed her father with a bright, excited smile. An offer Nux just couldn’t refuse.
Sable rested on her father’s lap, this was one of the few places where she completely let her guard down around, that made her lazy.
Azarion, knowing she wouldn’t eat like this, fed his little sister, Sable, trusting him, continued to get pampered.
The other children mostly kept to themselves, but they interacted with Nux in their own way. Some just liked being around him, some were showing him what they learned and how good they had gotten.

The women too, were talking amongst themselves, each sharing everything their children did. The Progenitors did the same, with the children present, they were all these people talked about. Of course, some Progenitors were just fighting, especially Dagahra, who was now being questioned about why he took Ignira away and didn’t bring her back.
It was lively, comfortably lively.
Until...
Caesar, who was sitting on his chair, observing everything silently, until finally, he took another bite of the food they were served and—
"Nux."
He called out.
The conversations didn’t stop instantly, but they indeed slowed down, some of the children stopped too.
Caesar knew this would be the best attention he would get, plus, Nux was already staring at him, so the rest didn’t matter. He directly asked the question he wanted to ask.
"Why did you call all of us here?"
And the instant he asked that question, in an instant—
The entire hall turned silent.
This was something everyone wanted to know.
Nux didn’t answer immediately, he observed everyone present, his children, his wives, and the Progenitors and then—
The warmth in his expression faded slightly, a change even Mira noticed instantly.
"Father...?"
She called out, slightly worried.
Zyrax, Drakar, Ignira, Frostra, and Ragnar instantly recognized that look, it was the one he had when he sparred against them.
Nux straightened his posture and finally—
"From now on..."
He began.
"...I will be locking this Universe.
No one will leave."
He spoke with a solemn look on his face, his eyes glanced at everyone, until they stopped on one particular woman.
Aeliana.
Aeliana was one of the women who left the Universe the most, especially after Samael.
Samael was... Azriel’s grandson and Azriel, because of everything he had been through, was extremely doting on him.
This was also the reason he called Samael time and time again and Aeliana, using these chances, left to meet her father as well.
But right now...
As Aeliana looked at Nux’s expression, she understood what he was saying.
She wasn’t supposed to leave either.
"What happened...?"
She asked with a serious look on her face.
She had known Nux for a long time, she knew he wouldn’t stop her without any reason. If he was stopping them—
Then something must have happened.
Something serious.
It wasn’t just her, the rest of the women understood that too. Even the children sensed something was wrong.
They all looked at Nux and Nux...
"The War between Light and Darkness is over."
He announced with a serious look on his face and—
"What!?"
"What are you talking about!?"
"Over!?"
The reactions were instantaneous.
The last thing they knew, the War was only getting more heated. Many worlds had perished, both sides had taken strong hits and the anger was boiling.
This obviously wasn’t the peak of the War, but the tensions were rising and they were rising at a strong rate.
The War shouldn’t stop...
Not right now.
There was no reason for it to stop.
But...
"It is over."
Nux spoke with a grim look on his face.
And that was when Amaya noticed something—
She asked.
Nux looked at her and she explained.
"What else? You wouldn’t look this tense just because the War is over."
The Devourer questioned.
Yes, the War was important for Nux. Because of the chaos it caused, it made it easier for him to devour the worlds, so much so that at this point, Nux doesn’t even go and devour worlds himself.
He just... sends a hunting party.

The Dragon trick was great to induce fear, but in the end, Nux knew it had its limit, for the first few times, it wouldn’t make a difference, but if the same creature continued to attack again and again, even the Infinities would have no choice but to attack it.
They would not stand still and let it do whatever it pleased, it was a matter of pride.
So Nux created these... hunting parties.

All these parties had one of his clones capable of connecting the world they were attacking to him, once the connection was made, it allowed Nux to devour those particular worlds, without leaving his Universe.
But...
"Last five hunting parties have disappeared and the last thing my clones saw was one of the Infinities attacking them."
Nux revealed.
"What...?"
And the women widened their eyes in shock.
"But that... shouldn’t be possible..."
Amaya frowned.
"The hunting parties are now as efficient as you were..."
She muttered.
And it was true.

While only ten years had passed in Nux’s Universe, about a hundred had passed in the Main Universe, and in these hundred years, Nux has constantly been sending hunting parties and training them to be more and more efficient.
At this point, they had reached a level that was similar to his own.

Yes, like how Nux, while he was targeting Light Worlds, was so quick that by the time Seraphielle learned one of her worlds was being attacked, it was already over and Nux had disappeared together with the world.

This was the reason Seraphielle couldn’t stop Nux, this was the reason the entire ordeal had become so complicated for Light that it had no choice but to push far to cause a distraction for its people.
The hunting parties had reached that level of efficiency as well.

Nux had devoured more than fifty High Level Worlds, all those Eternals that ruled those worlds were at his complete disposal, some of these Eternals also had Absolute Laws, not to mention Nux had devoured a good number of Light-born Eternals, heck, he even had the Strongest Child of Light at his disposal.
Nux’s army was strong.

Ridiculously strong, they were capable of leveling any world that is not a Supreme World almost instantly, with this army subduing the world’s forces, together with his clone, that had learned to form a connection between his main body and the world they were in, devouring a world had become an instantaneous activity.
Stopping it had become impossible.
Unless...
Unless the enemy already knew they were coming.

Which should have been impossible as well, because just like Nux, his hunting party has no connection to the Main Universe, no being should be able to sense their presence, not unless they attack first.
But the fact that the hunting parties have disappeared, that too, five times, each one being intercepted by an Infinity—
It meant...
"Yes, the Infinities have figured out a way to know what world we are targeting and they are now actively moving to stop us."
Nux spoke, and the instant he confirmed what the women were thinking—
The lively atmosphere in the Meeting Hall... disappeared.

chapters.title: Chapter 2321: Could it be... him?
paragraphs: "Yes, the Infinities have figured out a way to know what world we are targeting and they are now actively moving to stop us."
Nux spoke, and the instant he confirmed what the women were thinking—
The lively atmosphere in the Meeting Hall... disappeared.
Of course, the children couldn’t hear any of it, Nux had put all of them to sleep as the conversation began without them knowing or understanding what had happened.
They just knew that their father, for some reason, had sealed the Universe and they were no longer supposed to leave, and then... they fell asleep.
Nihyron tried to fight it, he had sensed his father had done something, so just to challenge him, he tried to resist.
But he was far too young for him to be challenging Nux in this manner, so he too, couldn’t hold out.
"They... figured out a way...?"
Aeliana spoke with a solemn look on her face.
Riona asked.
Amaya, however, shook her head.
"That isn’t important, at least not right now."
And she was correct.
"We first need to understand how much they know.
To what extent can they sense our movements, we need to... experiment."
The Devourer spoke and Nux nodded at her words.

"These past five times, every time our hunting party entered that world, one of the four Infinities was waiting for them. The rest of the party was crushed the moment it entered and my clones were captured.
Of course, I ended all the connections I had with it, so the only thing they had in their hands was a powerless puppet that has no memories or abilities.
They wouldn’t find anything with it."
"But they are still capturing your clones."
Thyra pointed out.
"Yes."
Nux nodded.
"That means they still do not completely understand everything. They are still looking for answers."
"Or they just simply want to capture you."
Vyriana commented.
And honestly—
Nux did not have an answer.

All this time, he had been playing the Infinities exactly like he wanted to, of course, there were some moments of uncertainty, but overall, all his plans worked as he intended them to, the Infinities moved like he expected them to, fell for his traps like he expected them to—
It had been a smooth-sailing ride this entire time.
But for the first time in a long, long while, Nux was... answerless.
What the Infinities had done was completely out of his expectation, something he couldn’t have any possible answers to.
Questions like, how did they find a way?

Did they know how to stop him all this while? If that was true, why move now? Why not move earlier? After all, the only reason Nux survived was because he was fast and by the time the Infinities knew he had attacked, it was over.
But... if any of the Infinities had been waiting for him to attack and had attacked him the moment he arrived—
Nux didn’t think his chances of making it back from that situation were high, not back then, when he had barely devoured a few High Level Worlds.
Heck, even now, even when he had devoured more than a thousand High Level Worlds using the War to his advantage and was now much, much stronger than he was in the past—
He still wasn’t sure he could take on an Infinity.
Or maybe they didn’t have a way before and only figured something out now?
Even if that was true, the question was the same.
Figured out what exactly?
How did they do it? Was it because he made a mistake he didn’t notice?
There were too many questions and absolutely no answers.
"Is there something else that we know...?"
Sharnoth, keeping her calm, asked another question.
Nux looked at her and nodded.
"We do."
He spoke as he looked at Aeliana, the Vampire frowned in confusion and Nux—
"They are trying to reach Father-in-law."
"The Infinities...?"
Aeliana asked and Nux nodded again.
"Yes, last time Father-in-law contacted them, he left the artifact to reach him with them. They contacted him through it."
"What did they say?"
Aeliana asked.
"They said they wish to meet him."

Amaya muttered with a deep frown.

Nux nodded again.

Aeliana completed those words.

Lyriana nodded as well.

Eisheth muttered with a heavy expression.

"But how did the Infinities figure out a way to stop Nux’s hunts just because Zylarith contacted them?"
Lyriana questioned with a confused look on her face.
Zylarith knew about them, sure, but that still shouldn’t have helped the Infinities figure out a way to stop them.
"Could it be a coincidence?"
Rune asked.
That could be true as well, in fact, that seemed more likely, but...
"No."
Sharnoth shook her head.
"If Master made a move, he would have made it after full preparations.
He must have planned it all."

Compared to everyone here, she knew Zylarith the most, she knew how thorough that man was. He would be as thorough as Nux, if not more, this was the reason Sharnoth, at some level, believed Zylarith was actually Nux’s Soul Father, even though the rest of the women felt that it was bogus.
"Are you saying that... Zylarith figured out a way to stop Nux’s hunts? Something that none of the Infinities, not even the Infinity of Eternity could?"
Felberta narrowed her eyes as she looked at Sharnoth and—
"That is correct."
Sharnoth nodded.
If it was Zylarith, he was definitely capable of it.
"How did he do that?"
Felberta asked.
"I wouldn’t know."
Sharnoth could only shake her head and the women turned silent.
The Progenitors too, ever since the conversation began, remained completely silent, not once did they try to interrupt because they had no valuable input regarding the situation.
"Could there be... a traitor among us?"
Suddenly, Rune asked another question.
Of course, when she mentioned a traitor, everyone knew she wasn’t talking about the wives, that was simply impossible, Nux wouldn’t even consider that—
But that didn’t mean...
The Progenitors were excluded from suspicion.
The Progenitors realized what everyone at the table was thinking as well, especially when Rune was making no effort to hide it as she stared at them with her piercing green eyes.
But then—
"Search our memories."
Faustina spoke directly.
"Faus!"
One of the Beastkin Progenitors raised his voice, Faustina, however, shook her head.
"It happened after we returned and started living here permanently, even I would be suspicious."
The moment she said those words, silence lingered in the hall. Faustina, on the other hand, looked at Nux and nodded—

"I never doubted you, Mother."
Nux shook his head.
"I know.
This is the reason I wish to prove that you were right to put your trust in me.
Do it, read my memories."
She spoke but then—
"There is no point."
Amaya shook her head.
"If there is indeed a traitor, the Infinities would make sure he or she wouldn’t be caught.
We cannot possibly fight them in that regard, things they know are far more advanced than what we do, we wouldn’t be able to catch their tricks."
"Then what else can we do?"
Rune asked and Amaya looked at her with the same serious look and—
"As I said before—
We run experiments."
