chapters.title: Chapter 2337: Do not take that lightly.
paragraphs: "We were... fortunate..."
Felberta spoke with a solemn look on her face when she saw the recording on the screen hovering in front of her. The rest of the people around her nodded.
The gathering was over and everything changed in an instant. Nux’s Universe was now completely sealed.
In these past ten years, Nux had created hunting parties, these parties, however, were different from the normal ’puppets’ Nux used.
Nux didn’t erase their memories and turn them into loyal subordinates, at least not now. The first few hunting parties were indeed formed using such puppets, but later, Nux noticed another thing.
Leaving the Universe, attacking another world and devouring it...
It was... fun.
It was something people who had been suppressed by Supreme Rules craved.
So he did something else.

A new system was created, a guild system, a system that gave ’missions’ to people, it was like Mercenary Worlds, and one of these Missions was to take Nux’s clone, leave the Universe and devour the outside world.
Of course, such missions were only assigned to the best of the mercenaries, these were like S rank missions where failure wasn’t an option and very quickly, the system was a success.
More and more ’mercenaries’ joined, and the exceptional ones were allowed to go outside and devour the worlds, of their own free will.
But now...
That changed.
Some of these hunting parties had... failed.

Which in itself was strange considering every time they attacked, they went with way extra firepower, sometimes, literal Eternals would go target Middle Level Worlds, or a High Level World would be attacked by hundreds of Eternals.
So when the first hunting party had failed, Nux was informed the next instant, but at that moment—
Four other Parties had already left the Universe for their hunts and...
They had all failed as well.
This was the reason Nux called the gathering so urgently and now, no being could leave the Universe, to do, not just devouring, but any mission in general.
Now, Nux had taken the control back, he was the one who decided who would leave and who would not.
His puppets, that had been put into a half-asleep state since they were no longer being used, were now awake again.
"We were indeed."
Amaya nodded, she had a solemn look on her face as well.
"You wouldn’t have survived that."
Aeliana nodded.
"We don’t know that."
Nux answered, seemingly confident but then—
[Don’t be foolish.]
A strict voice was heard.
It was Azriel.

Yes, the gathering was over, the children were put to sleep, the Progenitors were sent away since Nux only wanted it to remain between him and his wives, but later during the conversation, Azriel contacted them and since then, he had been a part of their discussion.
[You wouldn’t be able to defeat them.]
Azriel shook his head and spoke with this odd sense of confidence.

What they were currently watching was the recording of the first time the Infinities attacked the party and from the recording, from the look in the Infinities’ eyes as they pounced on Nux’s clone, how quickly they all used their domains to stop him from leaving, the shine in their eyes when they reached Nux—
It made one thing very clear.
They didn’t know it was merely a hunting party, according to them, it was the Anomaly.

Nux didn’t know what their reaction was when they later found out since the recording didn’t last that long, but he could guess they were highly disappointed, and that was confirmed when they saw the second recording.
The time when they attacked the second party, this time, although they made the move just as quickly as before, as if Nux was actually there, this time—
Their eyes were... less excited.
As if somewhere in their mind, they knew they might fail.
As for the last two attacks?
There weren’t even all four Infinities who attacked their party, it was just... one Infinity, almost as if they knew this time would be a fail as well.
Their disappointment was clear.
So what the girls were saying was that Nux was lucky he wasn’t the one devouring when they first attacked because if it was him—
He would have to face all four Infinities at the same time and...
It wouldn’t be a battle he could have won.
"I am stronger than you think."
Nux countered, looking at Azriel, the Vampire Progenitor, however, shook his head.
[You are stronger than what I believe, I know that.
But the Infinities are... much stronger than you believe.
Your mind cannot comprehend what existence an Infinity truly is.]
"And you think you can comprehend what an entirely different Universe is?"
Nux tilted his head.
This wasn’t arrogance.
Nux wasn’t planning on going and challenging the Four Infinities, what he was saying was a simple statement.
Yes, he didn’t understand an Infinity’s existence, that was true, none of the memories he had seen from all the worlds he had devoured showed it—
But at the same time—
Azriel didn’t exactly know what sort of existence he was either.
Nux was... strong.
He was genuinely strong.
But—
[A new Universe.]
Azriel corrected.
[It hasn’t been a long time since you have become... whatever it is you have become.
You are young.
I am not saying you don’t have the potential to defeat them but...
These are beings that have existed for eons.
Do not take that lightly.]
Azriel warned.
Nux wanted to say something, anything to take his stand but in the end, he too, knew it was a pointless discussion.
There would never be a concrete answer to this discussion, not until he and the Four Infinities actually faced each other—
Which, he had no intention of doing unless he was absolutely sure of his victory.
After all, as much as Nux craved a genuine battle, now it wasn’t just his wives he had to live for—
Now he had his children too.
Nux couldn’t possibly leave this cruel world without a father to protect them—
His children would always grow safely, no matter what it took.
"I won’t take them lightly."
So in the end, Nux just nodded and didn’t continue further.
This wasn’t why they had gathered here in the first place, they had better, far more important things to do.
They had already begun their ’experiments’ like Amaya had told them to and... they had quite a few... interesting observations.
"Anyways, let’s see what we have so far, shall we?"
Nux asked as he looked around, Azriel dropped the matter too. He had seen Nux grow, he knew he wouldn’t put his and his family’s lives at stake just to prove a point.
He was not that foolish.
So the Vampire Progenitor too, turned towards the rest of the women, to take part in the conversation.
"Till now, we have sent ten more ’hunting parties’ to devour more worlds."
And Amaya began, taking control over the conversation, the rest of the people nodded, they already knew that.
"A few things we are sure of, is that there is no traitor in our Universe, every being in our Universe knew about the hunting parties, the Infinities did not, that alone breaks that possibility."
Again, the people nodded, that was logical too.
"Now the question is how did the Infinities know we were coming.
We do not know.
We have no answer for this question, neither are we able to find an answer to this question, not with what information we have so far.
So...
Let’s change the question to something we can answer or... find the answer to—
The Infinities have the ability to stop our hunting parties, so now...
We need to understand how... strong their ability actually is.

What are the things they can predict, what they cannot. We need to understand the limits and boundaries of their powers and see if we can come up with something to take advantage of that, hence, the ten parties we sent."
Again, the people nodded, waiting for Amaya to continue—
"The first two weren’t different.

They were just sent to make sure whether the Infinities would be able to stop them or not, these parties didn’t target Light or Darkness Worlds that our normal hunting parties usually target these days.
These were sent to Eternity and Balance Worlds, worlds that the ’Anomaly’ wouldn’t usually attack, so there was no way for the Infinities to be prepared for the attack.
But...
The same thing happened again.
One of the Infinities was there to stop them, both times.
So we can be sure that this isn’t the Infinities guessing our possible targets, they haven’t predicted a ’pattern’ we unconsciously leave—
No, they indeed have a way to predict where we are going to attack and they move beforehand to protect that world and hopefully capture Nux."
The air in the room turned grim, they all knew that at some level, this was somewhat obvious, somewhere in their hearts, they knew that the enemy did have a way to stop them but...
Now that it was confirmed, this seemed... much heavier.
"After the first two parties—
We sent the third, this time, the third party returned with positive news."
Amaya smiled lightly.

chapters.title: Chapter 2338: The Infinities were there?
paragraphs: "After the first two parties—
We sent the third, this time, the third party returned with positive news."
Amaya spoke with a light smile on her face. The rest looked at her with slight surprise and she continued—
"This party was... weaker than the others.
While the last two parties had Eternals as they attacked Middle Level Worlds, this time, we lowered the level.
This time, we sent Transcendents to attack a Low Level World and once again, the Infinities appeared and the party was hunted down the instant they appeared."
"Infinities appeared to... deal with Transcendents...?"
Vyriana frowned in confusion and Amaya nodded with a smile.
"Yes."
Riona’s eyes shined—
"This means they have no way to know... who is attacking, they just know that there will be an attack."
"That is correct."
Amaya nodded.
"The Infinities have no way to differentiate between Nux and other beings from our Universe, their strength, their movements, their Aura, they cannot differentiate any of them.
To them—
All of us are... Anomalies.
This is also the reason they are the ones who make the move even when it’s only Transcendents attacking the worlds."

"What if... they only do that to ensure no one runs away? Eternals have a slower reaction speed compared to them, what if they feared that the moment we realize they were waiting for an attack, we would summon them back and they wouldn’t get anything?"
Lyriana questioned with a frown.
"No, that doesn’t make sense."
Sharnoth shook her head.
"The Infinities do not want the puppets, they want the Anomaly.
If they knew only the puppets would attack, they wouldn’t bother moving on their own and would send their subordinates instead.
The Infinities do not like to move on their own, we know that well."
"What if they are trying to get rid of all the puppets we have?"
Lyriana asked.
That was quite possible too, it was a common strategy to take the enemy’s arms and legs in order to force him out.
But there was a flaw in that statement too—
"They think we come from another Universe, you think they would want to deal with every single being of a particular Universe... all on their own...?
Every single day?"
Sharnoth shook her head.
"There are quadrillions of beings in a single Universe, they couldn’t possibly keep fighting every single one of them, it is just not practical."
"But we still believe Zylarith is with them, correct? If that is true, then they shouldn’t believe in the theory of another Universe at this point."
Lyriana frowned, but again, Shadow shook her head.
"They are the Infinities,
Arrogance is etched into their very beings, if they believe something, it would be next to impossible to make them think otherwise.
Not to mention master doesn’t have a way to prove his words, sure, he can tell them all the stories of Yrniel and everything else—
But in the end, it had been centuries since he last saw Nux.
Let alone the Infinities, even he would now be doubting whether somehow Nux became affiliated with another Universe or not."
Sharnoth then paused for a moment and added another point—
"And even if the Infinities believe him, that Nux isn’t from any Universe and that the only puppets he has are the ones he collected from their Universe—
At this point, Nux has trillions of them.
You think they would want to capture every single one of them individually, on their own?"
Sharnoth asked and Lyriana turned silent.
The rest of the women watched silently, Amaya then nodded at them, at Sharnoth to be more specific.
"I came to the same conclusion,
The Infinities have no way of knowing who is attacking.
So they would basically react to anything we throw at them and using that information, I continued the experiment and sent another party—
This party wasn’t sent to attack the worlds, they were just sent to... observe the Main Universe and take no action whatsoever.
I wanted to know how the Infinities would react to them, would they know that our party was there?
Because if they did, it would mean that from now on, we wouldn’t be able to leave our Universe? That we are basically trapped here.
Fortunately, however, that doesn’t seem to be the case.
The Infinities did not appear even as our party continued to roam around the Universe, they even interacted with a few people, but again, the Infinities didn’t appear."
"What if... they didn’t appear on purpose?"
Astaria questioned.
"At this point, the Infinities too, would have understood that the Anomaly knows they have a way to stop him.
That must have stumped them too.
This was their biggest breakthrough in this battle so far, and it... had failed.
So what if... they are trying to make us let our guard down?
What if they are not attacking because they wish to create an illusion that their power is no longer working, or that they can no longer keep it activated?"
"That’s possible."
Amaya nodded.
"But for now, it doesn’t matter because from this moment forward, none of us are leaving our Universe, not until we have a clear understanding of what’s going on."
She declared looking right into Nux’s eyes.
Nux just nodded silently, he had no plans to leave either.
Amaya nodded back, then she glanced at Astaria and—
"They can set all the traps they want, it won’t matter. None of us are going to fall for it. All their planning would do is to let our parties begin their hunt again."
"Which they shouldn’t be able to do, especially since they need to protect the worlds in order to keep their reputation."
Felberta muttered.
"I doubt they care about their reputation that much at this point, getting their hands on Nux is much more important."
Aeliana corrected, Felberta nodded in understanding as well.
"So for now, we believe that they do not know the instant we leave our Universe and get to theirs, correct?"
Shadow asked, wanting to continue the conversation.
"Yes, that is correct."
Amaya nodded.
"I tested it a few times, I sent the same party to different parts of the Universe, about a hundred times now, and the Infinities did not appear, not even once.
So entering the Universe is safe.
Now, we need to understand how far we can actually go.
Interacting with beings of the Universe poses no problem, the Infinities did not react till then.
So I pushed forward.
I sent a party inside a world, there was no mission, they weren’t supposed to devour anything, I wanted to see if entering the world is a trigger."
"And?"
Eisheth asked curiously.
"Nothing."
Amaya shook her head.
"Nothing happened, the Infinities did not appear.
To see whether all of this wasn’t a trap, or that the Infinities have actually stopped reacting to our movements, I sent another party to devour some other world.
And the Infinity of Darkness was there."
"So they were reacting."
Lyriana commented, Amaya nodded.
"That means entering the world isn’t a trigger either."
Ember asked and Amaya nodded again.
"That is correct."

"So we can enter the Universe, we can enter the worlds, then... what’s the trigger? The Infinities are already inside the worlds we target, how are they not already there when we send our party, it makes no sense."
Melia asked with a frown.
"Or is it... the intent?"
Riona guessed, she didn’t seem very sure but—
"I came to the same conclusion."
Amaya nodded.
"When I send a party without any commands, the Infinities aren’t there, but when I send them to devour those worlds, the Infinities are.
This seemed more like an intent."
"But... these are puppets...
They have no intent of their own."
Felberta frowned.
"Correct."
Amaya nodded.
"This wasn’t exactly about intent, it was... connected to fate."
"Fate...?"
Rune frowned.
"Mhm."
Amaya nodded, then she began explaining.
"After entering the worlds posed no problems, I tried interacting with the world, talking to its residents, that didn’t do anything either.
I then sent a party to steal something, that didn’t change anything either but then, I told another party to... steal something important to that world.
And it happened."
"The Infinities were there?"
Felberta asked and Amaya nodded.
"Exactly."
"So anything that affects the fate of the world... is the trigger."
Aeliana muttered, her crimson eyes shining brightly.
"That is what I think, yes."
Amaya nodded.
"You... think?"
Vyriana raised her eyebrows.
"These are all, at one level, just... guesses.
I cannot say anything with certainty, I’ve only had a few months to figure all this out."
"A few months is a long time."
Vyriana snorted.
"Yeah? Try experimenting knowing that you need to wait at least a week before testing another one of your theories, then we will talk."
Amaya snorted.
The one week wait was necessary because if she did all of this at the same time, the Infinities would know they were experiments and if they did—
They would do everything in their power to make sure they came to the wrong conclusion and had incorrect information.
Amaya couldn’t allow that—
So she played it patiently.
Vyriana backed down as well, she could tell how much all of this had worried Amaya, not just her, it was the same for every single one of them.
So whatever information they did have—
It was important.
"Anyways, I still need time to run more experiments, only then I would be able to say anything with certainty."
Amaya spoke and the rest nodded.
[Do we know anything else? What triggers the fate of the world? How strong must the trigger be? Anything?]

chapters.title: Chapter 2339: What about the children?
paragraphs: "Anyways, I still need time to run more experiments, only then I would be able to say anything with certainty."
Amaya spoke. The rest of the people nodded and then—
[Do we know anything else? What triggers the fate of the world? How strong must the trigger be? Anything?]
Azriel asked with a solemn look on his face.
The Vampire Progenitor could sense it.
This was the final moment, a moment that would change the very fate of their Universe and the worst part?
He was not ready for it.
He was still... weaker than his prime self.
It wasn’t a war he could participate in, he needed more time and right now, the only thing in his mind was to buy that time.
Amaya looked at him for a moment, then she nodded slightly.
"That’s what I am trying to find out. My experiments are still ongoing, I wish to see what triggers the reaction out of the four of them.

I am thinking of trying assassinations, starting with a common thief, to a corrupt noble, then a World Leader, I would see how the Infinities react to them all and see what triggers a reaction. Coming up with an accurate answer, however, would still be difficult."
[Because they would sense what you are trying to do.]
Azriel muttered with a solemn nod and Amaya nodded back.
"That is correct. The more experiments I do, the more they would realize that their reaction only gives us more information, while they get nothing in return, other than our puppets, of course."
[But?]
Azriel raised an eyebrow, he knew there was something else the Devourer wanted to say and... he was correct.
"But I am sure I would be able to get the answers I need before they set their traps.
After all, like us, they too are walking onto a path they have never tread on before. They too must not be prepared to take any chances."
Azriel nodded at those words.
He then stared at the rest of the women, before his eyes fell on Nux and—
[Are you sure about your decision?]
He asked. Nux, however, rolled his eyes and—
"Yes, I am. Now before you say anything, please stop. I am not taking any risks, I have made it plenty clear. Not a single child of mine will be leaving my Universe."
Nux spoke with conviction, he had no intention of backing down.
He knew why Azriel was asking what he was asking, now that he had closed the Universe, Azriel could no longer meet Samael, his grandson and Nux regretted that too.

He had seen how close Samael and Azriel had gotten, he had seen the warm side Azriel showed to the boy, the side Nux had only seen him show to Aeliana before, he had seen how much Azriel valued Samael but...
With everything going on outside, with Zylarith out there planning... who knows what...

Nux did not wish to take any risk, even when he knew that sending his child to Azriel, where he would most probably be safe since no one in the entire Universe could sense where Azriel actually was, he... he was still paranoid.
Of course, Azriel understood that as well.
If it were up to him, he would have done the exact same thing.
After all, the fact of the matter is, right now, Nux was stronger than Azriel and Azriel still needed time to reach the level he was in the past.
But still—
[What about the children?]
Azriel asked directly.
And the instant he did, all the women turned towards Nux and Nux...
He, ignoring Azriel, looked at all his wives and finally...
"That’s... not just my decision to make."
He answered honestly.
"We make it together."
He looked at his wives and spoke with a silent nod, a nod that would have put a smile on their faces if this was a normal situation but...
Thiswasn’ta normal situation and there was... no smile on their faces.
They just seemed... unwilling.
"How much resources do we have...?"
Felberta asked directly.
It was already clear from the very beginning, their own Universe, although it could help them support life, growing it was an entirely different thing.

They were using foreign resources to force the Universe to support their children’s growth, it was something they needed to continue, at least till their children reached the Primordial Stage, then, they could wait for the Universe to catch up to them and allow their children to grow naturally.
That was the plan.
But...
Now, that plan wasn’t feasible anymore.
Devouring more worlds now seemed impossible, at least not until they found a way around whatever trick the Infinities were using to stop them.
And clearly, that needed time.
Till then, they needed to use the resources they had been saving all this time.

And none of them liked that feeling, after all, if they needed to use the existing resources with no way to renew those resources, it meant they had a limited amount of time, and they needed to fix this mess before that time ran out or their children wouldn’t be able to grow like they should.

Till now, this wasn’t a problem since the children were frozen in time right after the gathering all those years ago. They decided to make it so because they knew they needed time to understand what was happening, and for that, they needed all their focus here and not on the children.
Of course, the limited amount of resources they had was another reason they decided to freeze the children.
But...
That couldn’t continue any longer.
They were already missing the children, but even more importantly, keeping them in a time freeze any longer than they already had would damage their minds and their bodies at some level.
After all, time was a powerful concept, their bodies weren’t strong enough to bear its burden, not right now.
Therefore, they needed to release the children, and this was exactly the reason Felberta asked what she asked.
How long did they have?
Once the children were awake and started using those saved-up resources for their growth, how long would those resources last?
And the one who answered that question was Shadow.
"Twenty years."
The moment the women heard those words, they blinked in surprise.
"Twenty...?"
Astaria tilted her head in confusion.
"That’s it? We have devoured hundreds of worlds! How do we only have... only twenty years’ worth of resources? That makes no sense."
She complained.

All these years, they weren’t just devouring Low Level Worlds, they had even devoured High Level Worlds, worlds that were on a similar level as Umbrasol—a world that the moment Nux devoured it, he became an entirely different level of existence.
How could... they only have twenty years of resources after devouring such worlds...?
Shadow looked at her sisters and instantly realized what they were thinking, and their thoughts made sense at some level but...
"You are forcing a literal Universe to do what would usually take it billions of years, you think that won’t come with a price?"
Shadow asked a simple question and the women turned silent, Shadow however, wasn’t done.
"And don’t think the children aren’t at fault."
She chuckled as if she remembered something amusing.
"What do you mean?"
Felberta frowned and Shadow—
"Oh come on."
She laughed.
"Have you not seen those little things? They are barely ten and no Semi-Saints have what it takes to stand against any of them. Some of them could give even Divines a hard time.
Sure, it makes sense since they arehischildren but...
Do you really think that’s it?"
The women didn’t say anything, they just turned towards Nux, who, instead of looking at them, looked away, not wanting to look into their eyes.
Shadow then chuckled softly, almost as if she found all of this to be silly and—
"He used extra resources to strengthen them."
She revealed the truth.
"What...?"
The women frowned, Shadow on the other hand, just shrugged.
"You all must have sensed it as well, no? Our children are much stronger than usual and I am not talking about their cultivation—
Most of them are only Great Sages or Semi-Saints, but their bodies, or their abilities—
They are strong enough to affect even Divines with their abilities, did you think that was just a coincidence, or was it because you thought they were his children so it made sense?"
Shadow asked as she looked at her sisters and then—
"While all of that may be true, the real reason behind it all is that Nux has been using extra resources to strengthen the children.
He isn’t directly affecting their cultivation since that depends on the amount of work they put in, but his actions are making their bodies and their abilities stronger."
"So that’s it..."

A few women, especially Astaria, Vyriana and Aeliana’s eyes shined with enlightenment, these were the women who focused more on their children’s strength than others and they often found it strange how quickly those little things grew.
But if the reason behind their growth was because a certain someone was using extra resources to make them stronger then...
Then it all made sense...
"How long will the resources last if we stop strengthening them?"
Amaya asked with a solemn look on her face and Shadow—
"Thirty years."
She answered.

Sure, it makes sense since they arehischildren but...
Do you really think that’s it?"
The women didn’t say anything, they just turned towards Nux, who, instead of looking at them, looked away, not wanting to look into their eyes.
Shadow then chuckled softly, almost as if she found all of this to be silly and—
"He used extra resources to strengthen them."
She revealed the truth.
"What...?"
The women frowned, Shadow on the other hand, just shrugged.
"You all must have sensed it as well, no?
Our children are much stronger than usual and I am not talking about their cultivation—
Most of them are only Great Sages or Semi-Saints, but their bodies, or their abilities—
They are strong enough to affect even Divines with their abilities, did you think that was just a coincidence, or was it because you thought they were his children so it made sense?"
Shadow asked as she looked at her sisters and then—
"While all of that may be true, the real reason behind it all is that Nux has been using extra resources to strengthen the children.
He isn’t directly affecting their cultivation since that depends on the amount of work they put in, but his actions are making their bodies and their abilities stronger."
"So that’s it..."

A few women, especially Astaria, Vyriana and Aeliana’s eyes shined with enlightenment, these were the women who focused more on their children’s strength than others and they often found it strange how quickly those little things grew.
But if the reason behind their growth was because a certain someone was using extra resources to make them stronger then...
Then it all made sense...
"How long will the resources last if we stop strengthening them?"
Amaya asked with a solemn look on her face and Shadow—
"Thirty years."
She answered.

chapters.title: Chapter 2340: Ten thousand years.
paragraphs: "How long will the resources last if we stop strengthening them?"
Amaya asked with a solemn look on her face.

She hated asking that question, anything that benefited the children was important, she understood that well and if she were in Nux’s stead, she too would use resources the same way, even if the resources weren’t directly affecting the children but...
While she understood everything, she, at the same time, also understood how critical of a stage they were in.
Even now, she didn’t know how long it would take for them to find a solution to the problem they were facing, heck, she didn’t even know if theywouldfind a solution at all.
At this point, they needed to save as many resources as they could.
And Shadow understood that, so—
"Thirty years."
She answered and Amaya blinked.
"That’s... fifty percent more..."
Shadow nodded silently.
"So if we weren’t strengthening the children since the start, we would have resources for five more years."
Riona muttered, but this time, Shadow shook her head.
"More."
She spoke directly.
Riona narrowed her eyes, Shadow looked at Nux, who was now counting the number of stars around them and—
"He used more resources when the children were small, if he hadn’t, the resources would have lasted around a hundred more years."
"That’s a thousand years in the Main Universe..."
Amaya muttered softly, looking at Nux.
"Yes."
Shadow nodded.
"But in his defence, the resources Nux used gave the children a very strong, stable foundation, one that almost no being in the Universe, either ours, or the Main Universe would have.
This is also the reason the children grew so quickly, the resources didn’t affect their cultivation, but the benefits the children received boosted their growth."
"Alright, there is no point discussing what has already happened."
Aeliana waved her hand, dismissing the entire thing.
When the attention fell on her, she glanced at Shadow and—
"What about now? If we stop using resources like we have been using, they would last thirty years, correct?"
The Vampire asked.
"Yes."
Shadow nodded.
"And what level would the children reach in these thirty years?"
The Vampire asked.
"Hmm? Most of them should be able to reach... Primordial Stage... or even Transcende—"
Shadow answered without thinking but—
"Divine."
Nux, who had been silent this whole time, spoke and his words instantly attracted the women’s attention.
"Divine...?"
Shadow frowned, as someone who knew quite a lot about the Universe, this answer... didn’t make sense in her mind.
"Nux, all of them are Great Sages or higher and they are barely ten, they have thirty more years to continue growing and you are saying...
They would only reach the Divine Stage...?
That doesn’t make sen—"
"You don’t understand."
Nux shook his head.
He then looked around, not at beings like Sharnoth or Aeliana, but at Thyra, Rune, Melia and the rest of the lot.
The ones who...
Who were once stuck at a certain cultivation stage for years, unable to move up.
"This isn’t a fantasy land."
He began.
"They became Great Sages in ten years, that doesn’t mean they would become Divine in another ten, and reach even higher with more time."
Nux then looked in a particular direction, the direction where the first seed of the Universe was located—
The Seed that represented the Law of Absolute Growth.
The Seed that had now... sprouted into something far far far bigger.
A complete Tree whose roots and branches held literal worlds, it was the base of their Universe, the base that depended on the Law of Absolute Growth or what the people called it—
The Tree of the Beginning.
"One’s rate of growth changes.

You did not sense it because all this while, I have been feeding the Law of Absolute Growth, which is currently only focusing on the children with resources according to the stage the children were in.

At first, the resources required were less, but as the children grew stronger, they needed more resources and I continued to provide those raised amounts of resources, this is why none of you ever noticed anything, this is the reason the little ones continued to grow as fast as they did."
Nux then looked at his wives and—
"But now it’s different.
The thirty years’ worth of resources that we have is for Great Sages, not for Divines or Primordials. The children would be able to grow, even now, but becoming Primordials?
That is highly unlikely.
So don’t get your hopes up."
Nux spoke with a solemn look on his face.
After all, he could tell what the women were thinking, all this while, he had been thinking the same thing, even before the Infinities came up with the same thing.
What the women were hoping for was for the children to reach the Primordial Stage and since Nux would make sure the Laws they comprehended were Absolute, they would be Primordials with Absolute Laws—
Yes.
They would be Immortals.

If they reached that level, Nux wouldn’t even have to leave the Universe to constantly steal resources from the Main Universe since they could always wait for their own Universe to grow and expand on its own, naturally.
That was what Nux was aiming for from the beginning—
Once his children were immortals, he would make a deal with the Infinities of the Main Universe, he would...
Leave the Main Universe alone.
The race between him and Azriel to become the Universe’s God?
He would abandon it because he now had far more important things to worry about, he was no longer a man who was loved by multiple women—
He was now a father to twenty-four children—
He no longer wanted to chase ’thrill’ that could very well put his life at risk, he...
He did not want his children to grow without their father...
Weak?
Maybe.
But—
Nux didn’t care.

His journey was never about being the strongest or proving he was the strongest, his journey was about being able to live a long, long life together with his family without anyone being able to disturb him.

He had been struggling all this while since he feared that the Infinities would find a way to enter his Universe, but now that he had a stronger understanding of his own and the Infinities’ abilities, he knew that wasn’t possible.
So he was safe.
His family was safe.
That was it.
It was over.
Or...
It would have been over if he had enough resources for his children to become Primordials but...
He didn’t.
He needed more resources.
A lot more than he had already stolen.
And since the Infinities now had a way to stop it, he needed to do something and he needed to do something fast because if his calculations were correct—
If his children could only reach Divine Stage with all the resources they were left with—
Then they only had the same amount of time the Divines had.
Ten thousand years.
That was all he had.
If he couldn’t come up with a way to gather more resources in these ten thousand years...
His children would perish and he would be forced to see it happen right in front of his eyes.
Something that neither Nux, nor his wives had the heart to see happen.
Yes, it was now a race against time.
Nux understood that, and so did the women but...
"I don’t understand—
They have YOUR blood."
Shadow didn’t back down.
"YOUR blood.
You said it yourself, they are the Primordials, true Primordials! Their cultivation speed should be way faster than any being in the Universe!
Why would they need more resources!? They are already being given the necessary resources!"
Shadow asked, losing her cool.
She was comparatively calmer since she had planned everything in her head, but with Nux now putting a bucket of cold water on her plans—
She was panicking, so much that her body had started trembling, a rare sight considering the woman knew almost everything about the Universe.
Nux, on the other hand, just looked at her closely and—
"Their cultivation speed is already faster than any being in the Universe."
He answered calmly.
"What are yo—"
Shadow couldn’t believe the ridiculous statement she just heard, but just as she was about to counter, she froze as she realized what Nux was talking about—
Yes, the children’s cultivation was faster than any being in their Universe because... no other being that was truly part of Nux’s Universe could... actually cultivate...
Heck, other than their children, no other complete, complex, intelligent being that completely belonged to the Universe even existed.
The Universe wasn’t at the stage where such beings could be born.
Yes, there were complex beings that were now part of Nux’s Universe, but they were all...stolen.
And while the Universe supported their cultivation and Nux could even help their cultivation grow using his Law of Absolute Growth without having to spend a ridiculous amount of resources but...
All those beings, despite being part of Nux’s Universe, were foreigners, that fact could never change.
Theirfoundationwould still be that of a foreigner’s, this is why Nux could raise that foundation in whatever way he liked without having to spend so many resources—
But for foundations that came from his own Universe—
For him to grow them—
He would need to change the very Universe, he would need to... grow the very Universe.
And Nux knew that—
"The fact that they carry my blood does not change anything, not for them."
Nux shook his head.

chapters.title: Chapter 2341: Would you be able to take it?
paragraphs: "The fact that they carry my blood does not change anything, not for them."
Nux shook his head as he glanced at Shadow.
"The only thing it affects is the ability they are born with."
"But they inherit our abilities..."
Melia frowned in confusion. The children inherited the abilities of their mothers’ blood, then how did Nux...
"And my blood simply strengthened that ability. This is why every child’s ability is stronger than their mother’s.
But that is it.
That is all their blood does.
It doesn’t work like how it does in the Main Universe. Their blood does not determine what cultivation stage they would reach.
They do not possess what you would callpotentialbecause they... should not even exist."
Nux explained everything and as he did—
The entire space turned deathly silent.

Shadow now seemed pale, the rest of the women were shocked too, but for them, this was already an emergency. They already had this reaction a hundred years ago and while none of them had recovered till now, their heads were... still clearer than Shadow’s.
Ten Thousand Years, that’s all we have, correct?"
Amaya asked, looking at Nux, ignoring Shadow’s broken state. Nux looked back at her and—
"Considering they all become Divines, yes."
He nodded.
"Considering...?"
Amaya narrowed her eyes and Nux...
He didn’t know how he was supposed to say this, but he knew this wasn’t the time to hesitate—
"Divine is what I predict they would be, that prediction may or may not be true. It is entirely possible for a few to remain Semi Saints if they slack."
"Then we just need to make sure none of them slacks."

Astaria narrowed her eyes and this time, no woman stopped her. This was no longer about the children’s strength, this was about their survival, and for that, even if they had to become much stricter, the women wouldn’t hesitate.

Even women like Evane, Skyla, Allura, Aisha, Eisheth, and Edda, who weren’t particularly concerned about how hard the children worked as long as they kept smiling, suddenly had serious looks on their faces.
The children...
They would be seeing entirely new mothers the moment they woke up.
[Wait.]
Suddenly, Azriel called out with a confused look on his face.
Everyone turned towards him and he asked a simple question—
[Say the children become Semi Saints in these thirty years, that means they would live for three thousand years, correct?]
He asked.
"Yes, that is correct."
Nux nodded.
[Then considering the time in your Universe moves slower than normal, wouldn’t these three thousand years actually be... thirty thousand years in our Universe?]
Azriel asked and the instant he did, Aeliana’s expression changed.
"If it’s thirty thousand years...
Then you..."
She spoke, pointing at her father and Azriel nodded, knowing exactly what his daughter was thinking.
[Thirty Thousand years would be more than enough for me to break through and become an Infinity.
It would allow me to not only recover my past strength, but also go beyond.
Those four wouldn’t be an issue Thirty Thousand years later, I guarantee that.]
Azriel announced as his crimson eyes shone confidently.
He didn’t seem to have a shred of doubt despite knowing he would be up against four Infinities and Zylarith.
And the odd part about all this?
None of the women doubted him either.
He was already stronger than the other Four Infinities when he was bound to Yrniel.
But with his restrictions now gone and a Law even stronger than that already ridiculous Law he had?

Azriel, the moment he became an Infinity, would reach a level no being had ever reached. He would be a monster none of the so-called Four Strongest Beings in the Universe would be able to stand against.
But—
"Once you become an Infinity... wouldn’t you be forced to stop us...?"
Felberta questioned with a frown on her face.

The only reason Azriel, despite being chosen by the Universe as its Hero, had been able to ignore their movements was because the Universe knew that he currently wasn’t strong enough to stop the Anomaly—

But that would change once Azriel became an Infinity, because the moment he did, the Universe would know and since the Infinities had already stopped the Anomaly, the Universe’s Child being unable to stop the Anomaly, even at his strongest, would be a clear giveaway.

The Universe would understand that its child and its enemy were together and its reaction would be far, far more violent. It might even self-destruct together with Azriel and that wouldn’t help anyone.
[I have a way out.]
Azriel spoke again, looking at Felberta.
[I will allow one attack.]
He revealed the plan. Felberta narrowed her eyes and Azriel continued—
[In a few thousand years, Yrniel will reappear, the Universe’s Protection over it will disappear and Zylarith will sense that.
The Infinities will use that chance to attack, knowing that I would be forced to reveal myself in order to protect it.
Then, I would have no choice but to go against the Four Infinities, who are now coming for the world I was born in.
That would start the second battle between the Five Infinities. I do not know how long that battle would last.]
Azriel paused for a moment and glanced at Nux—
[But the moment I win.]
He spoke with certainty, as if he never once doubted the outcome of the battle.
[You will move.]
He ordered.

[You will prepare your Anomaly Army or whatever, and you will devour as many worlds as you need. Target the Four Supreme Worlds too, those would give you far more resources than normal worlds. Don’t think about how the Universe would react, or whether it would self-destruct, leave all that to me.
You devour however much you require.
Make sure it’s enough for the children to become Primordials.
Then—
I will move and I willcapture and killthe Anomaly once and for all, is that clear?]
The Vampire Progenitor asked and the women looked at him with a newfound shine in their eyes.
They understood the plan, it was perfect.
At that point, the Universe would know well enough that the Four Infinities hadn’t killed the Anomaly, they had just stopped it. It would know that the Anomaly might reappear at any time.
And reappearing right after the War between the Five Infinities, when the Universe was at its weakest, was something that the Universe would never find suspicious.
It was something any enemy with half a brain would do.
Then, once the final attack was launched and they had devoured enough, Azriel would move, ’capture the Anomaly’, which could be any one of Nux’s puppets and kill him.

The Universe would sense it all, Azriel would declare the enemy leader dead and that they no longer had a way to return. The Universe would still be doubtful, but since they already had what they needed, they would no longer need to attack the Universe, convincing the Universe’s Will that its child truly had ended the Anomaly’s terror.
And with that—
Azriel would become the God of the Universe, revive Aeliana’s mothers and...
Everyone would live happily after.
But...
Amaya had a question—
"Would you be able to take it?"
She asked as she glanced at Azriel. The Vampire Progenitor frowned in confusion and Amaya—
"If what Nux said was right, the amount of resources we would need for the children to become Primordials would be huge.
We would need to devour millions of worlds and... ignoring how the Universe would react to an attack that big—
Attacking such a large number of worlds would... automatically increase the chances of us devouring your wives’ souls."
Amaya spoke and the instant she did, silence fell over the space. Aeliana froze completely, trying to understand what that meant but before she could think too much—
"That won’t be an issue."
Shadow, who had been spiralling down into the hole of despair all this while, instantly brought her attention back to the topic when they had a solution and she shook her head.
"Even if we did devour them, we would be able to find them and I can do what Lord Azriel wishes to do.
I can go through all their reincarnations, bring back the memories of their lives as Lord Azriel’s wives and create bodies for them.
The only difference would be that they would then be part of our Universe, which wouldn’t exactly be a problem since they would still be with Lord Azriel regardless."
She explained.
"You can... do that...?"
Aeliana blinked and Shadow grinned again—
"Did you forget?
I am the Goddess of Our Universe."
She spoke, puffing her chest up, her usual cheerfulness had returned now that everything seemed to have a perfect solution.
[Then I will be relying on you.]
Azriel nodded at Shadow, who nodded back with the same grin.
"You can leave it to me."
She patted her chest in pride, then, she looked around, seeing everyone’s smiles but the moment her eyes fell on Felberta, she paused.
Felberta didn’t seem... happy.
No, she was looking at Nux, more specifically at his fists and when Shadow saw them, her smile faded away as well.
Nux’s fists were trembling.
As if... he didn’t agree with the plan they had come up with...

He didn’t seem to have a shred of doubt despite knowing he would be up against four Infinities and Zylarith.
And the odd part about all this?
None of the women doubted him either.
He was already stronger than the other Four Infinities when he was bound to Yrniel.
But with his restrictions now gone and a Law even stronger than that already ridiculous Law he had?
Azriel, the moment he became an Infinity, would reach a level no being had ever reached.
He would be a monster none of the so-called Four Strongest Beings in the Universe would be able to stand against.
But—
"Once you become an Infinity... wouldn’t you be forced to stop us...?"
Felberta questioned with a frown on her face.

The only reason Azriel, despite being chosen by the Universe as its Hero, had been able to ignore their movements was because the Universe knew that he currently wasn’t strong enough to stop the Anomaly—

But that would change once Azriel became an Infinity, because the moment he did, the Universe would know and since the Infinities had already stopped the Anomaly, the Universe’s Child being unable to stop the Anomaly, even at his strongest, would be a clear giveaway.
The Universe would understand that its child and its enemy were together and its reaction would be far, far more violent.
It might even self-destruct together with Azriel and that wouldn’t help anyone.
[I have a way out.]
Azriel spoke again, looking at Felberta.
[I will allow one attack.]
He revealed the plan.
Felberta narrowed her eyes and Azriel continued—
[In a few thousand years, Yrniel will reappear, the Universe’s Protection over it will disappear and Zylarith will sense that.
The Infinities will use that chance to attack, knowing that I would be forced to reveal myself in order to protect it.
Then, I would have no choice but to go against the Four Infinities, who are now coming for the world I was born in.
That would start the second battle between the Five Infinities.
I do not know how long that battle would last.]
Azriel paused for a moment and glanced at Nux—
[But the moment I win.]
He spoke with certainty, as if he never once doubted the outcome of the battle.
[You will move.]
He ordered.
[You will prepare your Anomaly Army or whatever, and you will devour as many worlds as you need.
Target the Four Supreme Worlds too, those would give you far more resources than normal worlds.
Don’t think about how the Universe would react, or whether it would self-destruct, leave all that to me.
You devour however much you require.
Make sure it’s enough for the children to become Primordials.
Then—
I will move and I willcapture and killthe Anomaly once and for all, is that clear?]
The Vampire Progenitor asked and the women looked at him with a newfound shine in their eyes.
They understood the plan, it was perfect.
At that point, the Universe would know well enough that the Four Infinities hadn’t killed the Anomaly, they had just stopped it.
It would know that the Anomaly might reappear at any time.
And reappearing right after the War between the Five Infinities, when the Universe was at its weakest, was something that the Universe would never find suspicious.
It was something any enemy with half a brain would do.
Then, once the final attack was launched and they had devoured enough, Azriel would move, ’capture the Anomaly’, which could be any one of Nux’s puppets and kill him.
The Universe would sense it all, Azriel would declare the enemy leader dead and that they no longer had a way to return.

The Universe would still be doubtful, but since they already had what they needed, they would no longer need to attack the Universe, convincing the Universe’s Will that its child truly had ended the Anomaly’s terror.
And with that—
Azriel would become the God of the Universe, revive Aeliana’s mothers and...
Everyone would live happily after.
But...
Amaya had a question—
"Would you be able to take it?"
She asked as she glanced at Azriel.
The Vampire Progenitor frowned in confusion and Amaya—
"If what Nux said was right, the amount of resources we would need for the children to become Primordials would be huge.
We would need to devour millions of worlds and... ignoring how the Universe would react to an attack that big—
Attacking such a large number of worlds would... automatically increase the chances of us devouring your wives’ souls."
Amaya spoke and the instant she did, silence fell over the space.
Aeliana froze completely, trying to understand what that meant but before she could think too much—
"That won’t be an issue."
Shadow, who had been spiralling down into the hole of despair all this while, instantly brought her attention back to the topic when they had a solution and she shook her head.
"Even if we did devour them, we would be able to find them and I can do what Lord Azriel wishes to do.
I can go through all their reincarnations, bring back the memories of their lives as Lord Azriel’s wives and create bodies for them.
The only difference would be that they would then be part of our Universe, which wouldn’t exactly be a problem since they would still be with Lord Azriel regardless."
She explained.
"You can... do that...?"
Aeliana blinked and Shadow grinned again—
"Did you forget?
I am the Goddess of Our Universe."
She spoke, puffing her chest up, her usual cheerfulness had returned now that everything seemed to have a perfect solution.
[Then I will be relying on you.]
Azriel nodded at Shadow, who nodded back with the same grin.
"You can leave it to me."
She patted her chest in pride, then, she looked around, seeing everyone’s smiles but the moment her eyes fell on Felberta, she paused.
Felberta didn’t seem... happy.
No, she was looking at Nux, more specifically at his fists and when Shadow saw them, her smile faded away as well.
Nux’s fists were trembling.
As if... he didn’t agree with the plan they had come up with...

chapters.title: Chapter 2342: We will figure a way out.
paragraphs: Shadow called out with an uncertain look on her face. Hearing her tone, the rest of the women noticed Nux’s reaction as well and their smiles faded away.
What was the matter?
Why was Nux reacting like that?
They all thought the same thing.
Felberta, who had been watching Nux from the moment this conversation began, started thinking another thing.
Could it be that... Nux didn’t like depending on Lord Azriel...?

She remembered the contest between the two, regarding who would become the Universe’s God first. It was something they decided centuries ago. Most of them had already forgotten about it, especially since everything that had happened, but...
Knowing Nux, he must still remember.
But at the same time...
She also knew Nux wasn’t someone who would let such a vain contest put the lives of his children in jeopardy.
Then what was it?
Did he not trust Lord Azriel would be able to win against the Four Infinities?
That was a possibility as well.

And it wasn’t just him. Felberta herself had been thinking about it too. Lord Azriel, at his strongest, was the strongest being she had stood in the presence of. The air around him was unnatural, she would never deny that.
She also wouldn’t deny that, given time, he would be able to surpass his previous self.
However...
She had also seen the Four Infinities, and they too were not weak.
Yes, they believed that Lord Azriel, at his prime, was stronger than the Four Infinities, but the source of that information was none other than Zylarith and...
She didn’t know if she could trust that man and form a plan that affected the children’s lives based on that.
Was that it?
Was that what Nux was thinking?
She wondered.
"Nux, what is it?"
Vyriana asked in a strict voice. Nux looked at her, then at Shadow, before finally looking at Azriel—
"We do not have thirty thousand years."
He shook his head.
[What...?]
Azriel’s expression changed. It wasn’t just him, the women seemed confused too.
"Are you saying the children won’t even become Semi Saints in the next thirty years?"
Astaria’s frown deepened.
"That is not it."
Nux, however, shook his head again.
"But this is not about them being Semi Saints."
"Then what is it about?"
Lyriana asked.
Nux paused for a moment and that was when Azriel narrowed his eyes.
[It is the difference between the Flow of Time between your and my Universe.]
He spoke.
Nux looked at the Vampire Progenitor and nodded with a hesitant look on his face.
"What...?"
Shadow’s frown deepened.
"But the Flow of Time between the two Universes has always been constant..."
She commented. Nux looked at her and shook his head.
"That was because resources were being used to stabilize our Universe."
The women’s frowns deepened and Nux explained properly.
"The time in our Universe is different from the Main Universe. There is no connection between them whatsoever, meaning that there is no link between them.
A hundred years here could be one there, a thousand years there could be one here, it is all random."
[Are you saying...]
Azriel’s tone became grave. Nux looked at him and completed his sentence with a nod.

"After these thirty years, once we run out of foreign resources, we have no way to know how long we have. We can either have enough time for you to become an Infinity, or we might not. There is no way to be certain."
And the moment those words were said—
A deafening silence spread all over the place.
No one knew what to say. These were their children’s lives they were talking about and every single person here hated that they had no way out of this mess.
The one who had it the worst was Allura.
The Succubus had already sealed her thoughts, making sure no one else knew what she was thinking and in her mind, she started blaming herself.
How could she not?

She was the reason all of them were in this mess. She was the one who couldn’t control herself, she was the one who became carefree, she was the one who conceived knowingly and hid it from everyone till it was too late.
Had she not done that—
Had she not conceived, no one else would have.
Then they wouldn’t have children, meaning that whatever it was that was happening outside, it would have had nothing to do with them.

All of them could stay in the Universe for as long as they desired, the Universe could have grown on its own and in a few billion years, once the Universe was ready, they could have given birth to their children.
And who knows?
In that time frame, Nux himself would have gotten strong enough to take care of their enemies and that would have hastened everything.
If only she had been patient...
Allura clenched her fists even more tightly.
"Stop blaming yourself."
That was when Nux spoke up. Allura looked up and saw him staring at her. She blinked in surprise, she once again checked if she had forgotten to hide her thoughts from him but—
"I do not need a mere link to understand what the woman I love is thinking."
Nux spoke directly, looking right into her eyes. Allura didn’t know what to say and Nux didn’t stop.
"It was not your mistake, you did what you felt was correct."
Nux wasn’t saying it just to say it.

Allura had always been like this, always silently taking care of him without taking any credit. Even during the times when his emotional state was a mess, she was there, using her own methods to keep him afloat.
Wanting a child was also one of her ways of doing exactly that.
Yes, it was true that Allura wanted a child, but that wasn’t the only reason she did what she did. She sensed that more than her, Nux needed one.
A Family.
Allura had noted Nux staring at a family, especially how fathers played with their children, more than once. She had noticed that desire, that longing in his eyes.
Even when he didn’t directly feel that way since he didn’t allow his mind to think of that possibility, deep in his heart—
He wanted children.
That was also the reason Nux didn’t stop Allura the moment he found out.
"It was me."
Nux admitted.
"I let my guard down."

Honestly, even though one section of his mind had always considered the possibility of the Infinities somehow figuring out a way to stop them, he had been terrorizing the Universe for decades. He had manipulated the Infinities, the strongest beings in the Universe, into the exact situation he wanted and there seemed no way out of it.
Everything seemed to be going his way, the two Infinities were at War, the other two refused to move, he had more than enough worlds to devour, it was... perfect.
It was all under his control.
It wasn’t just that.
It had been centuries since Nux had faced a genuine challenge. He didn’t even remember the last time he felt that he might actually lose his life.
He had been... winning and none of his close wins had been... close.
With the power to appear and disappear whenever he desired, return to any of his wives’ shadows in case he died, and other absurd Laws he had comprehended—
He had become... invincible.
That invincibility made him arrogant.
And in that arrogance, the section of his mind that always considered the possibility of the Infinities fighting back continued to be pushed back, again and again and again.
In his mind, the Four Infinities were no longer the strongest beings in the Universe, the strongest enemies he would ever face, or a threat—
They became... people he could easily manipulate.
Beings he could play with and win.
Beings who were helpless against him, despite their strength.
And somewhere along the way, that led him to believe that the Infinities would never win, that he... would never lose.

This was the reason he let go. This was the reason he let Allura and others conceive and give birth to their children, even though he knew this could very well put his children in danger. After all, he never once considered he might lose.
And that...
That arrogance was now coming to bite him.
The worst part?
There was nothing he could do about it but face it head on.
"I’ll figure out a way."

Nux spoke as he appeared next to Allura and gently held her hands. Allura looked up and when she did, Nux felt a foreign force squeezing his heart because her eyes were moist. She was barely holding back her tears.
Nux tightened his hold, his heart started racing. For the first time in a long, long while—
He was scared.
But with that fear—
Came a determination far stronger than anything he had ever felt.
This battle—
He would win it as well.
No matter what it took.
"We will figure a way out."
He spoke, looking at Allura, then at the other women around him. Then, he glanced at Amaya and—
"Let’s start experimenting, this time, without holding back."
And Amaya—
She looked into her husband’s eyes and—
"Yes."
She nodded.

chapters.title: Chapter 2343: Nux Leander, you seem to be in a tough position.
paragraphs: "Mother..."
Azarion called out in a low voice as he walked towards Allura with a hesitant look on his face. Allura looked at him and gently placed her hand over his cheek.
"What is it?"
She asked with a gentle smile on her face.
"What’s happening?"
The boy asked directly, not holding back one bit.
"What do you mean?"

Allura tilted her head, confused. She then held Azarion’s hand, pulled him close to her and made him sit beside her. Azarion did, then Allura gently placed his head on her lap and started patting his head in a short, calming rhythm.
"Don’t try to hide it."
Azarion, however, didn’t fall for the trick. He kept his eyes open so he wouldn’t fall asleep and stared at his mother till he got an answer.
"I have no need to hide anything from you, you little thing."
"Lies do not suit you, Mother."
Azarion spoke directly, his purple eyes still staring at his mother, as if they refused to give up. He needed an answer, and he needed it today.
Allura looked at him for a moment, then she just smiled.
"Rion, what are you talking about?"
She asked gently, still trying to feign ignorance.
"Father called us to a gathering, we all gathered, shared a table with each other, then the next moment, all children woke up in their beds with their mothers by their side.
You think we won’t find it suspicious?"
"Your Father and Mothers wanted to talk regarding a personal matter, so we put you all to sleep."
"What was that personal matter?"
Azarion asked but Allura just chuckled.
"It won’t be personal if I tell you, now would it?"
She spoke as she ruffled his hair.
"What was so personal that you needed to put us asleep for years?"
Azarion questioned and the moment he did, Allura froze.
She...

From what she knew, they had erased the memories of every being in their Universe. For the rest of the Universe, it should have been like the children were never frozen in time. Only Nux, his wives, and the Progenitors knew the truth, and every single one of them was told not to speak to the children about this.
Then how did he...
"Nihyron came to me."
Azarion answered, knowing exactly what his mother was thinking. Allura narrowed her eyes at those words and Azarion continued—
"He sensed the shift in time, he also noticed that he can no longer sense where any of you are, almost as if someone is purposefully restricting him from doing that."
Allura looked at Azarion, Azarion looked back.
"You know only one person can do that."
Allura remained silent, what could she even say?
Azarion, however, did not understand that.
"What’s happening, Mother?"
He asked again.

"You froze us in time, now we can no longer come to you until you want us to, Kaelith’s the same too, he noticed the Chaos Energy in the Universe has grown, which only happens when a long time passes."
"It is good that you are getting along with your brothers."
Allura praised.
Both Kaelith and Nihyron didn’t usually talk to others, so knowing that Azarion talked to them regularly made her nod in approval.
Azarion, however, just stared at her with a deadpan look on his face and Allura—
She just sighed.
"There are things I cannot tell you, Rion."
"What things?"
"I can’t tell you that."
"Where’s Father?"
He asked another question, but again, Allura shook her head. Allura then placed her hand on Azarion’s cheek again and—
"But I want you to do one thing for me."
"What is it?"
Azarion asked bitterly. He didn’t like how his mother didn’t tell him anything but was now asking something from him.
"You need to keep your siblings in check. They will have the same questions too, you need to handle them."
"How am I supposed to handle them when I don’t even know what’s happening myself?"
"By telling them what I am about to tell you right now."
Allura answered as she looked into her child’s eyes.
"Everything’s fine. Father is just busy dealing with a tricky opponent. Once he wins, he will return."
"Father’s... fighting?"
Azarion blinked.
The thought of his father fighting felt too overwhelming for him.
All his life, every time he had seen his father spar with anyone he could think of, it was never a battle, it was just a show where people wagered how quickly the opponent would be on the ground.
And that was when his Father was significantly holding back. All the battles he ever fought, he was in full control of when to begin them, when to end them.
And now he was being told his father was fighting and no one knew when he would return...?
Just... who was this ’tricky’ enemy Mother mentioned?
Azarion wondered in his head, then an even more nervous question came into his head.
"Will he... win?"
He asked.
This wasn’t a child doubting his father’s strength, Azarion knew how strong his father was. What this was, was a child who was afraid of losing his father.
Allura saw that and out of instinct, she tightly held Azarion’s hand and—
"Of course he will."
She answered.
"Have you ever seen him lose?"
She asked with a chuckle.
"I have not."
Azarion answered with a smile and Allura nodded. The mother and son stayed in that position for a while, Azarion closed his eyes, wanting to sleep on his mother’s lap.
Then, after about a minute—
"I won’t tell them about Father’s fight."
Azarion spoke, keeping his eyes closed.
"They will worry unnecessarily. They are all children, after all."
"Alright, you do as you see fit."
Allura answered with a light chuckle as she continued lightly patting his head as Azarion drifted into dreamland.
On the other side of Nux’s Universe, Nux stood in a void with a grim look on his face.
"What happened?"
Vyriana walked up to him and questioned as she sensed the change in his expression.
"They... sent the Supreme Borns..."
Nux answered in a low voice and Vyriana’s face turned grim as well.

After their conversation, Nux took the lead in Amaya’s ’experiments’ and they stopped hiding anything altogether. Nux did not wait for a week to launch another attack just because he feared the Infinities would understand what he was trying to do.
The Infinities were no fools, at this point, they must have understood everything as well, so Nux dropped all pretense and launched multiple waves of attacks meant to dig information.

They already knew the Infinities were using the power of Fate to predict their attacks. What they needed to understand was the limits of their defense. They wanted to know when exactly it activated in order to try and find ways to move past it.
The result?
It was a failure.
They got the answer, yes, in just a few years, they understood the limits of their defense system and when exactly it activated. The problem, however, was that there was no way around it.

Nux and others tried everything. They first sent a hunting party into a particular world with no intent, intending to keep them there for weeks, hoping to one day just command the party to attack. They hoped that since the intent was shown at the last second, the defense system wouldn’t work, or even if it did, by the time the Infinities got there, it would be too late but—
The Infinities were already there. The party didn’t even get the time to settle in.
Nux and others tried countless such methods, to somehow fool the defense system, but it was absolute. Nothing they did worked.
The Infinities reacted every single time their hunting party was about to devour a world.
It was... frustrating, crushing even, especially for Nux, who could feel the time slipping through his hands.
Then one day, from his desperation, he thought of a plan.
Since their defense system was impenetrable, he decided to use a different approach.
Overwhelming the opponent.
The enemies didn’t know whether it was him or his party that attacked a certain world, so no matter where his party attacked, it was the Infinities who came for defense.
And since there were only four Infinities...
He decided to overwhelm them by sending a hundred hunting parties, targeting a hundred different worlds.

"Rion, what are you talking about?"

"Your Father and Mothers wanted to talk regarding a personal matter, so we put you all to sleep."
"What was that personal matter?"
Azarion asked but Allura just chuckled.
"It won’t be personal if I tell you, now would it?"
She spoke as she ruffled his hair.
"What was so personal that you needed to put us asleep for years?"

"He sensed the shift in time, he also noticed that he can no longer sense where any of you are, almost as if someone is purposefully restricting him from doing that."
Allura looked at Azarion, Azarion looked back.
"You know only one person can do that."
Allura remained silent, what could she even say?
Azarion, however, did not understand that.
"What’s happening, Mother?"
He asked again.

"You froze us in time, now we can no longer come to you until you want us to, Kaelith’s the same too, he noticed the Chaos Energy in the Universe has grown, which only happens when a long time passes."
"It is good that you are getting along with your brothers."
Allura praised.
Both Kaelith and Nihyron didn’t usually talk to others, so knowing that Azarion talked to them regularly made her nod in approval.
Azarion, however, just stared at her with a deadpan look on his face and Allura—
She just sighed.
"There are things I cannot tell you, Rion."
"What things?"
"I can’t tell you that."
"Where’s Father?"
He asked another question, but again, Allura shook her head.
Allura then placed her hand on Azarion’s cheek again and—
"But I want you to do one thing for me."
"What is it?"
Azarion asked bitterly.
He didn’t like how his mother didn’t tell him anything but was now asking something from him.
"You need to keep your siblings in check.
They will have the same questions too, you need to handle them."
"How am I supposed to handle them when I don’t even know what’s happening myself?"
"By telling them what I am about to tell you right now."
Allura answered as she looked into her child’s eyes.
"Everything’s fine.
Father is just busy dealing with a tricky opponent.
Once he wins, he will return."
"Father’s... fighting?"
Azarion blinked.
The thought of his father fighting felt too overwhelming for him.
All his life, every time he had seen his father spar with anyone he could think of, it was never a battle, it was just a show where people wagered how quickly the opponent would be on the ground.
And that was when his Father was significantly holding back.
All the battles he ever fought, he was in full control of when to begin them, when to end them.
And now he was being told his father was fighting and no one knew when he would return...?
Just... who was this ’tricky’ enemy Mother mentioned?
Azarion wondered in his head, then an even more nervous question came into his head.
"Will he... win?"
He asked.
This wasn’t a child doubting his father’s strength, Azarion knew how strong his father was.
What this was, was a child who was afraid of losing his father.
Allura saw that and out of instinct, she tightly held Azarion’s hand and—
"Of course he will."
She answered.
"Have you ever seen him lose?"
She asked with a chuckle.
"I have not."
Azarion answered with a smile and Allura nodded.
The mother and son stayed in that position for a while, Azarion closed his eyes, wanting to sleep on his mother’s lap.
Then, after about a minute—
"I won’t tell them about Father’s fight."
Azarion spoke, keeping his eyes closed.
"They will worry unnecessarily.
They are all children, after all."
"Alright, you do as you see fit."
Allura answered with a light chuckle as she continued lightly patting his head as Azarion drifted into dreamland.
