chapters.title: Chapter 2344: How pathetic.
paragraphs: "Nux, look at this."
Shadow called with a stunned gaze, not saying anything else because her mind had pretty much frozen.

Hearing her words, Nux, who was nearly having a breakdown, turned towards her. No matter his state, his wives mattered to him the most, he would come running even if he were dying, let alone having a mere breakdown.
Knowing that she had his attention, Shadow pointed at the screen in front of her. Nux followed her gaze and that’s when he saw her.
The woman every being in the Universe, even the Infinities, was trying to find, yet none succeeded.
The Seer.
"Nux Leander, you seem to be in a tough position."
The woman spoke with a light, almost playful smile on her face. Her melodious tone had this strange power to erase all the frustration and desperation her listeners were feeling.

Not just Nux, the women standing beside him were the same. They all stared at the screen in front of them with somewhat dazed looks on their faces, while all the tension in their heads was erased and exchanged with... confusion.
What was this woman doing here?
They wondered in their heads.
"She captured one of our men."
Shadow answered that question.
Right now, they had sent millions of beings into the Main Universe to launch an attack against the Infinity Armies.

The War between the Supreme World of Light and the Supreme World of Darkness was over, the differences between the four Infinities were settled, and with Zylarith as the catalyst, the four Infinities were now standing together, facing Anomaly before he became an even bigger threat.
Yes, the official War between the Anomaly and the Supreme Worlds had already started.
And the Supreme Worlds were winning, by a ridiculously huge margin.

Nux’s men stood no chance against the enemy army led by the Supreme Borns. Even when all his men had the ability to revive after being killed, the battle was still not in their favor simply because in the enemy frontlines—
There stood the four Strongest Beings in the Universe.
Yes, the Infinities were participating in the War from the beginning and they were eradicating Nux’s army with an ease that almost felt... elegant.
As for the frontlines of Nux’s Army, the place he was supposed to be—
That was empty.
Because even now, Nux wasn’t sure he could defeat the four Infinities right now and he didn’t wish to take the risk and try finding out.
The worst part?
He couldn’t even bring his army back to his Universe because he feared that if he did that—
The Infinities would follow and once they were in—
It wasn’t just his life that would be in jeopardy, his family would be at risk too. It was something Nux simply couldn’t do.
So all he could do was watch his men die in front of his eyes, watch the enemy tear apart his limbs, coil around him, preparing to choke his children to death.
This was the reason Nux was... in the state he was.
And to think... in a situation like this, this woman had captured one of his men just so she could talk to him.
"What is it that you want?"
Nux took over his puppet’s body and asked directly.
He did not have the time to play her silly games, not right now, not when his children’s lives were at risk.
"Hmm? I took the trouble to come to you even though you are so difficult to reach, and this is how you treat me?"
The Seer chuckled, amused by the situation.
Nux, however, didn’t share that amusement, not one bit.
"Why are you here, Seer?"
Nux asked again.
"Can I not have a little chat?"

Seer laughed, still playing her games. Honestly, Nux wanted to leave his puppet’s body and end the conversation, he was already on edge and the last thing he wanted was to deal with the woman he did not understand, but...
He couldn’t do it.
Too much was at stake here. He was losing on every end and if things continued like this—
Just imagining what would happen brought him to his knees.
He needed a solution, desperately.
And...
As odd as this woman may be, if there was one thing Nux knew, it was that if there was anyone who could help him right now—
It was her.

This was the reason that even when the woman was clearly playing around with him, even when she was enjoying seeing his desperation, and even when therewerechances that she may not even help him or prove to be helpful even if she tried to help—
Nux had no choice but to be here.
To... beg this woman for help if need be.
"You can."

Nux spoke, closing his eyes as if he had given in and hearing his answer, the Seer, for a good few moments, didn’t say anything. It was almost as if she was trying to read him, which made no sense because according to what she said—
She should know everything about him.
Nux, however, didn’t consider any of that, he just waited for her to say anything and she did.
"As I was saying, your situation seems quite bad."
She spoke, looking down, where Nux’s armies were fighting, or more accurately, being dismantled by the enemy.
"I was too arrogant, I bit more than I could chew."
Nux accepted his mistake.
He didn’t know why, but he felt this was the only way he could even hope to get this woman’s help.
"You did."
The Seer nodded.
Nux couldn’t see her eyes but he could tell she was looking at him with this quiet amusement, almost as if... she had predicted this would happen.
The worst part?
He... felt glad when he thought of that possibility.
How pathetic.
He thought inwardly, laughing at himself.

There was a time when he would even hate the thought of another being somehow predicting what he was about to do, but... to think he was now glad that was the case simply because that gave him hope that she might have a way out.
After all, even when she predicted this, this woman came to him, not to the enemy. Even if there was something she wanted from him, wouldn’t she need to offer something in return?
That was how it worked, was it not?
Not to mention...
This woman had once promised him three Gifts on her own.
She had already given him two and he would really appreciate it if the last one came just about now.
And as if she had predicted his thought process as well, the Seer chuckled—
"Don’t worry, I haven’t forgotten about the Gift I promised you."
Nux looked at her in surprise. Yes, this time, he didn’t even bother hiding his expression because, what was the point?
The woman would know it anyways.
"I told you before, you will get your gift when it’s the right time."
"No time’s righter than now."
Nux answered almost instantly.
"Is that so...?"
The Seer muttered, her words almost sounded ominous, but Nux didn’t care, he just nodded.
"Trust me."
"So what is it that you need?"
The Seer asked directly.
"How did they do it? How are the Supreme Worlds predicting my attacks?"
Nux asked.
"Hmm? You want to know that as a gift?"
"If that means I can somehow stop them, then yes."
Nux nodded.
"You wouldn’t be able to."
The Seer shook her head dismissively.
"Then... I want you to help me."
Nux asked directly.
"That’s a lot to ask as a gift, I promised you a gift, not a wish."
The Seer chuckled, clearly enjoying the conversation.
"I will do anything you want if you help me.
You have my word."
Nux declared, then, he paused for a moment and—
"Please, help me."
He begged.
Once again, the Seer turned silent, then, the smile on her face faded away and—
"Do not use the word please in front of me. You should know by now that I am only teasing you for my amusement since I will not receive many chances to do so in the future."
She spoke directly.
Nux didn’t know what to say.
"I need your help."
He just repeated what he said before. His calm, playful, confident outer exterior had already broken. It was... a painful sight, especially for Nux’s women, who were hearing every word he said.
And for some reason—
Seer was the same.
The situation no longer amused her, rather,
"Nux, that is enough."
She spoke in a heavy, strict tone.
"You made a mistake, that was it. It doesn’t mean it has ended.
You should already know I came here to give you your third gift, a gift that will show you a way out of this situation you are in.
So stop acting this weak and stand your ground.
No one you care about is going to die."
She spoke directly and the instant she did, Nux’s expression changed.
Seer, however, didn’t care, she then waved her hand and a piece of ordinary paper appeared in the air, right in front of the being Nux had possessed.
"Take it."
"Is this... my third gift?"
Nux questioned with a silly look on his face.
Seer didn’t say anything, she just gestured Nux to look at it. Nux grabbed the paper and read it.
It was... space coordinates.
"What’s this?"
He asked and without any change in her expression—
"That’s where Zylarith is."

"I will do anything you want if you help me.
You have my word."
Nux declared, then, he paused for a moment and—
"Please, help me."
He begged.
Once again, the Seer turned silent, then, the smile on her face faded away and—
"Do not use the word please in front of me.
You should know by now that I am only teasing you for my amusement since I will not receive many chances to do so in the future."
She spoke directly.
Nux didn’t know what to say.
"I need your help."
He just repeated what he said before.
His calm, playful, confident outer exterior had already broken.
It was... a painful sight, especially for Nux’s women, who were hearing every word he said.
And for some reason—
Seer was the same.
The situation no longer amused her, rather,
"Nux, that is enough."
She spoke in a heavy, strict tone.
"You made a mistake, that was it.
It doesn’t mean it has ended.
You should already know I came here to give you your third gift, a gift that will show you a way out of this situation you are in.
So stop acting this weak and stand your ground.
No one you care about is going to die."
She spoke directly and the instant she did, Nux’s expression changed.
Seer, however, didn’t care, she then waved her hand and a piece of ordinary paper appeared in the air, right in front of the being Nux had possessed.
"Take it."
"Is this... my third gift?"
Nux questioned with a silly look on his face.
Seer didn’t say anything, she just gestured Nux to look at it.
Nux grabbed the paper and read it.
It was... space coordinates.
"What’s this?"
He asked and without any change in her expression—
"That’s where Zylarith is."

chapters.title: Chapter 2345: Then let’s move.
paragraphs: "What’s this?"
Nux asked with a confused look on his face and Seer answered without any change in her tone.
"That’s where Zylarith is."
"Zylarith...?"
Nux’s frown deepened.
"What does he have to do with all this?"

He questioned out loud, more to himself than to Seer, but knowing that Seer would give him the answer much faster than him trying to connect the dots on his own, he looked at her, only to find her body already fading away.
She was leaving, or more accurately, her projection was fading.
"Hey! Wait—!"
Nux tried to stop her, however, before he could say anything anymore—
"Burn that before they see it."
She spoke and the instant she did, Nux froze.
He didn’t have to be a genius to understand who ’they’ she mentioned were.
So that’s it...
Nux nodded inwardly, his mind had started to wonder that even if the Seer wanted to give him the coordinates, why not tell them to him?
Why give him an ordinary paper that would need to be erased out of existence just to erase all its traces?
But now it made sense.

She did it so she could stop him from stopping her. She knew that the instant she told him to burn the paper, he would do it because he couldn’t risk the Infinities knowing the coordinates where he might be at.
And the worst part?
Her plan worked, because Nux stopped and he erased the paper out of existence before he broke his connection with his soldier.
The moment his consciousness returned to his own body, another being appeared in front of his soldier.
A Supreme Born.
He had sensed him from a distance.
Was it a coincidence that he came here just when Nux left?

Nux was sure it wasn’t, it was her. She must have separated the two of them from the Universe using her own way while they were talking, but now that the separation was no longer needed, things returned back to normal or from the Seer’s perspective—
Things returned to how they should be.
For the next few seconds, Nux stayed silent, almost as if he was recalling everything that happened to him in these last few years and assessing his current state of mind.
He, however, wasn’t given more time of his own as—
"Why would she give you his coordinates?"
Sharnoth questioned with a deep frown on her face.
Every time the name Zylarith was mentioned, it unsettled her. As someone who had been manipulated by him almost all her life, the last thing she wanted was to do anything related to him.
But with Seer herself pointing them in his direction...
There wasn’t much she could do other than analyse the situation as thoroughly as she could.

"Does it mean... he knows something? He probably knows what the Infinities have done that has allowed them to predict our attacks. I wouldn’t be surprised if he was the one who came up with the idea in the first place."
Sharnoth guessed.
"That doesn’t make sense."
Aeliana, however, shook her head.

"The Seer said knowing how they stopped us won’t do anything, we cannot undo what has already happened. There should be some other reason. Zylarith must know something we do not, something that... can prove to be helpful in this situation."
"If our assumption is correct, Zylarith was the one who caused all this in the first place, so it wouldn’t be wrong to think that."
Riona nodded, agreeing with Aeliana.
But...
"There might be another reason."
That was when Vyriana spoke up with a hesitant look on her face. The rest of the women turned towards her and frowned.
"What do you mean?"
Riona asked. Vyriana looked at her and answered—
"Zylarith doesn’t exactly have to know something about this particular incident, he would be helpful to us nonetheless."
The Dragon answered and Astaria’s expression changed.
"Are you saying...?"
"Yes."
Vyriana nodded again.
"Zylarith was an Infinity. If Nux devours him, he can upgrade our Universe’s Cultivation Bridge, and once that happens..."
"We would be able to become Infinities..."
Astaria completed those words.
This wasn’t a new plan, the women had come up with it long before, the only problem was that they had no way to get their hands on Zylarith.
But now they did.
"But... we only have three thousand years...
None of us would be able to become an Infinity by then."
Evane frowned.
But—
"No."
Shadow shook her head.
"We don’t just have three thousand years, we can have as many as we desire."
She muttered.
As the Goddess of the Universe, slowing down time while her sisters cultivated wasn’t impossible for her.

They couldn’t freely manipulate time to extend their children’s lives, but that restriction didn’t apply to the women. Their bodies were strong enough to handle the false flow of time without any complications.
"So you are saying... if Nux devours Zylarith, uses his memory to strengthen the Universe’s Cultivation Bridge—
Then we can cultivate while Shadow controls the Flow of Time around us, and once we break through and become Infinities—
We leave the Universe, deal with the Infinities, while Nux devours worlds for our children?"
"Nineteen versus Four, I doubt it would be a battle they would be able to win."
Ember spoke with a dangerous grin.
"Does that mean... by the end of this...
We would be stronger than Nux?"
Vyriana questioned with a playful look on her face.
Nux stared at her with a deadpan expression. To think the woman would joke around during a time like this.
But in his mind—
Even he couldn’t help but believe that it was... at some level... plausible.
Sure, they won’t be able to manipulate time endlessly, but three thousand years could easily be turned into three hundred thousand years and that...
Should be enough for the women to reach that level, or at least... that’s what Nux wanted to believe.
But the thing was—
This plan had quite a few flaws.
Becoming an Infinity wasn’t easy. If it were, there wouldn’t be just Five Infinities in the entire Universe.
Plus, even the Main Universe, a fully grown Universe, could only support five Infinities and no more—
Who was to say that his Universe would be able to support so many?
Honestly, the more he thought about it, the more questions appeared in his head, but the thing was—
He didn’t know a thing about Infinity. All the knowledge he had after devouring tens of thousands of worlds was practically useless when it came to understanding Infinity.
This was the reason he had so many questions in the first place.
What he did know, however, was that the Seer was the one who pointed him in this direction. That meant there must be something he would get out of this situation.
Who knows, once he understands what Infinity is, he himself might find a way to become one?
That was a possibility as well.
So the next step seemed obvious enough.
He needed to go see that Soul Father of his. It was about time he became useful.
But just as Nux was making up his mind—
"What if... this is a trap?"
Amaya spoke up with an uncertain look on her face.
Everyone turned towards her and the woman’s frown deepened—
"We are planning on the assumption that the Seer is on our side. How do we know that?"
She asked, then, she glanced at Nux and—
"Don’t forget, when you first met her, you found her suspicious. There is no reason to trust her blindly.
For all we know, Zylarith might not even be there, or worse, the Seer might be colluding with the Four Infinities and wants to lure Nux out using Zylarith as bait."
"If she wanted to give Nux to the Infinities, she had more than a few chances to do so..."
Lyriana spoke with a light frown.
"What if... she changed her mind right now?"
Amaya asked.
Everyone turned silent.
It wasn’t that they didn’t want to trust Seer, it was just that they were in no position to trust anyone at all, and Seer wasn’t an exception to that rule.
But the question was—
What else could they do?
This was their only way out and they knew that, so—
"Let’s send a puppet."
Nux raised his voice. The women turned towards him and he continued—
"If we move with no intent to devour a world, the Infinities cannot sense us. Zylarith shouldn’t be an exception either.
So I’ll create a puppet with an ability to hide in another dimension, move to the coordinates the Seer gave us and if we see Zylarith there and see no signs of the Infinities—
I will go there myself and trap Zylarith in my domain.
How about it?"

"Once Zylarith is in your domain, the Infinities won’t be able to find him, even if they want to. Then all you would need to do is devour him and since he is merely a Soul, there is no way he would be able to resist you."
Aeliana’s eyes shined with a strong light, liking the plan the more she thought about it. Nux nodded, he glanced at the rest of the women, then at Amaya and this time, even Amaya agreed.
"That should work."
She spoke.
"Then let’s move."
Nux nodded, not wanting to waste even a single instant anymore.

chapters.title: Chapter 2346: Welcome, Father.
paragraphs: In a long, unending, silent void, a thin black line appeared in the middle, and as that black line widened, a being with a ridiculously handsome face, long black hair, and determined golden eyes stepped forward.
And as this being hovered in this unknown space with terrifying calm, he began to observe where he was.
It was not a world, that much was for sure. There was no sky above him, no ground beneath him, no sun, no moon, no water, no wind, nor was there a fixed structure of... anything at all.
His next thought was a dimension, a separate dimension with its own strange structure, but that wasn’t the answer either.
If he had to give it a term or an explanation, then it was...
A forgotten reality.
The being looked around, his golden eyes shining with curiosity, then he expanded his senses, looking for anyone around and...
Just as he expected—
Theyweren’t here.
’It wasn’t a trap.’
He nodded to himself because whiletheyweren’t here,
Hewas.
And that made the being smile.
’So this is where you were hiding.
So this is why not even the Infinities were able to find you.’
He thought inwardly as his senses continued to perceive the... place he was in, if it could even be called a ’place’ in the first place.
Because whatever this was...
It was... different.
Even as he extended his senses, he got no answers.
No world’s energy reacted to his, no ’Laws’ existed here, no life, no death, no time, no space, no beginning, no end.
There was nothing.
Heck, he couldn’t even sense the Universal Energy that was everywhere in the Universe, even in the deepest, unexplored parts of the void.
It was almost as if...
This place was removed from the Universe’s memory.
A place that shouldn’t exist but... did.
And that was where Zylarith Chaosveil was. That was the reason no one could find him.
It was because no one remembered this place even existed.
’Heh.’
Nux laughed inwardly, mostly at how absurd Zylarith’s abilities were and at the same time—
At that woman.
Because even after all this, even when he hid in a place forgotten by the Universe itself, in a place even the Infinities could not find, there he was—
Standing right in front of the coordinates she gave.
Nux didn’t even have to move, he didn’t need to extend his senses, he didn’t have to find him. He was right there—
Right in front of him.
Just...
What sort of existence was she?
He couldn’t help but wonder in his head.
But right now, that didn’t matter.
Because all that mattered right now was him. So without waiting, Nux extended his domain. Dark, inexplicable matter surrounded everything around, includinghim, and just like that—
Zylarith Chaosveil was inside Nux’s Domain.
Nux’s smile widened, his golden eyes shone as his domain was completed, separating him and Zylarith from the Main Universe, from the Infinities.
That was when Zylarith finally reacted.
He, in his Soul Form, turned around and looked at him with a confused, almost surprised look on his face.
He spoke in a... weak voice, almost as if he hadn’t used his true voice for countless years, yet even that weak word made the grey darkness around him tremble.
That, however, wasn’t important, because before he could even complete his question, Nux’s own body disintegrated into nothingness, almost as if its role was complete and it was no longer needed.
Zylarith’s frown deepened, but the next instant, his confusion disappeared and was replaced by understanding.
"A puppet."
He muttered out loud, already getting used to using his own voice and not just talking through different artifacts using his mind.
That was when he heard another voice—
"That is correct."
The voice echoed throughout the space, coming from every single direction, but that didn’t confuse Zylarith. He simply turned in a particular direction, and there he was—
Nux Leander, standing right in front of him, with that same calm but arrogant smile on his face.
"Welcome, Father."
Zylarith narrowed his eyes, the mist around him twisting.
He stared at Nux for a long time, almost as if his mind couldn’t process what was happening. Nux didn’t rush him either.
This was his Universe.
No other force could interfere with them.
And as strange as stating this felt, Nux now had time.
Time for a long overdue, heartfelt conversation with his dear Soul Father.
So for a while, the two beings stared at each other, Nux with a silent smile and Zylarith with a confused frown.
Then, about two seconds later—
Zylarith laughed out loud.
"You came."
He spoke, his unstable Soul Form shifting.
"After all this time...
You finally came to see me."
"You sound pleased."
Nux answered calmly.
"I am."
Zylarith’s smile widened.
"Do you know how boring it is to... exist like this?"
He muttered, his Soul body shifting again.
"To be alive, yet unable to breathe. To possess power, yet unable to release even a thread of it. To know that the moment I release myself, the Universe will remember my Soul and rush to devour me."
He commented as his Soul body finally began to take... a shape Nux could make some sense of.
It wasn’t a physical body, that much was obvious. The instability was still there, but it was still different from that translucent, generic form that he had always used.

Now, it was a taller figure, made of dark, shifting smoke and broken purple light. Even now, its edges were never still. Sometimes it looked like a human, sometimes it looked like a shadow stretched in different directions.
As he became more and more complete, pure Energy of Chaos coiled around him, as if it had been waiting for its true owner for trillions of years.
This was Zylarith Chaosveil, the being who accepted Chaos and became one with it.
*Picture*
"To be the strongest Infinity...
And be reduced to silence."
Zylarith commented, finally getting accustomed to... talking.
Nux watched him, and Zylarith did the same. Then, what looked like his face smiled as he looked around—
"You really have become an entity I cannot understand.
To think you managed to take me... outside the Universe."
He commented, then he looked around with a curious look on his face and—
"Is this it? Is this the other Universe they say you are a part of?"
He questioned. Soon, however, a frown appeared on his face and—
"No."
He shook his head.
"This is not a Universe.
It is... a dimension that is connected to that Universe but has no way to actually visit the Universe."
Zylarith looked at Nux again.
"Why not bring me to your main Universe?"
He wondered out loud. Then, his expression changed and the violet light in his eyes shone.
"Those women."
He commented.
"They are there."
And Nux’s expression broke. It was only for the slightest instant, but an old monster like Zylarith, no matter how long he had been ’asleep’ for, wouldn’t possibly miss it.
"You did not change."
He almost seemed disappointed.
"You have the same weakness you always did."
"They are not my weakness."
Nux answered almost instantly, his old hatred for Zylarith returning in an instant. Zylarith didn’t care. He just shook his head.
"They are.
More than you realize.
They gave away what you were trying to hide the hardest."
Nux narrowed his eyes and Zylarith continued—
"You have somehow become part of another Universe, but your Universe is weak. There is no being in there who can face Infinities, who can defend your wives from me—
You are probably the strongest being in there.
This is also how you managed to become its Absolute God.
That is quite an achievement, but since even someone like you managed to become that Universe’s God, that means either your Universe’s Infinities are dead—
Or the one that is more likely—
Your Universe is new."
Zylarith pointed out.
This time, Nux didn’t react to his words, but Zylarith no longer needed his reaction to confirm what he was saying. He already knew he was correct.
"This is why you are preventing me or any other Infinity from entering your Universe, because you know that if we came in, your Universe wouldn’t be able to resist.
It will fall under our pressure. We will become its true rulers, putting yours and your wives’ lives in our hands."
Again, Nux remained silent.
And his silence only amused Zylarith even further.

"You did quite well, considering the cards you were dealt. You put Seraphielle in a difficult position, forcing her to go to war with Ul’Thakar. You even made Equarios and Orravyn freeze, when all they needed to do was move, enter your Universe, and everything would have been theirs for the taking.
You played them like fools.
Not that it was a difficult task, considering it was them, but you still did it—
And for that, I praise you.
I just... don’t understand one thing."
Zylarith tilted his head.
"Why come to me?"
But soon, he changed his question—
"How did you even find me?"

Nux didn’t even have to move, he didn’t need to extend his senses, he didn’t have to find him.
He was right there—
Right in front of him.
Just...
What sort of existence was she?
He couldn’t help but wonder in his head.
But right now, that didn’t matter.
Because all that mattered right now was him.
So without waiting, Nux extended his domain.
Dark, inexplicable matter surrounded everything around, includinghim, and just like that—
Zylarith Chaosveil was inside Nux’s Domain.
Nux’s smile widened, his golden eyes shone as his domain was completed, separating him and Zylarith from the Main Universe, from the Infinities.
That was when Zylarith finally reacted.
He, in his Soul Form, turned around and looked at him with a confused, almost surprised look on his face.
He spoke in a... weak voice, almost as if he hadn’t used his true voice for countless years, yet even that weak word made the grey darkness around him tremble.
That, however, wasn’t important, because before he could even complete his question, Nux’s own body disintegrated into nothingness, almost as if its role was complete and it was no longer needed.
Zylarith’s frown deepened, but the next instant, his confusion disappeared and was replaced by understanding.
"A puppet."
He muttered out loud, already getting used to using his own voice and not just talking through different artifacts using his mind.
That was when he heard another voice—
"That is correct."
The voice echoed throughout the space, coming from every single direction, but that didn’t confuse Zylarith.
He simply turned in a particular direction, and there he was—
Nux Leander, standing right in front of him, with that same calm but arrogant smile on his face.
"Welcome, Father."
Zylarith narrowed his eyes, the mist around him twisting.
He stared at Nux for a long time, almost as if his mind couldn’t process what was happening.
Nux didn’t rush him either.
This was his Universe.
No other force could interfere with them.
And as strange as stating this felt, Nux now had time.
Time for a long overdue, heartfelt conversation with his dear Soul Father.
So for a while, the two beings stared at each other, Nux with a silent smile and Zylarith with a confused frown.
Then, about two seconds later—
Zylarith laughed out loud.
"You came."
He spoke, his unstable Soul Form shifting.
"After all this time...
You finally came to see me."
"You sound pleased."
Nux answered calmly.
"I am."
Zylarith’s smile widened.
"Do you know how boring it is to... exist like this?"
He muttered, his Soul body shifting again.
"To be alive, yet unable to breathe.
To possess power, yet unable to release even a thread of it.
To know that the moment I release myself, the Universe will remember my Soul and rush to devour me."
He commented as his Soul body finally began to take... a shape Nux could make some sense of.
It wasn’t a physical body, that much was obvious.
The instability was still there, but it was still different from that translucent, generic form that he had always used.
Now, it was a taller figure, made of dark, shifting smoke and broken purple light.
Even now, its edges were never still.
Sometimes it looked like a human, sometimes it looked like a shadow stretched in different directions.
As he became more and more complete, pure Energy of Chaos coiled around him, as if it had been waiting for its true owner for trillions of years.
This was Zylarith Chaosveil, the being who accepted Chaos and became one with it.
*Picture*
"To be the strongest Infinity...
And be reduced to silence."
Zylarith commented, finally getting accustomed to... talking.
Nux watched him, and Zylarith did the same.
Then, what looked like his face smiled as he looked around—
"You really have become an entity I cannot understand.
To think you managed to take me... outside the Universe."
He commented, then he looked around with a curious look on his face and—
"Is this it?
Is this the other Universe they say you are a part of?"
He questioned.
Soon, however, a frown appeared on his face and—
"No."
He shook his head.
"This is not a Universe.
It is... a dimension that is connected to that Universe but has no way to actually visit the Universe."
Zylarith looked at Nux again.
"Why not bring me to your main Universe?"
He wondered out loud.
Then, his expression changed and the violet light in his eyes shone.
"Those women."
He commented.
"They are there."
And Nux’s expression broke.
It was only for the slightest instant, but an old monster like Zylarith, no matter how long he had been ’asleep’ for, wouldn’t possibly miss it.
"You did not change."
He almost seemed disappointed.
"You have the same weakness you always did."
"They are not my weakness."
Nux answered almost instantly, his old hatred for Zylarith returning in an instant.
Zylarith didn’t care.
He just shook his head.
"They are.
More than you realize.
They gave away what you were trying to hide the hardest."
Nux narrowed his eyes and Zylarith continued—
"You have somehow become part of another Universe, but your Universe is weak.
There is no being in there who can face Infinities, who can defend your wives from me—
You are probably the strongest being in there.
This is also how you managed to become its Absolute God.
That is quite an achievement, but since even someone like you managed to become that Universe’s God, that means either your Universe’s Infinities are dead—
Or the one that is more likely—
Your Universe is new."
Zylarith pointed out.
This time, Nux didn’t react to his words, but Zylarith no longer needed his reaction to confirm what he was saying.
He already knew he was correct.
"This is why you are preventing me or any other Infinity from entering your Universe, because you know that if we came in, your Universe wouldn’t be able to resist.
It will fall under our pressure.
We will become its true rulers, putting yours and your wives’ lives in our hands."
Again, Nux remained silent.
And his silence only amused Zylarith even further.
"You did quite well, considering the cards you were dealt.
You put Seraphielle in a difficult position, forcing her to go to war with Ul’Thakar.
You even made Equarios and Orravyn freeze, when all they needed to do was move, enter your Universe, and everything would have been theirs for the taking.
You played them like fools.
Not that it was a difficult task, considering it was them, but you still did it—
And for that, I praise you.
I just... don’t understand one thing."
Zylarith tilted his head.
"Why come to me?"
But soon, he changed his question—
"How did you even find me?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2347: The weakest Infinity
paragraphs: "Why come to me?"
Zylarith asked, soon however, he changed his question to something else.
"How did you even find me?"

Again, Nux didn’t say anything and once again, to Zylarith, that didn’t matter. He was trillions of years old, the amount of information in his head made it difficult for any being to hide something from him—
Even Nux was no exception to that.
Because even as Nux hadn’t said a word since they met, Zylarith was already thinking of an answer and—
He got it.
"The Seer."
He spoke in realization. Nux didn’t show any reaction, but Zylarith was sure, and he didn’t seem offended, instead, he looked amused.
"So she finally moved."
"You know her."
Nux asked, trying to take back some control in the conversation.
"I know many things, child."
Zylarith chuckled softly.
"I know many people who think they know many things."
Nux shot back, but to Zylarith, this was just the action of a petty child trying to win a fight he wouldn’t.
"Why would she helpyouthough...?"
He thought inwardly. Nux did not matter, his secrets were already out, the Seer however, was trouble, even for him.
The only being even he couldn’t completely understand all his life.
The being with whom he, in the past, had... quite the connection with.
"What can I say? I am quite charming."
Nux chuckled, trying to get a reaction out of Zylarith but—
"You are even bigger of a fool than I thought if you believe she is helping you because you arecharming."
Zylarith just laughed, not giving any other important reaction.
Nux stayed silent.

Honestly, Zylarith’s question always bothered him too, now, more than ever. Why would the Seer help him? He obviously didn’t believe the answer he gave to Zylarith, he wasn’t that foolish, but the lack of an answer troubled him too—
Not that it mattered right now.
"You too."
Nux commented as he stopped thinking about it.
"For a being who is supposedly trillions of years old, your instincts are quite... weak. Or maybe it is because you are trillions of years old that your instincts have rusted? Hmm?
Who knows?
But for a being whose death is right in front of him, you are quite calm.
Foolishly calm."
"My death?"
Zylarith actually seemed surprised.
"My... death?"
He repeated.
Then he laughed.
"You should not have brought me here."
Zylarith looked at him and continued—
"At least the Main Universe was a place where neither of us could raise our hands. The Universe treats you like an enemy and it treats me like a soul that should not exist.
Both of us were tied down, neither of us could make a move, meaning neither of us could hurt each other—
But now?"
Zylarith paused for a moment.
Then, maybe out of the kindness of his heart—
"You do realize this little dimension of yours is not a prison for me, correct?"
He asked, making sure this child actually knew what he was doing.
And Nux—
He looked at him and his golden eyes shined.
Of course he knew that.
He didn’t directly come here after talking to Seer, he had gone to Azriel, and after talking with him, he had made an active decision.
"I know."
Nux answered.
Zylarith laughed.
"So you knew what would happen the moment you brought me outside of my Universe’s influence?"
He asked, just to be sure.
"I did."
Nux nodded.
"You knew what was going to happen when my Soul was no longer under the Universe’s scrutiny?"
"I did."
"You knew that the moment I was out, I would be able to use my Law, without anything holding me back?"
He asked again, this time, Nux looked at him calmly, then—
"That was the point."
Nux answered and the space around Zylarith trembled as more and more Chaos Energy gathered around him.
"So this is why you came to me."
Zylarith realized it, his violet eyes shined with a cruel light.
"You thought out of all the Infinities, I was the easiest to defeat because I no longer have my Physical Body."
"Exactly."
Nux nodded.
And he wasn’t lying.
That was the reason he targeted Zylarith.
He always knew Zylarith would be freed the moment he brought him here, so when he tried to devour him and when Zylarith fought back—
Nux always knew he wouldn’t just be facing a being who could no longer use his strength, he would face a being who was once called the Strongest Infinity.
Then why do something so dangerous knowingly?
Why choose the most difficult opponent of all?
Because while Zylarith may have been the Strongest Infinity at some point, right now, that was not the case.

Right now, Zylarith did not have a Physical Body, all he had was his Law. Not to mention, if he ever required, he could always deactivate his domain, return to the Universe, binding Zylarith again while he himself returned to the Universe before the Universe could do anything to him.
He had an escape plan ready, even before the battle began.
This was the reason Nux took the risk.
And for the first time since he brought him here, Zylarith lost his composure—
"So that’s what it is..."
He spoke, his voice becoming colder and colder.
"Theeasiest to defeathuh..."
Zylarith’s purple eyes now shined ruthlessly as he glared at Nux and—
"Then allow me to show you—
What mistake you have just made."
That was when it happened—
BOOOOOOOM
Zylarith released his energy, the void around him trembled violently, the Laws inside Nux’s dimension groaned, almost as if something was tearing them apart.
Nux noticed that change instantly and he narrowed his eyes.
He raised his head, almost as if commanding the Universe to tame the outsider who had just activated his powers inside it—
And it did.
A pressure Zylarith did not understand fell on him, trying to suppress him, trying to detain him, trying to... push him out of existence.
But—
"Heh."
Zylarith simply laughed and the pressure around him disappeared like it had never existed.
Nux’s face turned solemn.
He failed.
While his Universe couldcontainZylarith, his existence was... too large, too strong, for him to...commandhim.
That was when Zylarith made his first move.

A thin strand of violet-black light appeared above his palm, it twisted, it broke, and it reformed, becoming fire, water, then a bone, then a strange, hollow screaming face, a beautiful flower, then... nothing.
Then it happened all at once.
It was as if... Zylarith was testing his powers...
And the moment he realized the Chaos was reacting to him, that it was moving exactly like he wanted it to—
His grin widened even further.
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
Nux’s dimension trembled violently, the strand above Zylarith’s hand exploded in every direction as reality itself... began to distort.
Then, for some odd reason, the anger on Zylarith’s face disappeared and was replaced with a smile, almost as if...
Zylarith no longer saw Nux as an opponent after testing his power, to him, Nux was now... a source of entertainment.
"Do you know the difference between an Eternity and an Infinity?"
He asked with a curious look on his face.

Nux did not answer, he just stared at him in silence, prompting him to continue, after all, this was the reason he had brought him here in the first place, so he could let go and tell him the secrets he did not know.
Secrets no one else could tell him.
Zylarith knew that as well, he knew Nux was only acting like this because he needed answers, but it simply did not matter—
In his mind, the battle was already over.

So the least he could do here was entertain himself as long as he could, so he gave Nux what he wanted, after all, this was the least he could do for a child who had brought an entire Universe in his hands.
"An Eternity creates a Domain—"
Zylarith began as the space around him twisted because too much Chaos Energy had gathered around him.
"—because he needs walls.
A boundary where they can become Absolute.
A room.
A throne."
Zylarith then smiled and—
"Or a cage."
His voice then deepened and—
"But an Infinity..."

The entire dimension went silent as Zylarith’s form expanded, not physically, conceptually. His presence seeped into the void around him, into the light, the darkness, the laws and the empty spaces between them.
Nux recognized it instantly.
The Body of Chaos.
Only far more advanced, far more terrifying than Sharnoth’s.
"An Infinity does not need a Domain."
Zylarith’s voice came from everywhere.
"An Infinity does not need a Throne to rule, they do not need a clear Boundary to call themselves mighty.
For them—
Reality itself is enough."
He explained and Nux’s body tensed as he sensed the changes in the void around him. It was still dark, it was still his Universe, everything was still in his control, but...
Zylarith’s presence, his... Chaos...
Was now everywhere.
"Allow me to show you, Nux Leander."
Zylarith’s voice came again.
"What theweakest Infinity, the Infinity of Chaos, is."

chapters.title: Chapter 2348: So this Universe strengthens you.
paragraphs: "Allow me to show you, Nux Leander.
What theweakest Infinity, the Infinity of Chaos, is."
Zylarith’s voice came from every single direction, echoing right into Nux’s head. Nux expanded his senses, trying to keep control of the battlefield, but it was already too late—
Zylarith lowered his hand and the space between them folded.
Nux understood it—
The distance that separated them lost its meaning.
Zylarith’s only weakness, his Soul Form, which did not have the durability his normal body did, was now untouchable because the distance separating them was infinite.
Nux’s frown deepened.
Again, he hadn’t come here without preparation, he had talked with Azriel, he had learned what an Infinity was.

While Eternals and other beings created domains, an Infinity was a being whose understanding of their Law had surpassed the need for a Domain. Unlike an Eternal, who must create a Domain to gain absolute control within a limited space, an Infinity could impose their Law directly upon reality itself.
Anything that their Law could define, touch, interpret, or claim—
It became subject to their absolute authority.
This was also the reason Nux did not understand it—
Zylarith had power over Chaos, his Absolute Authority should be related to Chaos, Space should not be a part of it—
Then...
How was he manipulating space itself?
"Chaos is everywhere."
That was when Zylarith’s voice sounded again.
Nux’s dimension screamed, almost as if it was being ripped apart, while Zylarith continued with the same leisure as he raised his finger—
"Anything with order..."
Then he raised another finger.
"Anything with structure, anything with sequence, direction, purpose, form, meaning, memory, rule, or even name..."
Then, his smile widened—
"It is mine to ruin."
Nux didn’t care.
Zylarith was clearly drunk on power, so he needed to use this chance to devour him, now and here, before he became serious and made all this more difficult than it should be.
He used the Power over Space and appeared right in front of Zylarith, then, he punched.
BOOOOOM

Right now, Nux was inside his Universe, this was where he was at his strongest, his physical strength that was reinforced by thousands of worlds that he had devoured was more than enough to shatter even a High Level World in an instant—
It was a force strong enough to hurt even a Complete Infinity, let alone an Infinity that no longer had his physical body.
Yes, Nux was going straight for the kill but—
But the moment his fist moved, the distance between them changed again, Nux, who had teleported across infinite distance and was merely a step away from Zylarith—
Now, he was ten steps away.
Then a thousand.
Then he appeared beside Zylarith again, then behind... himself, then his location changed again—
With no pattern, no comprehensible understanding.
BOOOOM
His punch passed through empty air, destroying the space around it without hurting Zylarith one bit.
Zylarith, on the other hand, did not move an inch, he only looked at him with amusement.
"Did you not hear what I said?
Direction is order.
I can do with it what I please."
He spoke like a master teaching his disciple.
Nux didn’t say anything, he used the Space Law, preparing to repeat the same move again, Zylarith however, simply tilted his head and the space around Nux twisted.
Near became far.
Far became inside.
Inside became above.
Above became... nowhere.
Nux’s body vanished like he intended, but he did not appear where he wanted, he appeared somewhere else, somewhere random.
Zylarith saw that and smiled.
"Space is order too."
Nux’s face turned grim, he raised his hand, the Time flow in his dimension changed, everything slowed down, the space that was still twisted because of Zylarith’s sick power froze—
Nux stepped through the frozen moment and punched again.
For a moment, his fist almost reached Zylarith’s face, he was so close that even he had begun to believe that this one might connect.
But—
Just then, Zylarith’s eyes flashed.
The frozen time cracked, the cause and effect were reversed. The ’before’ and ’after’ changed places. He did ’punch’, but by the time the ’impact’ came, Zylarith was somewhere else.
Zylarith laughed.
"So is Time."
Nux looked at him, his expression now even more solemn. Zylarith looked back with the same confident smile.

Again, never once since this all began did he doubt his ability to win, even now, he believed that if he wanted, he could end Nux anytime he desired, but he just... allowed his child to play whatever games he desired, to use whatever moves he had collected, to show his father the progress he had made so far.
That was it—
That was all Zylarith was doing.
Nux could see it as well and he clenched his fists in anger and... humiliation. Still, he didn’t let his emotions get the better of him, not at a time like this.
He wanted to see Zylarith’s limits, if he even had any. So he did what he was best at, he continued to move.
This time, as he raised his hand, a black-red force formed around his fingers, the Energy of Destruction.
BOOOOOOOOOOM
The Energy moved towards Zylarith with the purpose of erasing him but—
"Purpose... is order too."
He commented as he watched the Energy of Destruction come, then, it stopped, trembled, and turned... inward.
The power that was meant to destroy Zylarith began destroying its own reason to exist.
It collapsed into itself and... vanished.
Nux’s eyes turned colder, the next Energy he used was the opposite of Chaos, Balance.
A vast and bright silver scale formed behind him, the chaotic space around him steadied, the twisted time returned to normal but—
"Using the only force that should be able to contain Chaos, huh?"
Zylarith’s eyes shined in amusement.
"Have you forgotten who I am?
If my power could have been suppressed by mere Balance, it wouldn’t have taken four Infinities to stop me, Equarios alone would have been enough.
But he wasn’t.
Equarios wasn’t enough—"
Zylarith then looked right at Nux and—
"What made you think you would be?"
He questioned with a mocking gaze and suddenly—
The silver scale behind Nux tilted, not to the left or the right—
It tilted in a direction that did not exist.
Balance began balancing the wrong things. Nux’s movement was balanced against stillness, his will was balanced against hesitation, and his very existence was balanced against... rejection.
For a brief moment, Nux’s body became heavy, so much that his head tilted forward, like he was bowing to Zylarith.
Zylarith’s smile deepened, he liked seeing the arrogant boy bow his head in front of him—
"That look suits yo—"
He tried to laugh, but Nux’s golden eyes shined intensely and he—
He stepped forward under all that weight.
BOOOM
The scale behind him shattered, his strength alone crushed the effect the scale had on him and that made Zylarith raise his eyebrow.
Nux, on the other hand, started walking towards him like a predator, his eyes burning with a hungry, overpowering light.
The laws around him screamed, Space twisted, Time cracked, Destruction lost purpose, Balance betrayed itself, yet—
He kept walking.

Inside, his body was being torn apart, blood came out of his mouth before vanishing, his bones were forced to remember how they were broken in the past, his muscles were told they had no direction to move, his organs were dragged into different states, dead, alive, burning, freezing—

The pressure that the Chaos around him had built on him was enough to crush armies of Eternals, or even affect an Infinity. Zylarith remembered using this exact method to stop Seraphielle from closing the distance between them, yet...
Nux did not stop, he glared at Zylarith as he kept taking one step after another forward.
Zylarith watched him, his amusement slowly starting to change into... interest.
"You are strong."
He had to admit it.
A move that stopped even an Infinity, he was taking it head-on, through sheer physical strength.
It was something Zylarith had never seen before.
Even Ul’Thakar, who was the strongest Infinity when it came to pure, raw Physical Strength, couldn’t do what Nux was doing right now.
"How?"
Zylarith couldn’t help but wonder out loud.
And Nux—
He just grinned.
"You have no idea who you are up against, do you?"

He spoke, his bloodied mouth and burning eyes only making him look scarier. Not that Zylarith seemed particularly scared, he was simply trying to understand how Nux, who clearly wasn’t an Infinity, was holding his own.
And that was when his mind came up with a theory—
"So this Universe strengthens you."
He smiled.
"Since you are its God, you must have a way to use some of its strength, this was the reason you brought me here.
You truly believed you had what it takes to defeat me just because in here, your physical strength is slightly higher than normal Infinities.
That is quite commendable."
He praised.
But the next second, he laughed out loud.
"Also quite foolish."
Nux narrowed his eyes, Zylarith, on the other hand, just grinned.
"Allow me to show you why."

Zylarith’s voice came from every single direction, echoing right into Nux’s head.
Nux expanded his senses, trying to keep control of the battlefield, but it was already too late—
Zylarith lowered his hand and the space between them folded.
Nux understood it—
The distance that separated them lost its meaning.
Zylarith’s only weakness, his Soul Form, which did not have the durability his normal body did, was now untouchable because the distance separating them was infinite.

While Eternals and other beings created domains, an Infinity was a being whose understanding of their Law had surpassed the need for a Domain.

Anything that their Law could define, touch, interpret, or claim—
It became subject to their absolute authority.
This was also the reason Nux did not understand it—
Zylarith had power over Chaos, his Absolute Authority should be related to Chaos, Space should not be a part of it—
Then...
How was he manipulating space itself?
"Chaos is everywhere."
That was when Zylarith’s voice sounded again.
Nux’s dimension screamed, almost as if it was being ripped apart, while Zylarith continued with the same leisure as he raised his finger—
"Anything with order..."
Then he raised another finger.
"Anything with structure, anything with sequence, direction, purpose, form, meaning, memory, rule, or even name..."
Then, his smile widened—
"It is mine to ruin."
Nux didn’t care.
Zylarith was clearly drunk on power, so he needed to use this chance to devour him, now and here, before he became serious and made all this more difficult than it should be.

Yes, Nux was going straight for the kill but—

Now, he was ten steps away.
Then a thousand.
Then he appeared beside Zylarith again, then behind... himself, then his location changed again—

chapters.title: Chapter 2349: Your Universe values you more than I thought.
paragraphs: "That is quite commendable.
Also quite foolish."
Nux narrowed his eyes, Zylarith, on the other hand, just grinned.
"Allow me to show you how."
He spoke as he raised his hand and just then—
Reality itself screamed.
The dimension began to twist, the void trembled violently, his surroundings now covered with dense Chaos Energy, ready to pounce on him and devour him whole.
Nux stood in the middle of it all, his golden eyes fixed on Zylarith, who was still smiling at him.
"Don’t die."
Zylarith spoke, then, he lowered his hand and the world around Nux changed.
His body froze.
Zylarith didn’t stop time, neither did he trap him inside space, he did not have that power, what he had however, was far worse.
Something inside Nux’s body began to... go wrong.

His bones trembled, then they shifted, for one instant, his skeleton forgot its own shape, his spine bent in a direction it should not have been able to bend. His ribs moved apart as if they had never been connected. His arm twisted because the very meaning of "arm" was disturbed.

Nux’s body shivered in agony, but never once did Nux let that pain come out of him in the form of a scream. He suppressed it all, and even as his face turned pale, he continued to glare at Zylarith, while at the same time, trying to understand what was happening to him.
"Heh."
Zylarith grinned.
He knew Nux was in pain, he knew he was suppressing it, to not give him the satisfaction of seeing him scream.
So he accepted the challenge.
"Let’s see how long it takes me to make you scream."
He waved his hand again and—
CRACK
A sharp crack rang out from inside Nux’s body.
His eyes turned red from pain, but he didn’t scream, but Zylarith wasn’t done either. He continued to wave his hand like a concertmaster and—
CRACK
CRACK
CRACK
Those loud, agonizing cracks echoed throughout the Universe, again and again and again.
Nux’s bones were moving in angles they had never moved in before, but Nux too, was someone who had trained with Vyriana, pain from broken, twisted bones was something he was familiar with.
But the issue was—
Zylarith could see that as well.

So he changed his methods, now, he didn’t just target his bones, he started targeting his blood, he stopped it from flowing forward and reversed its flow, then, he made it flow in different directions at the same time, some of it rushed toward his heart, some rushed away from it, some froze inside his veins, some just burned, some turned so heavy that his vessels burst.
Zylarith was messing with his body in a way that shouldn’t even be possible.
"Khawwrrkkk!!!"
Nux spat blood.
But that spat-out blood did not fall either—
It rose.
Then it scattered into red mist before returning to his mouth and forcing itself back inside, turning Nux’s face red, while his body shivered in pain he had never experienced before.
"Ughh."
He groaned, barely stopping himself from screaming.
Zylarith watched him with the same smile, then—
"Body is order."
He commented coldly.
Nux’s muscles tightened, his nerves exploded with pain, some of the pain did not even come from wounds he had, they came from wounds that had not happened yet.
Burns, stabs, force strong enough to crush his body, pressure directly on the soul, all of them arrived at once.
"Aagh..."
Nux’s body shook, he let out a light scream, so low that only he could hear it.

His skin split open, blood ran down his arms, chest, neck, and face. His healing kicked in, closing his wounds, but that only worsened the torture as Zylarith simply opened them again, this time, with even more precision, with... even more pain.
"Aaghhh..."
Nux screamed, this time, somewhat louder, still not enough to satisfy Zylarith.
That was a groan, not a scream.

So Zylarith twisted his organs, his heart forgot its rhythm, his lungs forgot how to breathe, his stomach forgot its place, his eyes started seeing what was behind him, his ears began hearing what was happening inside his body, his skin felt like it was being burned and frozen at the same time.
Chaos was one of the strongest Primordial Forces, one of the most dangerous ones, what it could do to one body was far, far scarier than what most people understood.
This was also the reason Zylarith was as feared as he once was, even the other Infinities wouldn’t let him have this level of control over their own bodies.
After all, with everything that was happening—
Their body would have simply stopped being... a body.
For any other being, even an Infinity, let alone letting out a scream, this would have been a direct end.
But not for Nux.
Because even as he was subjected to this torture, even as his head lowered, even as blood dripped from his mouth while his body inside was turned into a mess that couldn’t even be understood—
His eyes burned so strongly that it looked terrifying, so much so that for a moment, even Zylarith narrowed his eyes.
That was when, against all odds, Nux stood up and once again, he began walking forward.
Zylarith waved his hand—
CRACK
Nux’s left leg bent wrongly, the bone inside it snapped, twisted, and tried to tear away from the rest of his body, but Nux, with his eyes still on Zylarith—
CRACK
He forced it straight with another crack, then, he took another step.
Zylarith tried to reverse his blood again, Nux used sheer force to pump his heart and set the flow straight again, even if it meant bursting some of his veins.
Just like that, Nux, forcing himself through all that pain and his eyes still on Zylarith—
Forced his body straight.
"You didn’t scream."
He admitted.
"That went beyond my expectation.
Your Universe values you more than I thought."
Nux, without saying anything, wiped the blood from his lips with the back of his hand.
His skin was still being torn apart, his body was still being attacked from within, but his eyes never left Zylarith, glaring at him as he forced his broken legs to balance his weight.
"That body is not merely strong. It is not even a body in the normal sense."
Zylarith commented, studying Nux like he was a test subject.

Nux couldn’t care less, he just moved and this time, he did not rely on Space or Time, he pushed his body forward through sheer Might, his speed tore through the distorted reality and he appeared right in front of Zylarith, surprising even him.
Zylarith tried to break the concept of direction again, forward became backward, left became below, near became impossibly far, but to Nux and his physical strength, none of it mattered—
He pushed through it all, cracking the space around him through sheer force, forcing the distorted direction to accept him and—
BOOOOOOOOM
He punched.
The ridiculously strong force scattered Zylarith’s body into dust, that would have been the end of the battle but—
Zylarith’s Soul Form scattered like smoke, the enormous force passed through him, ripping through the empty space behind Zylarith.
"Interesting..."
Zylarith commented.
Then, the sheer force that Nux had released, that was travelling in the form of a shockwave, turned back, Chaos in the void had caught it and changed its shape into black-violet spears.
Nux’s expression changed as those spears dashed towards him, he tried to move away, but the Space around him was distorted, Time Flow was a mess, and his body... it couldn’t move as quickly.
Pierce Pierce Pierce Pierce
The spears struck his chest, shoulders, stomach, and legs, piercing into his flesh. Nux was pushed back three steps.
"Ughh..."
He groaned in pain as direct Chaos made an even stronger mess inside his body, he looked down at the spears buried in him, gritted his teeth from pain and then—
He clenched his muscles and...
Shatter
The spears shattered.
Zylarith reformed above the battlefield as if nothing had happened and that encounter alone was enough for Nux to realize it—
Physical Force did not work on him.
He noted it down.
Zylarith was doing the same, his eyes were studying Nux with even greater interest—
"To be able to keep advancing even when movement itself rejects you."
Again, Nux did not react—
He disappeared.

Zylarith frowned, not expecting him to move right this instant, his eons of experience told him that even the strongest of warriors needed some time to gather themselves after suffering through such agonizing pain.
But Nux didn’t.
This time, he used Space and Time together. The dark battlefield folded, Nux reached Zylarith instantly.
Or at least...
He should have.
But the next instant, Zylarith raised one finger and—
"Sequence."
Time broke.
Nux arrived before he moved, then he moved after he arrived, then the arrival itself lost its place.
The Space opened in ten different directions, and Nux’s body was dragged into all of them at once.
His right arm appeared above Zylarith.
His left leg appeared behind him.
His torso remained below.
His head flickered between three positions.
For an instant, Nux was scattered all across broken space.
And Zylarith—
His eyes watched it all with the same cold interest.
"Position."
He commented as the Space collapsed.
All the separated parts of Nux’s body were forced back together violently—
"Khawwrrrkkkk!!!"
Blood came out of his mouth.

chapters.title: Chapter 2350: You are... strange.
paragraphs: "Khawwrrrkkkk!!!"
Blood came out of his mouth, his bones screamed, but his eyes did not.
This time, he fought back.
Bright Golden Light erupted from his Body, filling the entire dimension, at the same time, Darkness spread beneath it—
The Light burned away the Chaos Energy.
The Darkness hid Nux’s presence inside it.
Together, they formed a strange battlefield where Zylarith’s senses should have been blinded and confused and Nux should have vanished inside it.
But—
"You do not get it, do you?
Even Light and Darkness themselves are no different—
They too, have a certain order, a certain structure to them—
And that allows me to ruin them."
Zylarith smiled and the next instant, the blinding Light suddenly betrayed Nux, it no longer blinded Zylarith, instead, it showed him everything.
Nux’s position, his breathing, his wounds, everything.
The Darkness was no different, what was hiding him suddenly swallowed every other space Nux could have hidden in, leaving only one clear shadow behind and...
Nux’s body was pushed out of that Shadow.
He was completely out in the open, with a broken body and Zylarith?
He was already waiting with a violet spear that directly pierced through Nux’s stomach.
Pierce
"Guhh..."
Nux grunted in pain, he grabbed the spear to pull it out, but the spear turned into a chain that bit his palm.
"Fuckk!"
Nux cursed out loud as he crushed the chain through sheer pressure, he punched towards Zylarith in desperation, this time, from a distance.
The force travelled in a shockwave embarrassingly slowly, Zylarith watched it with interest and—
"Trying to buy time?
You didn’t have to.
Just fall on your knees and ask for it, I’ll grant you an hour to recover."
He mocked as his body simply scattered, making the punch basically useless.
Or at least—
That was what Zylarith thought would happen.
But this time—
The shockwave didn’t just contain pure physical force, this time, it carried the black, vile Energy of Death, an Energy Zylarith didn’t notice until it was too late.
His scattered Soul Form moved away, but the Death Energy grazed one single fragment.
Yes, only one out of countless fragments Zylarith’s body had scattered into, the effect should have been small, almost negligible.
But the moment Zylarith reformed his body and his senses returned to him—
Zylarith flinched, his face changed, his eyes widened for a fraction of a second as he felt an agonizing pain enough to make most beings break down that very instant.
But Zylarith didn’t.
He didn’t even let out a sound, or at least, he tried not to, but in the end—
"Hap!"
A short, sharp breath escaped his mouth, something most warriors would have ignored.
But not Nux.
He noticed and the moment he did, that same bloodied grin appeared on his face again—
"Just as I thought."
He commented.
Zylarith’s expression became cold, but Nux didn’t stop.
"Your Soul Form is just that... your Soul.
That means your body is currently thousands of times more sensitive than normal, the pain you feel is thousands of times worse than normal..."
Nux understood, his golden eyes shined with a cruel, ruthless, predatory look on his face.
"You should have hidden it."
He grinned, relishing how one mistake was going to cost Zylarith the battle, but—
"You took this long to ’discover’ something so obvious.
Don’t look proud of yourself, that is embarrassing."
Zylarith looked disgusted.
Nux didn’t care, he just laughed as Death, Space and Time gathered around him.
"What you think doesn’t matter.
All that matters is...
I now know where to hit."
Saying those words, Nux disappeared and appeared behind Zylarith again, punching his back with a fist covered with Death Energy.

Zylarith’s Soul scattered again, Nux used Space to seal the area, the scattered fragments stopped for a moment, time wrapped around them, slowing their escape. Nux used that time to plunge the fragments into Death Energy—
For the first time, Nux had built an attack that could actually hurt Zylarith enough for him to be on all fours.
But Zylarith was still Zylarith—
His eyes flashed.
Chaos struck the three Laws at once.
Space forgot what it was supposed to seal, Time forgot what it was supposed to slow, Death forgot what it was supposed to end.
And just like that—
Zylarith reformed his body with next to no damage.
"You didn’t think that would work because it did before, did you?
That little victory of yours only happened because I allowed it to happen."
He spoke arrogantly.
Then, he waved his hand again and Chaos around Nux came at him from every side in the form of blades, hands, mouths, storms, even Laws that Nux couldn’t name—
All of these tore into Nux, the Light Energy around him shattered, Darkness scattered, Space collapsed, Time cracked, Death was pushed back—
"THIS IS NOT OVER!!"
Nux screamed in pain, Life Energy burst out to heal him, but Zylarith just shrugged.
"You just don’t get it, do you?"

This time, he didn’t even explain it. The Life Energy inside Nux’s body twisted, the wounds it touched opened wider, the broken bones it tried to mend split apart again, the torn flesh it tried to close was torn apart even further.
Nux clenched his fists in agony, the sheer thing holding him down was his will to not scream.
The more Life Energy he used, the more it tormented him, in the end, he had no choice but to stop using it and let his body bleed openly.
That was when Zylarith appeared right in front of his broken body, his smoky hand reached toward Nux’s face and—
"You are powerful."
He spoke in a low, amused voice.
"You are durable."
His fingers touched Nux’s forehead.
"You are... strange."
A burst of Chaos exploded point-blank.
BOOOOOOM
Nux’s body was thrown down and collided with a nearby asteroid, shattering it in an instant.
Zylarith floated above him and—
"But you fight like a child who has found many sharp tools and believes holding more of them makes him a master."
Nux tried to regain control over his body but—
Slap
Zylarith formed a simple hand with Energy of Chaos and—
He slapped him in the most humiliating way.
And Nux...
He could only take it.
Slap
Slap
Slap
Slap
A series of slaps echoed throughout the dimension, it didn’t hurt Nux, they were not meant to, they were only meant to... humiliate him.
To show him his place.
To make him understand how foolish of a move challenging an Infinity, that too, the strongest Infinity, was.
"And now, because of your mistake—
This is what’s going to happen."
Zylarith began after he grabbed Nux’s head and forced him to look at him.
"I will not kill you."
He shook his head.
"I will use you to get to your Universe, I will capture your wives who you swore to protect, who you claim to love, who claim to love you—
And I will do to their bodies what I did to yours."
Nux’s expression changed.
For the first time since the battle began, his eyes reflected... fear.
And that made Zylarith smile.
"Your Universe strengthens your body, correct?
Let’s see how long they would last."
He grinned.
"And don’t worry, I will not kill them.
In fact, I plan to let them live a good life if they so desire it.

The only thing they would need to do for the pain to stop tormenting them would be to kneel in front of me, place their heads right beneath my feet, allowing me to step on them, step on their pride, then lick my feet with earnest looks on their faces."
Zylarith’s grin became demonic.
"I would like to see what their faces look like when they do that."
Nux’s body trembled in rage he had never experienced before.
BOOOOOOOOOOM
In a single instant, ALL of his Laws were activated—
Space.
Time.
Light.
Darkness.
Life.
Death.
Creation.
Destruction.
Balance.
Chaos.
—combining with each other for a final, life-threatening explosion.
But—
With one wave of Zylarith’s hand—
All the Laws cracked, twisted and bent under Chaos.
Zylarith closed his fist and the Energies disappeared, only the Chaos remained and that Chaos—
It was no longer Nux’s.
It was Zylarith’s.
It moved right inside Nux’s body and began to tear through his body.
"KKhawwwrrkkkk!!!"
Nux coughed out blood again, but Zylarith didn’t even let him do that, he tightened his hold on his face, then, he moved closer.
"Get this into your head, Nux Leander.
You may have all the Primordial Laws, but that doesn’t make you the strongest.
You, of all people, can never defeat me, even if I am at my weakest."
He spoke, his voice becoming more and more terrifying.
"You cannot out-understand me.
You cannot out-control me.
And if you ever try to use Chaos against me again—
I will make you scream with your own power.
Just like I will do right now."

He spoke, as a large amount of Chaos Energy moved towards Nux, ready to tear him into pieces, to make him scream in agony he had never experienced before in his life, to... break him apart, piece by piece.
But then—
Just as Zylarith was sure of his victory—
It happened.
